544138|2026-09.headline: JG Chemicals posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of INR361.01 crore (+64% YoY) and PAT of INR27.95 crore (+86% YoY), with EBITDA margin at 10.71%.
544138|2026-09.overview: Management reported its best-ever quarter, with revenue, EBITDA and PAT all at new quarterly highs, driven by tire and rubber demand and a favourable product mix. H1 FY27 revenue rose 54% to INR676.66 crore and PAT rose 72% to INR54.07 crore. Sequentially, EBITDA margin eased from 11.50% in Q1 to 10.71% in Q2, which management attributed to raw material cost lags. Capacity additions at Dahej (trial runs next month) and Naidupeta (now mid-January 2027 commissioning) remain the main growth levers.

segments.name: Zinc oxide (tire and rubber)
segments.commentary: Principal market; management says it is the largest zinc oxide supplier to the tire industry. Q2 volume growth was in the mid-teens, and the company says it has surplus capacity for the next 6 to 9 months.

segments.name: Non-rubber applications
segments.commentary: Over 18% of sales in H1 FY27, up from close to 10% in FY24, spanning ceramics, specialty chemicals, agriculture and pharma. Target is about 30% in the next 2 to 3 years.

segments.name: Zinc sulphate
segments.commentary: Installed capacity of 10,000 MTPA at Naidupeta, utilisation about 50%; contributes under 3% of revenue, expected at 5% to 7% share over time.

guidance_outlook: Dahej Phase 1 (about 15,000 MTPA zinc oxide): trial runs next month (December 2026), followed by customer qualification and ramp-up.
Naidupeta brownfield (about 5,000 MTPA): slipped from Q3 to mid-to-end January 2027 commissioning; earlier management said Q4 FY27.
Total zinc oxide capacity to rise to about 79,900 TPA after both projects; management says this covers demand through FY28 and FY29. Dahej Phase 2 expected to start around mid-to-late 2028.
Dahej utilisation targeted at about 60% to 70% in FY28.
Consolidated EBITDA margin targeted at 14% to 15% in about 3 years; management says the current level is sustainable.
Internal target to double revenue every 3 years; management expects FY27 revenue well above INR1,200 crore.
Dahej revenue potential of about INR900 crore now expected around FY29 to FY30, with peak potential said to be higher.
Net cash expected above INR100 crore at FY27 end; no borrowing expected even if H1 revenue doubles.
capex_capacity: Dahej greenfield (Gujarat): Phase 1 about 15,000 MTPA of a planned 40,000-plus MTPA facility; trial runs next month.
Naidupeta brownfield: about 5,000 MTPA addition; commissioning mid-January 2027.
Post both projects, installed capacity to be over 115,000 tons of zinc chemicals, per management.
Acquired about 16.74 acres of freehold land at Naidupeta (Tirupati District, Andhra Pradesh) through BDJ Oxides Private Limited for future expansion.
Zinc sulphate: 10,000 MTPA installed; some new zinc sulphate products expected in FY28, with details to be shared in early 2027.
Naidupeta solar Phase 1 operational, meeting about 25% to 30% of energy needs; payback about 4 years. Further capacity under evaluation after new government regulations from 1 January.
JG TUR (Tire Upscaled Rubber, recycled rubber): pilot trials successful with key customers; full-scale venture being planned, with capex and timeline to be shared later.
demand_pricing: Q2 volume growth in the mid-teens; management expects Q3 numbers to exceed the current run rate, and October was the highest production month to date.

Indian auto volumes in Q2: passenger vehicles about 30% YoY, two-wheelers about 15%, commercial vehicles about 29%, three-wheelers about 23%. Indian tire majors have about INR25,000 crore of announced capex.
Raw material: over 100 global suppliers. Margin dip QoQ attributed to lag between LME-linked purchase cost and selling price, plus longer lead times from West Asia disruption.
Management says the West Asia cost increase was passed on to customers in Q1 and has already been absorbed.

Industry consolidation: management says customers are shifting volumes from small zinc oxide producers (70% to 80% of India's producers) to larger players, and expects some business reallocated to JG over 5 to 7 years.
Pricing: management says it is agnostic to zinc price, since selling price follows the prior month's LME average. Per-ton price may fall if zinc falls, but volume growth is the focus.
Battery-grade zinc oxide: JG is the only Indian producer benchmarked and approved under an international zinc battery initiative; volumes expected in 2 to 3 years, high-margin, low volume.

qa_highlights.question: What was the volume growth in Q2, and why did gross margin fall about 130 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth was in the mid-teens. Management said gross margin moves with inventory lead and lag, and it focuses on EBITDA and per-ton margin instead. It sees a blended EBITDA margin of 14% to 15% within about 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative in H1 FY27, and will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital is 90 to 100 days. Management said March inventory was low due to shipping delays from the West Asia crisis, and that cash should be significantly higher at 31 March. Debtor days are in line with history.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall QoQ, and was the procurement discount on dross and ash changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed a time lag: lower-cost material bought at lower LME prices arrived late, while higher-cost domestic material hit plants first. Management expects this to average out by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej timeline, Phase 2 start, and the sustainability of non-rubber growth and margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 is expected around mid-to-late 2028. Specialty grades for pharma, cosmetics and specialty chemicals are expected to lift margins more than ceramics. Blended EBITDA is expected to move toward 14%.

qa_highlights.question: Is demand sustainable into Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tire demand is strong, with OEM and replacement demand both firm. It expects no demand aberration given 7% to 8% economic growth, and says Dahej should help with ceramics, which has a low base.

qa_highlights.question: Dahej utilisation, tire versus non-tire mix, and ceramics target?
qa_highlights.answer: Dahej utilisation is targeted at about 60% to 70% in FY28. Management aims for 10% to 15% of the ceramics market, against over 30% share in India overall, and notes two large tire plants about 5 km from Dahej.

risks_watch: Naidupeta commissioning has slipped from Q3 to mid-January 2027; Dahej trial runs and customer qualification timing must hold.
Working capital is heavy (inventory rose from INR92 crore in March to INR154 crore in September; receivables from INR177 crore to INR207 crore), and H1 operating cash flow was negative.
Quarterly EBITDA margin volatility from LME pricing lags and West Asia-related lead times.
Ceramics demand was hit by West Asia gas issues, and the ramp-up depends on the Dahej market.
Recycled rubber (JG TUR) and battery-grade zinc oxide still at pilot or qualification stage with no quantified revenue.
Zinc sulphate utilisation about 50%, with ramp-up dependent on new specialised grades.
544138|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, capacity and margins, with management repeatedly calling Q2 a record. It was more defensive on the sequential margin dip and negative operating cash flow, attributing both to timing and inventory lags. Specific timelines (Naidupeta, Dahej Phase 2, FY28 zinc sulphate launches) were given loosely or deferred.
key_quotes: JG delivered its best ever quarterly performance in the current Q2 FY27, surpassing the previous record achieved in the Q1.
JGC is India's largest zinc recycling company and a leading manufacturer of zinc oxide, a value-added green chemical, today manufactured using recycled zinc.
So if you see quarter-on-quarter, you will see a slight dip in the EBITDA margins.
I think at the end of the year, it averages out.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Blended EBITDA margin eased to 10.71% in Q2 from 11.50% in Q1 on LME lag, with management targeting 14% to 15% only in about 3 years; expansion depends on specialty non-rubber mix (over 18% of H1 sales, target ~30%) and lag normalising by year-end.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dahej Phase 1 (15,000 MTPA) trial runs in December 2026 and Naidupeta (5,000 MTPA) slipped from Q3 to mid-to-end January 2027, taking zinc oxide capacity to about 79,900 TPA, though the Naidupeta slip tempers confidence.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 volume grew mid-teens, management expects Q3 above the current run rate, October was the highest production month, and zinc oxide utilisation is above 80%, with Indian tire-segment auto volumes strong (PV ~30% YoY).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Zinc oxide utilisation above 80% and the company says capacity covers demand only through FY28-FY29, so further capex is likely; JG TUR full-scale venture capex and zinc sulphate product details are due in early 2027, and 16.74 acres of Naidupeta land is already acquired.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue well above INR1,200 crore versus H1 of INR676.66 crore (+54% YoY), which implies a strong H2, but no formal revision has been made and the Naidupeta slip limits upside.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Naidupeta has already slipped from Q3 to mid-January 2027, and Dahej trials and customer qualification must hold; working capital is heavy (negative H1 operating cash flow, inventory INR154 crore, receivables INR207 crore), and LME lags pressured Q2 margin.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Some new zinc sulphate products are expected in FY28 with details due in early 2027, and battery-grade zinc oxide volumes are 2 to 3 years away, but both are at pilot or qualification stage with no quantified revenue.

rows.label: Dahej ceramics and non-tire ramp-up
rows.why: Non-rubber share rose from ~10% in FY24 to over 18% in H1 FY27 with a ~30% target in 2-3 years, and Dahej is expected to help ceramics where JG targets 10% to 15% of the market; Dahej utilisation is targeted at 60% to 70% in FY28.

rows.label: Industry consolidation share gains
rows.why: Management says customers are shifting volume from the 70% to 80% of India's small zinc oxide producers toward larger players, with some business expected to be reallocated to JG over 5 to 7 years.

rows.label: Net cash above INR100 crore by FY27 end
rows.why: Net cash surplus was INR63.3 crore at 30 Sep 2026 and management expects over INR100 crore at FY27 end with no borrowing, though H1 operating cash flow was negative and working capital is 90 to 100 days.

tone.note: Management was confident on tire demand, Dahej and Naidupeta capacity and the long-term 14% to 15% margin, but defensive on the QoQ margin dip, negative H1 operating cash flow and the Naidupeta slip; analysts pressed on gross margin, cash flow and Dahej timing.

544140|2026-03.headline: Gopal Snacks Q4 FY26 revenue rose 29% YoY to Rs 409.6 cr; FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% with Rajkot plant fully commissioned.
544140|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was Rs 409.6 crore, up 29% YoY and 2.2% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 31.5 crore (7.7% margin) and PAT of Rs 29.9 crore (7.3% margin). For FY26, revenue grew 2.7% to Rs 1,508.2 crore, EBITDA was Rs 101.3 crore (6.7%) and PAT Rs 73.7 crore (4.9%). Management said supply was restored after the fire-related disruption, with Rajkot commissioned (installed capacity 1,05,000 MT) and the Modasa plant fully integrated. Insurance receipts reached about Rs 37.4 crore in FY26, with a further claim expected to be settled around Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 17.5 crore in Q4; about Rs 37.4 crore in FY26

segments.name: Gathiya
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 410 crore; FY27 growth target 18-20%. Management estimates Gujarat Gathiya industry growth at 15-20%.

segments.name: Namkeen
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 350 crore; FY27 growth target 15%. Gujarat Namkeen industry growth estimated at 14-15%.

segments.name: Fryums / Pellets
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 250 crore; FY27 growth target 15%, in line with industry.

segments.name: Wafers
segments.commentary: Base of about Rs 155 crore; FY27 growth target 40%.

segments.name: Others (papad, besan, spices, bakery, noodles, rusk)
segments.commentary: FY27 growth target of 30%. New products (kaju biscuit, popcorn) grew from Rs 25 crore to Rs 63 crore in FY26, with about Rs 50 crore of the Rs 38 crore delta from core states (as stated).

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% on an annualised average basis; exit run-rate expected near double digit.

FY27 incremental revenue target of Rs 330-350 crore: Rs 170-180 crore from core market (Gujarat), Rs 125-130 crore from focus states, Rs 35 crore from other states, quick commerce, railways and modern trade.
Advertisement spend projected at 2.2-2.3% of revenue in FY27 versus about 1.7% in FY26; trade spend cuts to be gradual, not major in FY27.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 40-45 crore, including a corporate office building at Rajkot; the rest is maintenance.
Finance cost expected to be slightly higher in FY27, about Rs 10 crore versus about Rs 7 crore in FY26.
Insurance balance claim expected to be Rs 35-40 crore (higher than the Rs 10 crore gap, as restatement cost exceeds WDV write-off), with receipt expected around Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Rajkot plant commissioned; installed capacity 1,05,000 MT. Gondal facility to be discontinued.
Plant roles: Rajkot makes gathiya, namkeen, snack pellets and extruded snacks; Modasa makes all namkeen and wafers; Nagpur makes gathiya, namkeen, pellets and wafers.
Third-party manufacturing used in Kashipur (UP; four SKUs making 76-77% of UP sales) and Chhattisgarh (wafers only) to cut transport costs in those markets.
FY27 capacity utilisation expected at about 43-45%, per management in response to a question; Q4 utilisation near the full-year level shown on slide 11.
demand_pricing: Core market (Gujarat) run-rate about Rs 85-90 crore per month; about 300 distributors; line-wide coverage at 29% of beats on twice-a-week service by end-Q4, targeting 40% by end-Q1 FY27.
Focus states run-rate about Rs 400 crore annualised across 600 distributors; 65-70 dealers added in Q4 and 69 new distributors in Q4 against an annual target of 250.
Per-day run-rate has improved since March; Uttar Pradesh H2 was 26% above H1; monthly UP sales about Rs 6.5 crore with 72% from two SKUs, target exit Rs 8.5-9 crore.
Grammage cut of about 4% taken in mid-April 2026 on small packs, with price hikes on larger SKUs; further action depends on competitor response.
Raw material basket: palm oil 26-27%, chana 21-22%, laminate 18-19%, potato about 6%. RM inflation impact about 4-4.5% so far, largely offset by grammage cuts, price increases and BOM changes.
Chana stock sufficient to about November 2026; H2 purchases to be made from market or imports if cheaper.
Distributor count 953 at end-Q4 versus 884 at end-Q3; 97% of business through direct distributors; DMS live at 90% of dealers.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 top line shape up now that supply is restored?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets Rs 330-350 crore revenue delta in FY27: Rs 170-180 crore core Gujarat, Rs 125-130 crore focus states, Rs 35 crore other channels.

qa_highlights.question: Why did focus states grow more slowly than core states in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Core states were hit harder by the fire, depleting the base. Q4 beat Q3 this year, reversing the usual 6-7% seasonal dip, and focus-state growth is expected to rebuild on distributor additions. Growth is expected at par near term and higher on an annualised basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is EBITDA margin guidance of 8-9% conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management held the 8-9% average guidance, citing raw material volatility. Exit run-rate is expected near double digit. Trade spend will be cut only gradually, with no major cut in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How much more insurance will be received?
qa_highlights.answer: Balance claim expected at Rs 35-40 crore, higher than the Rs 10 crore gap, with receipt expected around Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital and debt rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher chana inventory bought ahead of expected price rises raised bank borrowing. Receivable days rose by 9 days, but the working capital cycle is within the comfort zone.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company cut prices or pack sizes?
qa_highlights.answer: A 4% grammage cut was taken in mid-April 2026. Further action depends on how the industry responds.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation in palm oil and packaging (cited as 15-20% basket increase); H2 FY27 chana purchases exposed to pulse prices, with El Nino raising rain-deficit risk to rural demand.
Unorganised Rs 5 price-point players under pressure; no action seen yet. Industry pricing discipline may change.
Insurance balance claim timing (Q2 FY27 expected) and asset restatement progress.
Focus-state growth recovery and distributor additions versus the target of 250 for CY26.
Rising debt and finance cost (about Rs 10 crore expected in FY27) on higher inventory.
Trade spend and advertising step-up (2.2-2.3% of revenue) could compress margins if market-share recovery needs more spend.
544140|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and specific on recovery metrics, distributor adds and capacity; more cautious and hedged on margin drivers and raw material inflation, with the 8-9% margin guidance held despite analyst pressure to raise it. Some answers were vague on pricing and on how industry players will react.
key_quotes: Rigan Raithatha: Yes, next year for the margin front as we have been guiding, we still speak to the same guidance that is 8% to 9%.
Rigan Raithatha: So, as far as trade spend is concerned, we would be obviously looking on that front but that our reduction on the trade spend would be in a very gradual phase wise manner.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.when: FY27, exit run-rate near double digit
rows.why: EBITDA margin guided at 8-9% for FY27 versus 6.7% in FY26 and 7.7% in Q4 FY26, with exit run-rate near double digit; offset risks are ad spend rising to 2.2-2.3% of revenue from about 1.7% and 4-4.5% raw material inflation so far.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Rajkot already commissioned (installed 1,05,000 MT) and utilisation is only about 43-45% for FY27, so no new capacity is needed in the window; Gondal is being discontinued, not expanded.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets Rs 330-350 crore incremental revenue (about 22-23% on Rs 1,508 crore), with Gujarat run-rate Rs 85-90 crore per month, 953 distributors (up from 884), and 69 new focus-state distributors in Q4; no firm order book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at about 43% (FY26 level, FY27 guided 43-45%) is far below the 80% threshold, and FY27 capex is held at Rs 40-45 crore, mostly maintenance plus a Rajkot corporate office.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held the 8-9% margin guidance despite analyst pressure to raise it, citing raw material volatility, and its revenue target is described as aspirational.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Palm oil (26-27% of basket), packaging and chana (21-22%) inflation, plus rising ad and trade spend, could compress the 8-9% margin if pricing does not hold; El Nino raises rural demand risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Others segment (papad, besan, spices, bakery, noodles, rusk) targets 30% growth, and kaju biscuit and popcorn grew from Rs 25 crore to Rs 63 crore in FY26, but no specific new launch dates were given.

rows.label: Insurance balance claim Rs 35-40 crore
rows.why: Management expects a balance claim of Rs 35-40 crore, above the Rs 10 crore gap, which would add a one-off cash inflow once received.

rows.label: Chana inventory and debt build
rows.why: Chana stock covers only to about November 2026 and bank borrowing rose on pre-bought inventory, with finance cost guided to about Rs 10 crore in FY27 from about Rs 7 crore in FY26.

rows.label: Focus-state and UP expansion
rows.why: Focus states run at about Rs 400 crore annualised across 600 distributors, UP H2 was 26% above H1, and the focus-state target is Rs 125-130 crore incremental in FY27.

tone.note: Management was confident on distributor adds, supply recovery and the Rajkot capacity, but cautious on margin drivers and raw material inflation, holding 8-9% EBITDA guidance despite analyst pressure to raise it; analysts pushed on focus-state growth, pricing discipline and the margin outlook.

544140|2026-06.headline: Gopal Snacks Q1 FY27 revenue hit record INR 422.3 cr (+31.1% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 7.4%; FY27 EBITDA guided at 8-9%.
544140|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly revenue from operations of INR 422.3 crore, up 31.1% YoY and 3.1% QoQ, with the fifth consecutive quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA more than doubled YoY to INR 31.5 crore (7.4% margin vs 4.7%), and PAT was INR 12.8 crore. Rajkot main facility restarted after the Gondal consolidation, though April saw about 5-6 working days of disruption (gas shortage and plant shift) that cost INR 12-13 crore of revenue in core markets. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ growth (INR 1,800-1,900 crore revenue) and 8-9% EBITDA margin with exit near double digits.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 5.3 crore in Q1 FY26
No exceptional items in Q1; prior quarter had insurance gain, so QoQ not comparable
May and June at this level

segments.name: Core market (Gujarat)
segments.commentary: Flat sequentially in Q1 due to April disruption that cost INR 12-13 crore; management targets INR 100-plus crore per month from here. Gathiya is the leading product, followed by namkeen, snack pellets and potato wafers; wafers grew 15% YoY in core markets. About 65% of Gujarat Gathiya market is still unorganised.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 41% YoY; 100% of UP top line comes from two SKUs, Champakali Gathiya and Papdi Gathiya.

segments.name: Focus and other states
segments.commentary: Focus-state distributors rose from 440 (Q1 FY26) to 530 (Q4 FY26) to 567 (Q1 FY27); other states rose from 110 to 129. Maharashtra distributors went 194 to 205 to 198, with focus on Marathwada and the Nagpur belt.

segments.name: Other snack products
segments.commentary: Revenue in the other snacks bucket went from about INR 10 crore last year to about INR 23-24 crore per quarter, including Shot Go noodles, rusks, wafer biscuits, wafer rolls, jeera biscuits and washing bar.

segments.name: Alternate channels
segments.commentary: E-commerce was INR 2.79 crore in Q1 FY27 vs INR 2 crore in Q4 FY26. Modern trade was flat at INR 1.85 crore.

segments.name: Nagpur plant
segments.commentary: Capacity utilisation is below 30%; 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, of which about 60 have moved to Modasa for logistics reasons. Third-party units at Kashipur (about INR 2 crore per month) and Manendragarh support other regions.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guided at INR 1,800-1,900 crore (20%+ growth), reaffirmed; management says it has held the stance on 20%+ growth.
FY27 EBITDA margin 8-9% for the full year, with exit run rate near double digits.
FY28 EBITDA margin guided at 10-11% with exit near 11%; sustainable target 11-11.5%; average reaching that level around mid-FY28-29.
FY28 PAT margin around 7-7.5%; minimum 20% revenue CAGR over the medium term.
Insurance claim of about INR 30-40 crore on the fire loss expected in Q2 FY27; management says documents are submitted.
Seven NPIs planned across Q2 and Q3, five of them non-palm-oil with better margins; 6 lakh outlets targeted by end of CY2026 (from 5.25-5.5 lakh).
capex_capacity: Rajkot main facility restarted; production consolidated from Gondal to Rajkot, with expected savings in power, fuel, logistics and operating costs as utilisation improves.
Modasa and Nagpur plants contribute to the network; Nagpur utilisation is below 30%.
Double-service coverage now reaches 38% of outlets; run rate up 14-25% where it has been rolled out. Pilot of ARS (auto replenishment) started; DMS covers most of the distributor network.
Retail touchpoints on DMS at 4.24 lakh; another 60-70k outlets are served but not on DMS.
demand_pricing: Raw material inflation was 5% in Q1; 4.2% passed on through price hikes and grammage cuts, 0.8% absorbed in P&L. Another 0.2-0.3% hit is pending and will be passed through.
Q2 inflation is slightly lower than 100 bps additional, per management.
Management says the company now runs at par or lower grammage than competitors and relies on distribution automation rather than grammage to drive volume.
Management expects roughly 75-80% of growth from volume and about 20% from price in the rest of FY27.
Chana stored till Q3-end; potato stored; palm oil and laminate are bought from the market with no major near-term increase foreseen.
INR 5 price point remains about 60% of sales (down from ~80% in FY22); management says no visible industry shift.
Regional brands in core states (Balaji, Gokul, Shri Hari) remain present; Miraj and Star brands shut, and Miraj has restarted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 330-350 crore FY27 incremental revenue guidance still intact, and what is the festive run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the run rate is INR 150 crore+ per month, April was lower due to the Gondal to Rajkot shift, and 20%+ growth guidance stands.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin and when will it ramp up?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable target is 11-11.5%. FY27 exit near double digits, FY28 exit near 11%, and an average of that level around mid-FY28-29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the core market run rate target and how is the Gujarat business growing?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of INR 100-plus crore per month in core markets. Double service is being scaled up, and more products are planned to lift margins.

qa_highlights.question: What are the A&P and trade spend trends?
qa_highlights.answer: A&P was about 1% of sales in Q1 against a 2.2% annualised budget; trade discount is 2.5% of sales versus about 3.5% earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Nagpur utilisation below 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: 159 distributors were mapped to Nagpur, about 60 were moved to Modasa for logistics, and the 250-distributor-a-year addition is below plan for the 300-400 km catchment.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is an FMCG business with no order book, and daily run rate is steady with no month-end billing.

risks_watch: April disruption (gas shortage at Gondal plus Gondal-to-Rajkot shift) cost INR 12-13 crore of core-market revenue; watch whether May-June run rate of INR 150 crore+ per month holds and core Gujarat reaches the INR 100-plus crore per month target.

Raw material inflation: 0.8% of 5% Q1 inflation absorbed in P&L, another 0.2-0.3% pending pass-through, and management said Q2 inflation could be slightly below 100 bps additional; margin delivery depends on further price hikes and grammage cuts.
Insurance claim of about INR 30-40 crore on the fire loss is expected in Q2 FY27 from a PSU insurer; timing has slipped before and any delay affects reported profit.
Nagpur plant utilisation below 30% for over two to three years, with about 60 of 159 mapped distributors moved to Modasa; distributor additions below plan for the 300-400 km catchment.

Execution of FY27 guidance (INR 1,800-1,900 crore revenue, 8-9% EBITDA) and FY28 ramp to 10-11% depends on Rajkot savings, double-service coverage (38% of outlets) and seven NPIs in Q2-Q3, five non-palm-oil.

Competitive intensity: management says it now runs at par or lower grammage than peers, and A&P is about 1% of sales versus a 2.2% annualised budget, so any step-up in spend ahead of festive season could move margins.
key_quotes: So we strongly stand by our earlier guidance given of, you know, minimum 20% growth in this financial year over last year.
As of now, we are either at par or we are giving lesser grammage versus competition, but still we are able to maintain our revenue momentum because distribution automation is helping us a lot
So from May onwards, there is 0% disturbance in terms of operations.
So, we are FMCG company, Adarsh-Bhai, and typically we are not B2B company.
544140|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the top line and the 20%+ growth and 8-9% EBITDA guidance, which management reaffirmed several times. More cautious and less specific on the April disruption, Nagpur utilisation, Maharashtra distributor count and the insurance claim timing, where answers were partial and follow-ups were promised.

544140|2026-09.headline: Gopal Snacks Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22.9% YoY to INR 461.5 crore and EBITDA margin reached 9.0%, with FY27 guidance of INR 1,800-1,900 crore and 8.9% EBITDA margin maintained.
544140|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 22.9% YoY to INR 461.5 crore (up 9.3% QoQ), and H1 revenue rose 26.7% to INR 883.9 crore. EBITDA rose 72% YoY to INR 41.6 crore, with margin at 9.0% versus 6.4% a year earlier and 7.4% in Q1. Reported PAT of INR 45.9 crore includes a net exceptional gain of INR 35.3 crore, so underlying profit before exceptional items was INR 25.9 crore. Management said Gujarat run-rate is below its INR 100 crore/month aspiration, and that the full INR 36.4 crore fire insurance claim was received in October 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +72% YoY, +32% QoQ; margin vs 6.4% in Q2 FY26 and 7.4% in Q1 FY27
Includes net exceptional gain of INR 35.3 crore
vs INR 28.2 crore in H1 FY26; includes INR 35.3 crore net exceptional gain (INR 21.8 crore in H1 FY26)

segments.name: Namkeen
segments.commentary: H1 value growth 18.3% but volume growth only 8.6%; Q2 volume up 8% QoQ and 15% YoY. Grammage cuts are being taken SKU by SKU because the company is not market leader in several namkeen products.

segments.name: Gathiya
segments.commentary: Q2 sales up 25.6% YoY. Management said the company is taking share, as the category typically grows 15-18%.

segments.name: Wafers
segments.commentary: Q2 sales up 40% YoY; wafers grew 59% in focus states. Management plans about 30 wafer distributors added within 50-70 days, with Cristos positioned as upmarket and Gopal Wafers receiving trade margins.

segments.name: Snack Pellets and extruded snacks
segments.commentary: Q2 sales up 23% YoY; snack pellets grew 43% in focus states.

segments.name: Focus states
segments.commentary: Focus-state revenue about INR 132 crore in the quarter, growing about 35%. Maharashtra run-rate about INR 66 crore per quarter (INR 22 crore per month) and UP about INR 19 crore in the current quarter.

segments.name: Gujarat
segments.commentary: Core state revenue flat QoQ and below the INR 100 crore/month aspiration. Distributor count held near 311-312 for several quarters by design to protect distributor economics.

segments.name: Non-palm-oil products (bakery, cupcakes, suji, rusk, noodles)
segments.commentary: Contributed 3.25% of current top line; target 4.5% by FY27 end and 6.5% next year.

segments.name: New channels (railways, modern trade, quick commerce, exports)
segments.commentary: H1 railways INR 3.77 crore (vs INR 2.34 crore), modern trade INR 3.63 crore (vs INR 2.1 crore), quick commerce INR 7.07 crore (vs INR 3.48 crore). Exports near INR 1 crore in October vs INR 50-60 lakh average before. FY27 target INR 30-35 crore; FY28 target INR 75-90 crore.

segments.name: Joint ventures
segments.commentary: Manendragarh JV at INR 3.5-4 crore per month and at capacity; Kashipur about INR 1.25 crore per month; Hiriyur about INR 85 lakh per month.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance maintained at INR 1,800-1,900 crore, with EBITDA margin of 8.9%; H1 already in that range and H2 expected similar.
Management aspires to double-digit EBITDA margin, contingent on easing raw material inflation ('once the war scenario eases out').
Growth of at least 20% a year is targeted; about 6-7% of growth expected from network expansion and the rest from organic growth and new products.
Current momentum is 22-23% growth, per management.
Dual-servicing outlets to reach 65-70% by FY27 end (42% at September end, 43.5% at October end).
Distributor additions of about 220 expected in calendar 2026, against an earlier 250 target ('not exactly on track').
A&P spend expected at around 1% of revenue for the full year, similar to H1.
H2 operating cash flow expected to be better than H1, aided by insurance proceeds and inventory reduction from about INR 200 crore to INR 100-120 crore.
Besan unit at Nagpur (commenced September) expected to save about INR 3 crore a year in transport costs.
Laminate key-line-dimension changes worth about INR 6.7 crore annualised; benefit expected mainly next year due to two-month laminate stock.
capex_capacity: Besan manufacturing unit commissioned in September 2026 at Nagpur, reducing transport from Rajkot.
Company-level capacity utilisation about 37-38%; management said grammage cuts also depressed utilisation.
Operating leverage contributed about 1% of margin benefit in H1 FY27.
Manendragarh JV has run out of capacity; Kashipur and Hiriyur JVs are below that level.
Chana storage up to about 50% higher than last year, with chana stock expected to last until mid-January and potato until mid-December.
demand_pricing: Cumulative inflation impact to H1 is about 5.5% versus FY26 average: about 4% passed through grammage, 0.6% through price, and 0.7-0.8% through trade discount and mix.
Sequential Q1 to Q2 inflation impact on gross margin was 2.3%: 1.1% from grammage, 0.4% from price, and 0.4% from trade discount and mix.
Raw material basket: palm oil about 27%, laminate/packaging about 22-23%, chana about 19%.
INR 10-plus price point contribution rose to about 21%; management expects about 3.5% of that category next quarter.
Management said the company will not chase volume at the cost of margins, and rivals are expected to need price hikes or grammage cuts.
Two local brands (Star, Kolhapur; Miraj, Nathdwara) shut down last quarter; no closures noted in Q2 so far.
Gokul, a brand run by a promoter relative's splinter group, is now treated as a regular competitor.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company satisfied with core-state (Gujarat) growth against the INR 100 crore/month run-rate aspiration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not satisfied with the Gujarat run-rate and is aiming at INR 100 crore per month without cutting margins; pricing and grammage are being managed carefully.

qa_highlights.question: How much of gross margin is from pricing versus mix and grammage?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross margin gain came from a mix of grammage correction, price correction, and about 0.4% from lower trade discount and mix.

qa_highlights.question: What is the volume outlook in namkeen after price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 namkeen value grew 18.3% against 8.6% volume growth. Grammage cuts are taken SKU by SKU, and two new namkeen products are planned for next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What progress has been made on dual servicing of outlets?
qa_highlights.answer: Dual servicing reached 42% at September end and 43.5% at October end in Gujarat. The target is 65-70% by FY27 end, and 25-30 Western snacks ready-stock distributors will be added in Gujarat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company growing 20% a year after FY27 and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will be at least 20% a year. H1 network additions of about 130 distributors contributed INR 13 crore, rising to about INR 60 crore in the full year and about INR 80 crore next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins reach double digits by year-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8-9% guidance stands and double digit is an aspiration that depends on raw material inflation easing.

qa_highlights.question: What are the H2 CFO drivers, and why was H1 CFO weaker?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 CFO should be better because of the INR 36.4-36.5 crore insurance receipt and inventory falling from about INR 200 crore to INR 100-120 crore. H1 was weaker because of higher inventory, including about 50% more chana storage and laminate stock.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company handle competitors burning cash in Gujarat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said competitors cannot sustain losses for long and will need to take price or grammage decisions; distributor count was held flat deliberately to protect per-distributor revenue.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation: palm oil (about 27% of basket), laminate/packaging (about 22-23%) and chana (about 19%); management ties margin recovery to easing of the 'war scenario', so the 8-9% EBITDA guidance and the double-digit aspiration depend on input costs.
Gujarat core-state run-rate remains below the INR 100 crore/month aspiration; distributor count held near 311-312 by design, and competitors' cash burn is a stated concern.
Namkeen volume growth (8.6% in H1) lags value growth (18.3%) as grammage cuts are taken SKU by SKU; watch whether two planned new namkeen products arrive next quarter.
Network expansion is behind plan: about 220 distributor additions expected in calendar 2026 versus an earlier 250 target ('not exactly on track'); Nagpur/Maharashtra additions slower than expected.

Cash flow: H1 CFO weaker than usual due to higher inventory (laminate, chana storage up about 50%); H2 relies on insurance receipt of INR 36.4 crore and inventory falling from about INR 200 crore to INR 100-120 crore.
Drought and possible chana and potato price increases in the next financial year; management said pass-through will rely on mix, lower trade marketing and price/grammage moves.
Non-core channels (exports, railways, modern trade, quick commerce) targeted at INR 30-35 crore in FY27 and INR 75-90 crore in FY28; watch execution, with exports only about INR 1 crore in October.
key_quotes: So definitely we are not satisfied with this run rate in Gujarat.
So once the war scenario eases out, definitely we'll reach to double-digit margins.
So we have almost got 1% of the benefit as far as operating leverage is concerned, and that will continue to give us the benefit go ing forward also
Not exactly on track, but we are confident that in the full calendar year we will be able to add roughly 220 distributors.
544140|2026-09.management_tone: Management was confident on volume momentum (22-23% current growth, Gathiya and wafers ahead of category) and on operating leverage, but cautious on margins, saying double-digit EBITDA depends on easing raw material inflation. It was candid on shortfalls: Gujarat run-rate below aspiration, distributor additions not exactly on track, and H1 cash flow weaker.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 9.0% in Q2 from 7.4% in Q1 and 6.4% a year ago, but guidance is held at 8.9% and double-digit margin depends on easing raw material inflation (palm oil ~27%, laminate ~22-23%, chana ~19% of basket).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Company-level utilisation is only 37-38% and no new plant is being added; the Besan unit at Nagpur was commissioned in September 2026 and Manendragarh JV is at capacity but no expansion is announced.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Current momentum is 22-23% growth, Gathiya sales rose 25.6% YoY and wafers 40% YoY, and H1 namkeen volume grew 8.6%, though grammage cuts are slowing namkeen volume relative to value.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 37-38% gives ample headroom, and capex was not discussed on the call beyond the commissioned Nagpur besan unit.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance of INR 1,800-1,900 crore was only maintained despite H1 revenue of INR 883.9 crore (+26.7%), and the 8.9% margin guide was held.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Distributor additions were cut to about 220 from 250 and described as 'not exactly on track', and Gujarat is below the INR 100 crore/month aspiration, though H1 revenue is already within the FY27 range.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans two new namkeen products next quarter, and non-palm products are targeted to rise from 3.25% to 4.5% of the top line by FY27 end.

rows.label: New channels to INR 30-35 cr FY27, INR 75-90 cr FY28
rows.why: H1 railways, modern trade and quick commerce each grew strongly (quick commerce INR 7.07 cr vs INR 3.48 cr), but exports were only about INR 1 crore in October, so the FY28 target needs a sharp step-up.

rows.label: H2 cash flow recovery from inventory and insurance
rows.why: Inventory is guided to fall from about INR 200 crore to INR 100-120 crore and the INR 36.4 crore insurance claim was received in October, so H2 operating cash flow should beat H1.

rows.label: Raw material inflation pass-through
rows.why: Cumulative inflation impact is about 5.5% versus FY26 average, with about 4% passed through grammage; management expects rivals to need price hikes or grammage cuts, while chana and potato prices may rise next year.

tone.note: Management was confident on 22-23% momentum, share gains in gathiya and wafers, and operating leverage, but cautious on double-digit margins tied to raw material inflation and candid about Gujarat being below aspiration, distributor additions cut to about 220, and weaker H1 cash flow. 544141|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 36.8% YoY to INR14.3 crores, the company's highest first half, on revenue up 29.6% to INR34.2 crores.
544141|2026-09.overview: Pune E-Stock Broking reported H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) consolidated revenue from operations of INR34.2 crores, up 29.6% YoY and 24% HoH, with PBT of INR19.1 crores (+38.8%) and PAT of INR14.3 crores (+36.8%). Net profit margin was 41.7%, up 220 bps YoY but down from about 50% in H2 FY26. Management said the quarter was shaped by a weak secondary market (F&O volume cuts, higher STT in April 2026) and used the call to position MTF, merchant banking, insurance distribution and AIF as fee-based growth drivers, most of which are only months old and contribute little revenue yet. Equity rose to INR225 crores from INR180.6 crores in March, helped by warrant conversions and a new warrant issue.

financial_highlights.change: +29.6% YoY vs INR26 crores; +24% HoH vs INR27.5 crores
+36.8% YoY vs INR10.4 crores; +51% HoH vs INR9.5 crores
+220 bps YoY; below ~50% in previous half
vs INR9.3 crores a year ago

segments.name: Broking and MTF
segments.commentary: Foundation business; MTF book crossed INR100 crores, fully collateralised by client shares and cash, and is being grown 'carefully'. Short-term borrowings (INR65 crores) mainly fund the MTF book.

segments.name: Research
segments.commentary: Team of MBAs, CAs, economists and CFAs; curated equity basket lets clients invest in a research team's ideas with a single order. No revenue split disclosed.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Works with 36 AMCs and more than 500 schemes; over 1,600 investors, AUM above INR240 crores, SIP book over INR1.5 crores. Capital-light, fee-based, recurring.

segments.name: PESB Alpha Fund (Cat III AIF) / PESB Asset Management LLP
segments.commentary: Launched November 2025, about INR55 crores under management; PESB invested INR15 crores. Management claims about 25% post-fee, post-tax return in year one; income accrues to the wholly owned fund-manager LLP. Clients typically commit for at least three years.

segments.name: Merchant banking
segments.commentary: Licence obtained about a year ago (2025); first fees earned in 2026. First mandate Apar Advertisers (SME) approved and expected to list within a couple of months; several other SME and mainboard mandates in pipeline. No fee figures disclosed.

segments.name: Insurance distribution (Pune Finvest / QURA Insure)
segments.commentary: Pune Finvest (79.8% subsidiary) received IRDAI corporate agency approval in July 2026; advisory operations began September 2026 under the QURA Insure brand, initially targeting the existing 65,000 clients. No revenue disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Sustain double-digit profit growth.
Improve return ratios as fee-based businesses (wealth, merchant banking, insurance, AIF) scale; management expects ROE and ROCE to move up steadily but gave no targets.
Grow to more than 1 lakh customers by 2027 (client base currently above 65,000, of whom above 17,000 are traded clients).

Plans: open flagship branches in high-visibility locations, grow the MTF book carefully, scale an open API-based algo trading platform for retail, and build GIFT City merchant banking, secured lending and insurance businesses.

Warrant proceeds (16 lakh warrants at INR234 each, 25% received) to be deployed mainly in MTF and merchant banking; branches and technology funded as needed; promoters participated in the warrant round so dilution is limited.
capex_capacity: Capital allocation is driven by MTF book growth and merchant banking; branch and technology spend is 'on need basis' per management.
Warrant issue: 16 lakh convertible warrants at INR234 each, 25% of subscription received; 18 lakh equity shares issued on warrant conversion during H1.
Dividend: final dividend of INR1 per share for FY26 paid.
PESB committed INR15 crores to PESB Alpha Fund; AIF size about INR55 crores.
Planned flagship branches in high-visibility locations; no count or timelines disclosed.
demand_pricing: Industry context: SEBI F&O measures more than halved option volumes in 2026 and cut individual F&O traders by about a fifth; higher STT on derivatives from April 2026 added pressure.
Industry margin trading book rose from above INR1.4 lakh crores (June 2026) to about INR1.6 lakh crores (September 2026), per management.
Mainboard IPOs raised a record INR94,200 crores across 78 issues in H1 CY26 (35% higher YoY per management); total IPO fundraise including SME exceeded INR1 lakh crores.
Management expects margins on insurance to fall under IRDAI commission-cap proposals but volumes to rise; sees MTF rule tightening as a long-term positive that reduces speculation in weak scrips.

Management said the call's market backdrop was weak: Nifty about 1% up for H1, down about 6% in September; FIIs net sellers of over INR2.3 lakh crores in April-September 2026; domestic institutions bought about INR3.9 lakh crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the view on merchant banking and the IPO pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ronak Jhaveri said the first mandate, Apar Advertisers (SME), is approved and listing is planned within a couple of months; several SME and mainboard mandates are in the pipeline and will be disclosed on BSE as they are signed.

qa_highlights.question: Will share capital increase, where will growth be funded, and how are Pune Finvest, PESB Alpha Fund, PESB Asset Management LLP and IFSC structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Arpit Shah said growth will be funded by internal accruals and the recent warrant issue, mainly into MTF and merchant banking. Pune Finvest is a 79.8% subsidiary holding the NBFC and insurance business; the AIF trust has appointed PESB Asset Management LLP, a wholly owned subsidiary, as fund manager. He did not detail the IFSC entity.

qa_highlights.question: Why a corporate agency licence rather than an insurance broking licence?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate agency approval came faster from IRDAI, with a consultant's guidance, and the holding-company structure delayed the insurance-company route; management said many NBFCs operate as corporate agents with no major structural difference.

qa_highlights.question: How will warrant proceeds be deployed and how is dilution weighed?
qa_highlights.answer: Proceeds go mainly to MTF and merchant banking, with branches and technology funded as needed. Promoters participated equally in the warrant round, so promoter stake is not expected to dilute materially.

qa_highlights.question: What are the return-ratio drivers and the biggest risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fee-based businesses are capital-light and returns should improve as they contribute; new licences are only a year old, so contribution is still small. The main risk cited is regulatory change, which is industry-wide, and management said it is confident of coping given over 15 years in the business.

qa_highlights.question: How will IRDAI commission caps and SEBI's MTF rule review affect the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance margins will fall, but volumes should rise; management expects no major issue from MTF rules and said it is prepared if final rules are stricter, with benefits over the long term rather than the short term.

qa_highlights.question: How will cross-selling of mutual fund and advisory products be done, and is it RM-led or digital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management uses RM-led face-to-face coverage for suitability and risk-profiling, backed by a digital team to reach clients in locations without physical presence.

qa_highlights.question: Is AIF fee income lumpy and how will the AIF scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AIF fees are consistent because investors commit for at least three years; year one delivered about 25% post-fee, post-tax return, and marketing through RMs and word of mouth is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is MTF concentration risk managed in a sharp fall, and what is the collateral shortfall record?
qa_highlights.answer: Software tracks positions, MTM and collateral shortfalls, with staff contacting clients; if a shortfall persists for more than five days, the stock is liquidated. No historical shortfall figures were given.

risks_watch: Regulatory risk: SEBI review of MTF rules and IRDAI proposals to cap insurance commissions could compress margins; management called the impact short-term.
Net profit margin fell from about 50% in H2 FY26 to 41.7% in H1 FY27; watch whether this is a trend as new businesses scale.
Weak F&O activity and higher STT on derivatives could keep broking volumes under pressure.
MTF book growth of INR100 crores plus INR65 crores of short-term borrowings raise funding and collateral-shortfall risk in a sharp market fall; no shortfall history was disclosed.
Warrant conversion (16 lakh warrants at INR234) and merchant banking/IPO execution depend on primary-market momentum; the Apar Advertisers listing is a near-term test.
Management gave no quantified revenue targets for new businesses, and merchant banking and insurance revenue was not separately disclosed.
key_quotes: Our consolidated revenue from operations grew around 30% to INR34.2 crores. EBITDA grew by 31% to INR22.3 crores, and net profit grew almost 37% to INR14.3 crores, our highest for any first half of the year.
We will not pursue growth at any cost. We will build with discipline, invest where we see clear opportunity, and remain mindful of the trust our clients and shareholders place in us.
So yes, we may find a short-term hitch in our profitability or margins, but in the longer term, it is actually working in our favour.
Since these licenses have come just a year back, there is no significant contribution to revenue from these segments as yet.
544141|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profit and the new fee-based businesses, citing record H1 PAT and a 25% first-year AIF return. Cautious on the market backdrop, regulation and risk, which management called a short-term hitch, and it gave no quantified targets for new businesses.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Net profit margin was 41.7% in H1 FY27, up 220 bps YoY but down from about 50% in H2 FY26, and new fee businesses are only months old with little revenue yet, so margin direction is unclear.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Flagship branches are planned in high-visibility locations with no count or timeline disclosed, and branch spend is 'on need basis', so timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets more than 1 lakh customers by 2027 from about 65,000 today, and the MTF book crossed INR100 crores, though the industry F&O volumes were cut sharply in 2026.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital allocation is tied to MTF and merchant banking growth with branch and technology spend on need basis, and no utilisation or capex figures were given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is only double-digit profit growth for FY27 with no quantified revenue or margin targets, and H1 PAT growth of 36.8% already exceeds it, but management has not signalled a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Weak F&O volumes, higher STT from April 2026, a 6% fall in Nifty in September and MTF rule tightening could slow broking and MTF growth against the double-digit profit guide.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Apar Advertisers SME listing
rows.why: First merchant banking mandate is approved and listing is planned within a couple of months, a near-term test of the merchant banking pipeline.

rows.label: QURA Insure insurance advisory scale-up
rows.why: IRDAI corporate agency approval came in July 2026 and advisory began September 2026 targeting 65,000 existing clients, but no revenue has been disclosed and IRDAI commission caps may cut margins.

rows.label: Warrant conversion and fund deployment into MTF
rows.why: 16 lakh warrants at INR234 with 25% received, with proceeds mainly going to MTF and merchant banking, while the MTF book already crossed INR100 crores and industry margin book rose to about INR1.6 lakh crores.

tone.note: Management was confident on record H1 PAT, the 25% first-year AIF return and new fee businesses, but cautious on weak markets, SEBI MTF rules and IRDAI commission caps, and gave no quantified targets; analysts pressed on merchant banking pipeline, dilution, return drivers and MTF collateral risk.

544144|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue up ~28% YoY and FY26 EBITDA up 16% to INR203.4 crore, but FY26 reported PAT still a loss of INR12.5 crore.
544144|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 28% YoY and total income reached INR1,758.8 crore (up 27.8%), with EBITDA of INR57.5 crore (margin about 3.3%) and a loss of INR5 crore versus INR13.7 crore loss a year earlier. FY26 total income was INR6,401.1 crore (up 15.1%) and reported EBITDA INR203.4 crore (margin 3.2%), while PAT was a loss of INR12.5 crore against INR10.5 crore loss in FY25. Management said the FY26 revenue and EBITDA were hit by acquisition costs, a cess provision and the new labour code impact, and it apologised for an error in the April 17, 2026 business update that misstated Q4 growth figures. Management guides FY27 to high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin of about 4.8-5%, with sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: vs loss of INR13.7 crore in Q4 FY25
up 28% YoY, after adjusting Honda/Piaggio divestment, acquisition impact and one-off provision

financial_highlights.value: loss of INR13 crore (before exceptional items loss of INR27 crore on reported basis)
financial_highlights.change: adjusted PBT loss about INR5 crore; adjusted PBT before exceptional items positive INR8.8 crore
vs loss of INR10.5 crore in FY25
up 19% YoY; organic INR4,493 crore, up 16%
up 7% YoY; organic INR868 crore, up 8%

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (new)
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes 8,090 units (up 20%), income INR654 crore (up 18%). FY26 volumes 32,572 units (up 9%), income INR2,551 crore (up 9%). Management cited entry-level supply shortages and OEM supply constraints in Keralam.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicle services
segments.commentary: Q4 service volumes 1,80,989 units (down 14%), income INR154 crore (up 2%). FY26 service income INR607 crore (down 2%) with volumes 7,39,794 (down 12%); ASP growth offset the volume decline.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles (new)
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes 3,716 units (up 59%), income INR645 crore (up 46%). FY26 volumes 12,546 units (up 30%), income INR2,125 crore (up 32%); BharatBenz Punjab acquisition contributed.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicle services
segments.commentary: Q4 service volumes 52,443 units (up 13%), income INR97 crore (up 75%). FY26 volumes 2,02,647 (up 10%), income INR351 crore (up 28%).

segments.name: EV (Ather 2-wheelers) new and services
segments.commentary: Q4 new vehicles 3,079 units (up 138%), income INR50 crore (up 113%); service volumes 11,261 (up 81%), income about INR3 crore. FY26 new vehicles 8,154 units (up 89%), income INR137 crore (up 72%); service volumes 39,659 (up 79%), income about INR9 crore (up 18%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 target of high double-digit top-line growth and consolidated EBITDA margin moving to about 4.8-5%; PAT approaching FY24 levels.
Sustainable profitability expected from Q2 FY27; Q1 FY27 still expected to be loss-making due to Maruti and JLR supply constraints.
PV service volumes guided to grow at least 10-12% in FY27, with ASP growth of about 12-13%; CV service volumes guided up 7-8% with ASP up 8-10%.
Standalone sales margin guided at about 3-4% in FY27; spare parts margin guided back to 5.5-6% with revenue growth of 6-8% (ex-BKT).
JLR volume guidance of 550-600 vehicles in FY27 after about 380 Audi/JLR volume shortfall in FY26 (guided about 450); Audi expected to break even this year.
Non-Keralam revenue share to exceed 50% in FY27 from about 47% in FY26; no high-value acquisitions planned in FY27, focus on consolidating FY26 acquisitions.
Inventory to be held at or below 30 days for passenger cars; debt increase attributed to acquisitions, with ~INR520 crore of INR600+ crore debt inventory-linked.
capex_capacity: Three acquisitions in FY26: BharatBenz dealership in Punjab, Maruti Suzuki dealership in Telangana, and Audi dealership operations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; Honda and Piaggio businesses divested (volumes counted to August 2025).
JLR Nagpur operations commenced April 1, 2026; new Maruti touchpoints and multiple Ather touchpoints opened in Q4.
Bank loan facilities increased from INR468 crore to INR643 crore; CRISIL A/Stable rating extended to March 2027.
Management said capex spends will be more monitored and no additional debt is planned beyond what is needed to run the current business.
Acquired Audi and Telangana assets totalled about INR85-90 crore of equipment and showroom assets, with acquisition cost approximately equal.
demand_pricing: Management said demand improved in H2 FY26 after GST reforms in September 2025, with stronger footfall, conversion and entry-level recovery; discounting moderated.
Shortages of entry-level vehicles in Jan-Mar 2026 eased in April-May; Baleno and Fronx have waiting periods.
Post OEM price increases, management reported no noticeable change in demand so far; some pre-ponement of bookings was seen.
Luxury segment: Q4 delayed by UK FTA price-cut expectation; price cuts applied to Range Rover SP and Autobiography, with bookings rising from April.
Service volume: running repair fell about 17-18% as the company deprioritised low-value jobs; collision repair volumes flat; free service volumes recovered in last 6 months.
Maruti share of service volumes about 65-70%; Maruti service volume decline narrowed from -7% (to Q3) to -2% in Q4.
Overall Maruti ASP up about 13% YoY; PV new vehicle weighted ASP up to about 6.5% from about 5.5% three years earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Why did service volumes fall and what service volume and ASP growth is guided for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 service volumes fell about 6% and ASP rose about 14%, with revenue up over 8%. For FY27 it guided 10-12% PV service volume growth and matching ASP growth; CV service volume growth of 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the service EBITDA margin gap versus peers close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated margin will not reach 18% because of CV and Ather mix, but the Passenger Car business should reach 18-19% service margin.

qa_highlights.question: How will standalone margins move from about 3% to 5% consolidated?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the margin drag to acquisitions and Telangana expansion; growth is to come from PV service volumes and ASP, plus JLR and Audi ramp-up, with consolidated EBITDA guided to 4.8-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add acquisitions and how will debt be reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: No high-value acquisitions planned in FY27. About INR520 crore of the INR600+ crore debt is inventory-linked; term loans will be repaid on schedule, and debt will fall if inventory release generates free cash.

qa_highlights.question: Is inventory under control and what is the demand reaction to OEM price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell from 49 to 36 (FY25 to FY26); management aims to keep it below 30 days. Post price hikes, demand was flat and supply has normalised in April-May.

qa_highlights.question: When will the company turn sustainably profitable and what happened in Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable profitability from Q2 FY27. Q1 remains affected by Maruti and JLR supply constraints; service volumes expected to grow Q1 over Q1.

risks_watch: Reported FY26 PAT loss of INR12.5 crore; Telangana loss of about INR26-27 crore and cess provision weigh on profitability, with Ind AS depreciation on acquisitions.
Debt rose after acquisitions; management says inventory debt is about INR520 crore of INR600+ crore total, with inventory days to stay below 30.
Error in April 17, 2026 business update, which misstated Q4 revenue growth; management apologised and promised process fixes.
CEO Raj Narayan has resigned to pursue an opportunity outside the industry; successor not named on this call.
JLR cyber-attack and supply constraints cost about INR70 crore of top line and INR8-9 crore of bottom line in FY26; Q1 FY27 supply still constrained.
Service volumes in running repair down 17-18%; management needs to show Q1 FY27 volume growth.
Fuel price and geopolitical uncertainty (referred to as a war situation) flagged as demand risks.
key_quotes: Before moving to the business performance, I would like to sincerely apologize for the error in the business update published on April 17 , 2026, for the quarter and the year ended March 31 , 2026, and take this opportunity to clarify the same.
Post the price increase announcement by the OEMs, we have not seen much of a change actually.
In terms of profitability from Q2 of FY '27, we should be having sustainable profitability.
Out of the INR600 odd crores, around INR520 crores is related to the debt on inventory.

544144|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~44% YoY to INR1,890 crore and reported EBITDA rose ~87% to INR71.5 crore (3.8% margin), with reported PBT turning positive at INR1.9 crore.
544144|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 44% YoY to INR1,890 crore, with new vehicle volumes up about 81% reported and about 91% like-to-like. Reported EBITDA rose about 87% to INR71.5 crore, margin 3.8% vs 2.9%, helped by a one-off ~INR5 crore lease-modification gain in other income. Organic revenue grew 33% YoY, indicating the existing network contributed alongside the FY26 acquisitions (RKS Maruti, Globe CV BharatBenz, Audi/Olympus). Management said the acquired businesses are now EBITDA-positive in aggregate (~INR9.4 crore) but still loss-making below EBITDA due to depreciation and finance costs; reported PAT was INR1.4 crore vs a loss of INR8.8 crore a year ago.

segments.name: Passenger Vehicles (ex-luxury)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR836 crore (+73% YoY reported, +54% excluding luxury per call); new vehicles 10,475 units (+83%); service volumes 1,90,801 (-5%) while service income INR169 crore (+11%). Organic PV revenue +49%. PV EBITDA margin ~4% per management, with Maruti ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at segment level.

segments.name: Luxury (JLR and Audi)
segments.commentary: Reported revenue +42%; new vehicles +39%; service volumes +87%. Organic luxury revenue +21%, service volumes +9%. JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA ~nil, with margin dip attributed to Audi.

segments.name: Commercial Vehicles
segments.commentary: Revenue INR564 crore (+33% reported, +35% per call; organic +21%); new vehicles 3,495 units (+41%); service volumes 52,647 (+15%), service income INR107 crore (+47%). Sequentially volumes moderated vs Q4. Management cites CV EBITDA ~3.6-3.75%.

segments.name: EV (Ather two-wheelers and e-VITARA)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR55 crore (+122% YoY; reported EV revenue +113%); new vehicles 3,330 units (+153%); service volumes 13,232 (+60%), service income ~INR3 crore. EBITDA ~INR2 crore; margin ~3.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects acquired businesses to be PAT-positive from Q2 FY27 onwards; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end of Q3, with Olympus possibly one more quarter.
RKS service volumes expected on track by Q4 FY27.
PV service volume growth expected at ~6-7% from Q2 (not the 15% previously guided), with ASP continuing to rise; Maruti service volumes expected to reach double digit from Q2.
Blended EBITDA margin: management hopes to reach ~4% and says ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% unlikely this year unless mix changes.
FY27 revenue targeted at INR8,200-8,300 crore vs ~INR6,400 crore in FY26 (~20-25% growth).
H2 PV growth so far running ~80-90% YoY in most months, expected to moderate on high base; Q3 flagged as key with Audi launch.
Capex limited to replacement and ongoing projects; no acquisition or expansion planned; surplus cash to be used first for debt reduction.
capex_capacity: Q1 network additions: new Maruti Suzuki service centre at Koyilandy (Kerala), two Tata CV outlets at Perumbavoor and Kazhakuttam, and a JLR sales and service facility in Nagpur.
New vehicle inventory ~32 days vs ~50 days a year ago; absolute inventory up only ~14% YoY despite higher revenue; sequential build ahead of festive season and OEM launches.
Audi inventory elevated, expected to fall to ~20-25 days in August-September.
Ather inventory ~5 days, JLR supply somewhat constrained.
Keralam revenue share fell below 50% for the first time (49%), state mix: Tamil Nadu 22%, Karnataka 12%, Telangana 8%, Maharashtra 5%, Punjab 4%, Andhra Pradesh 0.3%.
demand_pricing: Pre-festive inquiries up ~20% YoY over recent days, ~17-18% over the last month; bookings up ~22% YoY.
Keralam inauspicious period ends 16 August; retail expected to pick up from 17 August (Onam-Chingam).
CV demand weak in construction: tipper segment low to negative growth; SCV and cargo holding.
Maruti price increases modest (INR5,000-7,000 for most models; INR10,000-15,000 for some), with no major impact on demand or margin.
Entry-level cars recovered: Alto K10 and WagonR strong; S-Presso slowing; Arena returned to growth.
Spare parts short supply in the market, causing vehicles to stay in workshops.
Running repairs up ~8.8% in July; free service turned to growth in Q1.
Commercial ticket size ~INR16-17 lakh is pulling blended margin down.

qa_highlights.question: How are inquiries and bookings trending into the festive period, and what is the H2 FY27 growth outlook for PV, CV and EV?
qa_highlights.answer: Inquiries up about 20% YoY over recent days and 17-18% over the last month; bookings up about 22% YoY. Keralam is in an inauspicious period until 16 August, with retail expected to pick up from 17 August. PV H2 growth running about 80-90% YoY in most months, likely to moderate on high base; Q3 seen as key with Audi launch. CV construction demand weak (tipper low to negative), SCV and cargo holding.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin move toward 4-5%, and how will the acquisitions' turnaround affect margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5% will take a long time because CV mix is rising (average CV ticket ~INR16-17 lakh). Blended margin hoped to reach ~4% and ~4.3-4.4% by year end; 5% not expected unless mix changes considerably. Acquired businesses are EBITDA-positive in aggregate at ~INR9.4 crore; RKS and Olympus targeted for PAT profitability by end Q3, Olympus possibly one more quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up the INR11.2 crore adjusted PBT vs INR1.9 crore reported PBT?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap is acquisition effects: acquisitions contributed ~INR9.4 crore EBITDA (Globe ~INR2.1 crore, RKS ~INR7.4 crore, Olympus neutral), offset by ~INR12 crore depreciation and ~INR6.8 crore finance cost. At PBT, RKS was about negative INR5.3 crore and Olympus about negative INR4 crore; Globe roughly neutral.

qa_highlights.question: What are the segment margins, ex-acquisitions, for PV and Luxury?
qa_highlights.answer: JLR EBITDA INR10.5 crore vs INR8.2 crore a year ago; Audi EBITDA roughly nil, dragging luxury margin. PV EBITDA about 4% now, up from INR9.4 crore to about INR35 crore on Maruti, with Honda a negative INR4.2 crore in Q1. Maruti margin ~15.5-16% and JLR ~17-18% at the model level, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Service volume guidance: is the 10-12% growth target on track after PV service volumes fell 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management no longer expects 15%; PV service volume growth guided at ~6-7% from Q2 as Honda base drops out. Maruti service volumes up ~8% YoY, expected to reach double digit from Q2. Service ASP up ~15% in PV; Maruti ASP INR6.6 lakh to 6.7 lakh and JLR INR1.07 crore to INR1.26 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is new vehicle sales business profitable after interest cost, and what is the split of the INR30 crore finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Maruti sales EBITDA ~1.7% (vs about -2% a year ago), ~0.85% after interest; JLR ~5%; TCV/BharatBenz ~3% with interest under 1%; Ather ~4.2% with negligible interest. Split of the ~INR30 crore finance cost was not given on the call; to be emailed to the analyst.

Audi inventory elevated (expected to fall to ~20-25 days in Aug-Sep) and Audi margin at nil until Q3 launches; JLR supply constrained and Ather inventory ~5 days.
CV construction demand weak (tipper low to negative); Keralam market sentiment tied to Onam-Chingam timing; leadership transition as CEO Raj Narayan departs after August 2026.

But in terms of volume, we are hoping to grow from Q2 onwards. July numbers have come in pretty strong in terms of growth. So we're hoping to maintain that.

544149|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell about 12% YoY to INR364.94 crore on selective bidding, while PAT rose 11% to INR18.85 crore; FY26 consolidated order book is about INR2,500 crore+.
544149|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue was INR364.94 crore, down nearly 12% YoY but up 19% QoQ, as management deliberately skipped low-margin bids. EBITDA excluding other income fell 11% YoY to INR23.78 crore, yet margin edged up 3 bps to 6.51% and PAT grew over 11% YoY to INR18.85 crore. For FY26, revenue rose 5.32% to INR1,277.28 crore, EBITDA rose 7.5% to INR83.53 crore (6.54% margin), and PAT was INR64.35 crore (up nearly 3%). Management guided to upwards of 20% consolidated revenue growth in FY27 and announced the 100% acquisition of Citelum India, its first acquisition, for smart lighting and urban infrastructure.

segments.name: Government business
segments.commentary: Management is being more selective in bidding; 2 new contracts in Q4 FY26 and 17 for the full year. Mix was about 70:30 government to corporate, with a stated aim to rebalance toward corporate.

segments.name: Corporate business
segments.commentary: Management says corporate margin profile has improved since the pandemic. Management cited 177+ new customers and 250+ new sites added in FY26, with INR300 crore of multi-year new business value.

segments.commentary: Currently managing more than 350 TPD. Qualification allows bids for about 480-500 TPD by fiscal year-end, with a target of 800-1,000 TPD over 18 months. Vasai Virar MSW win was among top 3 qualifying agencies with technology partner MTS.

segments.name: Citelum India (acquisition)
segments.commentary: Board approved 100% acquisition of Citelum India Pvt Ltd from Citelum S.A.S. (EDF Group). Company is in smart lighting, street lighting, and city O&M, with smart city presence in Ahmedabad, Noida and Chennai. Financial terms and closing timeline were not disclosed on the call.

segments.commentary: Start-up B2C residential deep-cleaning platform with FY26 revenue of about INR46 lakh. Management expects traction to begin from Q2 FY27 and will not give a 2-3 year revenue guidance yet.

Pan-India network of 31 branches, serving 570+ customers across 4,000+ locations.

Management says it wins corporate deals against CBRE, JLL, SIS and Sodexo by offering direct service delivery rather than outsourced services.
Q4 revenue decline attributed to about INR180 crore of business not bid for on margin grounds, plus tender decisions pending from previous fiscal.

qa_highlights.question: How does Krystal differentiate from global players such as CBRE, JLL, SIS and Sodexo in large corporate mandates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the services are similar but Krystal is the direct service provider, while global players are property managers that outsource services. Many new customers were won against these players.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 3-5 year vision and business mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Rebalancing the government/corporate mix from about 70:30 by adding corporates, with government growth in waste management, O&M and city infrastructure. Management aims to be a diversified player with all verticals revenue-making and profitable within 5 years.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue has Taskmaster contributed and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 revenue was about INR46 lakh. Pilots are ongoing and traction is expected from Q2 FY27, but no 2-3 year revenue guidance was given.

qa_highlights.question: What quantifies the Q4 revenue drop of 11.7% YoY, and is it due to exits, slower orders or tender delays?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR180 crore of business was not bid for to protect margins, and some government tender decisions are pending, which pushed business into later periods. Management says the order book covers this and the shortfall will be made up in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for commercialising bioenzyme technology?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the technology is still in pilot with VPRC Chennai in Mira-Bhayandar and Vasai Virar, and no commercial cost or revenue timeline has been set yet.

544149|2026-09.headline: Krystal Q2 FY27 revenue rose 46.25% YoY to Rs 414.47 crore, but EBITDA margin eased to 6.0% from 6.32% on higher employee cost.
544149|2026-09.overview: Consolidated revenue for Q2 FY27 reached Rs 414.47 crore, up 46.25% YoY and 14.9% QoQ, with H1 revenue at Rs 775.18 crore (up 27.82%). EBITDA excluding other income grew 38.82% to Rs 24.86 crore, but margin moderated to 6.0% from 6.32% as employee cost rose to 75.9% of revenue from 72.3%. PAT grew 41.66% to Rs 18.67 crore in Q2, helped by a lower effective tax rate of 12.5%. Management highlighted the Citelum India acquisition, new segments (solid waste management, solar EPC, technical FM) and a Rs 2,980-3,000 crore order book spanning about 3 to 3.5 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Jabalpur is a pilot revenue-sharing FOCO store with DP retaining full operational control. Plan is 2-3 franchisee stores a year over the next four to five years, with the 51-store mix described as mostly COCO and a smaller FOCO share.

544162|2026-03.headline: Bharti Hexacom FY26 revenue grew 9.4% and EBITDAaL 17.9%, with Q4 revenue at Rs 2,414 Crores (+2.3% QoQ) and EBITDAaL margin of 47.9%.
544162|2026-03.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported strong FY26 operating leverage, with EBITDAaL margin up 3.4 points to 47.6% and a record 395,000 net homes adds. Q4 revenue grew 2.3% sequentially to Rs 2,414 Crores, while ARPU of Rs 252 was dented by two fewer days and was about Rs 257-258 on an EDB basis. Management flagged handset price rises, lower international roaming and 5G pack consumption as ARPU headwinds, and a Rs 4,000 Crore-range regulatory provision was booked on a changed interpretation of an existing issue. The call was largely a joint Airtel-Hexacom webinar; Hexacom questions focused on lagging mobile growth versus Airtel, FWA versus fiber strategy, and payout.

segments.name: Homes and office
segments.commentary: Record net adds of 148,000 in Q4 and 395,000 for FY26; FY26 homes and office revenue grew 51%. Q4 homes revenue rose about 21% sequentially, helped by FWA expansion to new pin codes, FTTH deepening and IPTV rollout.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance given; management said it does not provide guidance and that Hexacom remains committed to progressively increasing dividend payout.
ARPU headwinds expected to persist from lower international roaming, handset price rises and 5G consumption packs; management said there are no red flags on ARPU.

Hexacom will not give up on homes acquisition; in difficult terrain FWA is used to reach homes where fiber is costly, with fiber-first where available.
capex_capacity: Q4 capex was Rs 586 Crores, described as acceleration as planned.
FY26 capex directed to 5G densification, network modernization and homes and IPTV growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Hexacom mobile revenue growth (8.3%) lagged Airtel (close to 12%), and should it accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray said Hexacom is underpenetrated in its two circles and the ARPU gap has closed; postpaid and international roaming differences and smartphone upgrade stress may cause some lag, and convergence offers are being launched.

qa_highlights.question: Should Hexacom have a sharper payout ratio given limited growth engines and funded capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said dividend moved from Rs 3-4 to Rs 10-18 per share and it remains committed to a progressively rising payout, while growth engines available to the parent are not open to Hexacom.

qa_highlights.question: Could homes growth slow due to chipset and memory cost issues affecting FWA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FWA remains useful for reaching homes in difficult terrain such as the North East, and it will not give up on home acquisition, pivoting to fiber where available.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the ARPU shortfall beyond international roaming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 5G pack adoption that breaks the price ladder, handset price increases pressuring 2G to 4G upgrades, and lower roaming; the quarter-average ARPU is not a red flag per management.

qa_highlights.question: Should homes subscriber additions continue at the current pace?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined forward-looking guidance but said the objective is to keep growing homes and there is no fundamental reason to ease efforts, though competition exists.

qa_highlights.question: What does the regulatory charge in Q4 relate to and is it new demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not new; an existing matter was re-interpreted with auditors and the audit committee and a provision was taken under prudent accounting, with no specifics disclosed.

risks_watch: ARPU trajectory with handset price increases, lower international roaming and 5G unlimited packs; Q4 ARPU was Rs 252 reported.
Homes momentum if chipset and memory costs keep FWA more expensive and push the company toward slower fiber rollout in difficult terrain.
