544162|2026-06.headline: Bharti Hexacom Q1 FY27 revenue rose 4% QoQ to Rs2,510 Cr with EBITDAaL margin of 48.2%, while homes net adds slowed to 75k.
544162|2026-06.overview: Bharti Hexacom reported Q1 FY27 revenue of about Rs2,510 Crores, up 4% sequentially, with EBITDAaL of about Rs1,210 Crores at a 48.2% margin. Mobile added about 210,000 net customers on a 29 million base, with ARPU at Rs259 helped by one extra day. Homes, office and other business net adds were 75k and revenue grew about 8% sequentially; management attributed the slower homes intake to a deliberate tightening of acquisition quality. Operating free cash flow (EBITDAaL minus capex) was about Rs830 Crores and net debt excluding leases was about Rs960 Crores (0.2x EBITDAaL). The call was a joint Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom webinar, and most Q&A addressed group-level topics.

Homes, office and other net adds

segments.name: Homes, office and other
segments.commentary: Net adds of 75k, with revenue up about 8% QoQ. IPTV rollout is adding depreciation; EBIT margin for the CPE-based homes business is negative or immaterial until scale is reached.

Homes acquisition was tightened after the FWA push brought weaker quality and higher churn; management said fundamentals of the homes market have not changed.
Rajasthan was described as extremely competitive, while the Northeast position is comfortable; intensity on customer acquisition is said to be no different from other circles.

International roaming is improving from the prior-quarter West Asia-related decline.

qa_highlights.question: Why did mobile net adds weaken this quarter versus history, and was it circle-specific?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray said there is normal seasonality in customer depletion across the industry over 16-20 quarters and that additions typically pick up in the second half of the year. He declined to call out a circle-specific cause.

qa_highlights.question: Has the homes outlook changed given acquisition-policy changes and rising chipset costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no change in the market size, share-gain or pricing assumptions. The slowdown reflects a one-quarter correction in acquisition quality, which management expects to unwind in the next quarter or two.

qa_highlights.question: Why are energy costs lower year on year despite higher diesel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Karthikeyan Velu cited seasonal solar-powered tower benefits and some one-offs. Soumen Ray added that diesel stock in DG sets means the full diesel price impact has not yet flowed through, and that the underlying sequential trend is as planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did depreciation rise 4.9% QoQ, and when will homes turn profitable at EBIT?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation rose because of one extra day and the IPTV rollout. Management gave no timeline for homes EBIT turning positive, but said it will once the business reaches scale, and that fiber rental versus owned fiber makes little difference at the EBIT level.

qa_highlights.question: How many of the 400 relevant cities are in Hexacom's circles, and how big is the homes opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: Soumen Ray estimated about 15-17 of the 400 cities are in the Northeast and Rajasthan circles, and said the figure would be confirmed later. Wireless plus wired is the chosen strategy in these terrain-heavy circles.

FWA economics face pressure from higher memory and chipset prices, and the FWA pivot to fiber could slow rollout in some areas.

544162|2026-09.headline: Bharti Hexacom FY26 revenue grew 9.4% and EBITDAaL 17.9% to a 47.6% margin, but Q4 ARPU of Rs.252 was dragged by roaming and 5G pack dynamics.
544162|2026-09.overview: This is a combined Bharti Airtel and Bharti Hexacom Q4 FY26 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) earnings webinar, held May 14, 2026, with the Hexacom segment covered in the second half. Hexacom delivered record FY26 net adds of 395,000 and a 3.4-point margin expansion to 47.6%, while Q4 revenue rose 2.3% sequentially to Rs.2,414 crore. Q4 ARPU was Rs.252 (about Rs.257-258 on an EDB basis) and management acknowledged headwinds from lower international roaming, handset price increases and 5G pack adoption. The Board recommended a Rs.18 dividend per share versus Rs.10 last year. A parent-level Africa share swap (additional 16.3% stake in Airtel Africa) was also announced, though it does not directly affect Hexacom.

Management said FY26 revenue growth was 8.3% against about 12% at Airtel, and the ARPU gap has narrowed.

segments.name: Homes and offices (Hexacom)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 51% with record net adds of 395,000 for the year; Q4 added a record 148,000 with revenue up about 21% QoQ. Growth is driven by FWA expansion to new pin codes, FTTH deepening and the IPTV rollout.

Management expects smartphone upgrades to face some stress, which may leave Hexacom slightly behind on mobile growth.
Management said it will not give up on home acquisition and that FWA and fiber will both continue to be used where economical.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Hexacom is under-penetrated and the ARPU gap has narrowed; postpaid and international roaming mix will differ, and smartphone upgrades may stress growth. It is not lagging the market.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the cost of connecting homes is higher in difficult terrain and FWA lets it reach more homes; it will not give up acquisition and will prefer fiber where available.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5G pack adoption (eat-as-much-as-you-can packs) is a headwind alongside lower roaming and handset prices; Q4 ARPU is an average, with no red flag on the exit rate.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a prudent provision on an existing item where the interpretation changed; nothing new or exceptional, though the amount was not specified.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give guidance but said there is no reason to expect a slowdown and the effort to grow homes continues despite competition.

544166|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 27% YoY to INR113 crores and EBITDA 28% to INR23 crores (~20% margin), with PAT near INR8 crores held back by H2 hiring.
544166|2026-03.overview: Emmforce reported FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) revenue of about INR113 crores, up 27% YoY, with EBITDA of about INR23 crores (up 28%) and PAT of about INR8 crores. Management attributed the PAT moderation to manpower hired ahead of the US export programme and higher depreciation from EMSPL and capacity capex. The US OEM export order contributed only about INR5.5-6 crores, all in March 2026, after production started in December 2025 and final customer go-ahead came end-February. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR195 crores (INR165 crores automotive plus INR30 crores agri) and FY28 of about INR240 crores, with EBITDA margins of 20-22% and PAT near 10%.

financial_highlights.change: Moderated YoY due to hiring and depreciation

financial_highlights.metric: US export order revenue in FY26
Employee cost, H1 to H2 FY26
financial_highlights.change: Mainly attributed to US export order hires

segments.name: Automotive (drivetrain, US OEM and aftermarket)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity about INR200 crores with utilisation of 50-55%. FY26 automotive revenue about INR105 crores; FY27 target INR165 crores, with the ~INR60 crores increment mainly from the US export order. About 40% of automotive revenue expected from OEMs by end-FY27; management sees OEM share reaching ~60% over time.

segments.name: Agri (rotavator blades, parts, EMSPL)
segments.commentary: Installed capacity about INR150 crores with utilisation of 8-10%. Revenue run-rate about INR4 crores per half in FY26 (commercial sales from July 2025 per analyst question, TAFE sales from January 2026); FY27 target INR30 crores and FY28 target about INR50 crores. TAFE initially ordering about INR15 lakh per month, with its total monthly requirement of about INR35-50 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target about INR195 crores: INR165 crores automotive and INR30 crores agri; management said the INR190-195 crore figure is tracking in line for the current two months.
FY28 revenue target about INR240 crores, with agri contributing about INR50 crores.
EBITDA margin target 20-22% and PAT margin around 10% for coming years.
Order book exceeds INR500 crores, but management said only about INR60 crores per annum is executable, spread over the next eight years.
Asset turnover (gross basis) about 3x in FY26, rising to 3.5-4x in FY27.
Working capital to be funded from sanctioned bank lines and US export credit of up to six months; management said equity dilution is not needed and is open to invoice factoring.
No new product category planned for at least the next year; hydraulic gear pumps to become a separate division, though no numbers disclosed yet.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about INR350 crores (automotive ~INR200 crores, agri ~INR150 crores) against FY26 revenue of INR113 crores.
Dedicated greenfield US OEM facility commissioned; mass production started 15 December 2025.

EMSPL (agri and forging subsidiary) completed first year; houses a 1,600-tonne forging press and a fully automated rotavator blade line with major equipment from Japan; turned from cash loss to modest cash profit.
Facilities total about 150,000 sq ft in Baddi, Himachal Pradesh, with 600+ staff; R&D spend about 2% of revenue.
Capex in FY26 executed ahead of revenue ramp (capacity, backward integration, automation, forging, infrastructure) across automotive and agri.
demand_pricing: Management said the US customer visit (about two weeks, roughly 10 days before the call) showed positive response; orders above expectations and no recession signs seen.
Management said there is no dampness in demand so far; OEM business running at over INR5 crores per month and aftermarket doing well.

FY26 H2 revenue flat versus H1 on the base business; management attributed this to US customers running down inventory after the 25% tariff, with inventory rationalisation still ongoing while new orders came in.
Freight cost rose only slightly despite West Asia conflict; shipments on time; dollar realisations better per management.
TAFE blade order: initial share of about INR15 lakh per month, potential to reach 70-80% of its INR35-50 lakh monthly requirement.

New business of INR10-12 crores with PPAP samples submitted, commercial production expected Q3 FY27; another US bid order close to INR10 crores annually; long-term drivetrain order worth about INR10.5 crores per year.

qa_highlights.question: What was the final FY26 revenue from the large export order, and does it explain the margin hit?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR5.5-6 crores, all in March 2026. Management said the H2 employee cost increase (~INR6 crores to ~INR8 crores) was 90-100% due to this order's hires, with some senior hires for future expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Why is base business flat in H2 and what is the outlook excluding the export order?
qa_highlights.answer: Customers reduced inventory after 25% US tariffs hit their cash flows. Management said orders have since picked up more than expected and there is no visible slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: What gives visibility to scale agri from about INR4 crores per half to INR30 crores in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited full-season sales through Diwali, TAFE approvals and consistent ordering, distributor orders in Maharashtra, Karnataka and MP, and talks with large OEMs on blades and contract manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR500 crore order book is executable in FY27-28, and why is FY27 base growth absent from guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crores per annum, spread over eight years. Management said guidance was kept conservative; the INR60 crore export increment is the only increase in the automotive FY27 figure over FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What is working capital funding need and will equity be diluted?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank working capital is already sanctioned; US export transit is about two months and credit up to six months. Management said no equity dilution is needed and it is looking at factoring.

qa_highlights.question: Is there margin pressure from OEM business or input-cost headwinds (crude, war)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it targets niche parts with no pricing pressure, sees no margin dampness, and freight increase has been minor. Margin drag was attributed to manpower cost for the new project.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the group company merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the entity is a group company, not a subsidiary, and merger work is ongoing with a possible announcement in the coming months.

Agri target of INR30 crores (vs ~INR8 crores in FY26) rests on TAFE scaling and on OEM talks that management would not detail; seasonality limits sales to about Diwali.
Working capital is elevated and rising with US export receivables; funding relies on bank lines and possible factoring.

Customer inventory rationalisation is still ongoing per management; watch H1 FY27 order flow.
Pending merger of the group company; no timeline or terms given. Hydraulic pump division has no disclosed numbers yet.

544167|2026-03.headline: JNK India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 69.2% YoY to Rs 344.6 crore, with EBITDA margin at 15.2%; FY27 revenue growth guided at 25-30%.
544167|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 344.6 crore (+69.2% YoY), with EBITDA of Rs 52.3 crore (+89.9%) at a 15.2% margin and PAT of Rs 33 crore (+149.5%). FY26 revenue reached Rs 838 crore (+68%), PAT Rs 64.8 crore (+114.6%), and the order book ended the year at Rs 1,961.4 crore after Rs 1,694.4 crore of FY26 inflows. Management attributed margin expansion mainly to project mix (legacy orders completed in Q1-Q2) and guided 14-15% EBITDA margin as sustainable. Management guided FY27 revenue growth of 25-30%, with Dangote refinery and fertilizer reformer awards as key near-term catalysts.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 order inflow / order book (31 Mar 2026)

segments.commentary: Contributed 72.7% of FY26 revenue and about 94% of order book value.

segments.name: Process plant
segments.commentary: Contributed 17.4% of FY26 revenue and 3.5% of order book.

segments.name: Special fabricated equipment
segments.commentary: Contributed 3.1% of FY26 revenue and 1.3% of order book; described as a new segment.

segments.name: Flares, incinerators and others
segments.commentary: Contributed 6.3% of FY26 revenue and about 1.2% of order book.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at around 25-30% YoY, implying roughly Rs 1,050-1,090 crore on the FY26 base; management also called 25-30% feasible for FY28.
EBITDA margin expected in the 14-15% range going forward, based on Q3 and Q4 FY26 run-rate, with conservatism due to commodity price risk.
Revenue phasing: Q1 expected to be lowest, Q4 highest; H2 expected at roughly 40-60% of FY27 revenue.
Order book expected to cross about Rs 2,000 crore by end of FY27.
Operating cash flow expected to remain positive in FY27, though not on a large scale.
Dangote refinery fired heater award expected in Q1 FY27 and reformer award in Q2 or Q3 FY27; fertilizer reformer bid submission in Q1 with finalisation in Q2 or Q3.
Waste gas handling package at export expected to close within one to two weeks; clean aviation fuel bid lost (not lowest bidder).
Chemdist expected to add 10-15% of group revenue in the first couple of years.
capex_capacity: No major capex planned; management said FY27 growth needs little capex.
Planned smaller domestic facility for critical fabrication and storage, capex about Rs 10-15 crore; current facility is mainly export-oriented.
About 120 in-house engineers; fabrication outsourced to approved shops near sites, specialised bought-out items sourced from approved Indian suppliers.
Capacity constrained by manpower in engineering, procurement and project management, and by working capital; management said no meaningful capacity utilisation metric exists.
Current order book expected to be executed over roughly two years.
demand_pricing: Order book Rs 1,961.4 crore: 97.5% India, 2.5% international; JV (Chemdist) about Rs 67-70 crore, JNK India about Rs 1,890 crore, legacy about Rs 40-50 crore.
Bid pipeline about Rs 4,000 crore: about Rs 1,500 crore on JNK India alone and Rs 2,500-3,000 crore alongside JNK Global; conversion rate 25-30%, targeting Rs 1,300-1,500 crore inflows.

Dangote Phase 2 refinery: both inquiries received and JNK prequalified for fired heaters and reformers (and flares); competitors include other European players and Chinese bidders; combined bid with JNK Global as main bidder.
Export opportunities of about Rs 4,000 crore in Africa, Middle East and Russia; Middle East fertilizer/petchem opportunity of $200-300 million over two to three years.
Domestic refinery/petchem projects (BPCL Andhra, IOCL Paradip, Haldia) expected to take six months to a year due to crude pricing pressures; cracking furnace order opportunity likely in FY28.
Commodity pricing: generally no pass-through clauses except limited PSU contracts; procurement placed within one to two months of contract award.
Royalty: technical fee up to 2% of order value on exports booked in JNK India's name for items common with JNK Global.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion was project mix, and what is the normalised EBITDA run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA was about 7% in Q1, 12% in Q2, 14% in Q3 and above 15% in Q4 due to legacy project completion and new projects on input accounting; 14-15% is the normal range.

qa_highlights.question: Has EIL issued RFQs for Dangote Phase 2, and is JNK prequalified?
qa_highlights.answer: Both inquiries received and prequalified for fired heaters and reformers, plus flares; fired heater award expected Q1 FY27, reformer Q2 or Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operating cash flow is already positive, though modest; improvement driven by private and export customers with better down payments versus PSU orders.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative and how long does unbilled revenue take to convert?
qa_highlights.answer: Unbilled revenue mainly from new cracker furnace and process plant projects with private customers; expected to convert to cash in about three months.

qa_highlights.question: Can execution capacity support Rs 2,000-2,500 crore annual revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth needs balancing capability, handling and working capital; 25-30% annual growth appears feasible, with capacity built year on year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chemdist green hydrogen technology and pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Technology produces hydrogen as a by-product from green ethanol to ethyl acetate using a special catalyst; first project from Hydrogen Valley Pune, Rs 70 crore backlog; commercial-scale proof targeted next year. Standalone solar EPC not planned.

risks_watch: Commodity price volatility and geopolitical disruption to imports and exports; limited pass-through clauses on contracts.
Operating cash flow still negative in the last three years; working capital needs rising with project scale.
Revenue concentration: about 97.5% of order book is domestic and about Rs 1,600 crore of the order book is linked to BPCL Bina via JNK Global.
Dangote and reformer award timing (Q1-Q3 FY27) and competition from European and other bidders; clean aviation fuel bid lost.
Heavy H2 weighting (about 65% of FY26 revenue) and Q1 seasonality.
Chemdist technology not yet commercially proven; margin uplift from JV deferred by a couple of years.

So, considering all this, we feel the EBITDA margin of 14% to 15% is more sustainable.
Generally, we do not have the clauses to pass it on to the customer.

rows.why: No new productive capacity is commissioned; execution is constrained by engineering manpower (about 120 in-house engineers) and working capital, and only a Rs 10-15 crore smaller domestic facility is planned with no timeline.

rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of 25-30% (about Rs 1,050-1,090 crore on Rs 838 crore FY26), backed by a Rs 1,961.4 crore order book, with about Rs 1,890 crore on JNK India.

rows.why: Management says FY27 growth needs little capex and no utilisation metric exists; only a Rs 10-15 crore domestic facility is planned, so a major capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.why: Dangote heater award (Q1 FY27) and reformer award (Q2 or Q3 FY27) could lift order inflows toward the Rs 1,300-1,500 crore target, but management guides conservatively on margins and domestic refinery timelines.

rows.why: Domestic refinery/petchem projects (BPCL Andhra, IOCL Paradip, Haldia) are delayed six months to a year by crude pricing pressure, and clean aviation fuel bid was lost, with H2 carrying 40-60% of FY27 revenue.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Chemdist green hydrogen technology is not commercially proven; commercial-scale proof targeted next year, and cracking furnace opportunity is likely in FY28, with Chemdist adding 10-15% of group revenue in the first couple of years.

rows.label: Dangote Phase 2 refinery awards
rows.why: JNK is prequalified for fired heaters, reformers and flares, with a combined bid with JNK Global as main bidder against European and Chinese competitors, and the Rs 4,000 crore bid pipeline converts at 25-30%.

rows.label: Operating cash flow positive but modest
rows.why: Management says operating cash flow is already positive, but it was negative for three years, and unbilled revenue from cracker furnace and process plant projects is expected to convert in about three months.

rows.why: Export opportunities of about Rs 4,000 crore in Africa, Middle East and Russia and a $200-300 million Middle East fertilizer/petchem opportunity over two to three years, while the waste gas export package is expected to close within one to two weeks.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 25-30% FY27 growth outlook and near-term Dangote awards, but cautious on margins, crude-linked refinery timelines and commodity exposure; analysts pushed on H1/H2 split, cracking furnace timing and execution capacity.

544167|2026-06.headline: JNK India Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 80.6% YoY to INR 186 crore; EBITDA margin 11.8% after Chemdist losses, PAT up 8.5x to INR 9.6 crore.
544167|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 80.6% YoY to INR 186 crore and EBITDA rose 3.1x to INR 21.9 crore, with margin at 11.8% versus 7% a year earlier. Standalone EBITDA margin was 14%, with the gap explained by an operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore at the JNK Chemdist JV. Order book stood at INR 1,801 crore as of 30 June 2026, and FY27 guidance of 20-25% revenue growth and 12-14% EBITDA margin was reiterated. An export order received on 8 June 2026 was cancelled before any costs were incurred, due to licensor technical approval not materialising.

segments.name: Heating equipment (core)
segments.commentary: About 60% of the current opportunity pipeline; management targets heating at about 60% of revenue in the medium term. Export bids (about INR 3,000 crore) are mainly heating, largely routed through JNK Global.

segments.name: Non-heating / adjacencies (process plants, metals & minerals, offshore, renewables)
segments.commentary: About 40% of pipeline, with domestic bids of INR 3,000-plus crore. Target is about 40% of revenue from non-heating within 3-5 years; hit rate expected 10-12% initially versus 20-25% in heating.

segments.name: JNK Chemdist Technologies (JV)
segments.commentary: Contributed 8.8% of group revenue in Q1 FY27 with an operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore on high fixed costs. Guided to 10-15% of JNK India revenue and about 20% gross margin; expected to turn profitable by year-end. Current green hydrogen orders about INR 50 crore.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth guidance of about 20-25% for FY27 maintained.
Full-year EBITDA margin guidance of about 12-14% maintained; management said there is no change, though the company later said it would recheck the figures it had announced.
Pipeline of more than INR 6,000 crore (about 50:50 export and domestic); management expects these bids to be finalised in FY27 with a hit rate of 20-25% in heating.
Refinery and fertiliser order finalisation expected in Q2-Q3 FY27.
BPCL Bina execution to occur uniformly in FY27 and FY28; EBITDA in line with guidance.
Chemdist expected to be EBITDA-positive by year-end FY27 (full year, not a specific quarter).
capex_capacity: Unbilled revenue at end-Q1 about INR 200-221 crore following shift to input-method revenue recognition.
Company has board approval to register a branch office in Iraq; no physical setup yet and an agent is in place.
Non-fund-based (bank guarantee) limit enhancement may be needed for new contracts; no significant debt raising expected in the next 4-6 quarters, per management.
Revenue seasonality: Q1 is 10-15% of full-year revenue, H1 30-35%, H2 60-70%.
demand_pricing: Order book INR 1,801 crore at 30 June 2026; pipeline above INR 6,000 crore, up from about INR 4,000 crore previously.
Export pipeline about INR 3,000 crore, mainly Africa (Nigeria, Ethiopia) and Middle East; Dangote Phase 2 under discussion, described as a likely repeat order.
Non-heating TAM in India cited as USD 300-500 million (offshore) and USD 500 million-1 billion (metals and minerals); target project size USD 30-60 million, up to about INR 1,000-2,000 crore.
Commodity prices fluctuating; management said ongoing projects are costed and sub-vendor orders placed on fixed-price basis, so no major margin impact.
Working capital: large customers (Reliance, private companies, BPCL Bina) have friendly payment terms; JNK Global bank guarantees on back-to-back export orders.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term revenue target beyond FY27 and capacity to ramp non-heating business?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth of 20-25% annually; non-heating to reach about 40% of revenue in 3-5 years. Management said diversification will not ramp within 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export order cancelled and what has been done to prevent recurrence?
qa_highlights.answer: Cancelled due to end-user licensor technical approval not materialising; EPC contractor was confident, and no costs had been incurred. The licensor has since qualified JNK for future projects but not ongoing ones. SOPs being tightened.

qa_highlights.question: Margin decline in Q1 despite gross margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly Chemdist operating loss of about INR 3.6 crore; standalone EBITDA margin was 14% on lower Q1 revenue of about INR 170 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Hit rate and TAM in new non-heating segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Expected hit rate of about 10-12% initially versus 20-25% in heating; target bids of USD 30-60 million, and EBITDA margin in line with 12-14% guidance.

qa_highlights.question: JNK Global cooperation agreement renewal (3-year term in DRHP)?
qa_highlights.answer: Not formally renewed yet; management believes it is in force or continues automatically, with no change in terms.

qa_highlights.question: Unbilled revenue and accounting change?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue recognition moved from output to input method; unbilled revenue about INR 200-221 crore at end Q1. Management said working capital cycle is unchanged as customer payment schedules are unchanged.

risks_watch: Export order cancellation (8 June 2026 order) shows licensor approval risk on international EPC contracts.
Chemdist JV losses until break-even; management expects year-end profitability but gave no quarterly guidance.

Unclear reconciliation of EBITDA guidance (12-14% now vs 14-15% previously cited by an analyst) and corrections to the presentation, including a revised filing for standalone profit-after-tax margin rows.
Lower hit rate and new technology qualification risk in non-heating businesses; reliance on technology partners.
Governance: activist dispute at JNK Global (sub judice) and status of the JNK Global cooperation agreement, which is not formally renewed.
Revenue seasonality and back-ended recognition; unbilled revenue of about INR 200 crore to watch.
Bank guarantee limit enhancement may be needed for new contracts; Dangote Phase 2 award pending.

544172|2026-03.headline: Indegene Q4 FY26 revenue crossed ₹1,000 crore for the first time (+32.8% YoY); FY26 revenue ₹35,105 million, up 23.6% in INR.
544172|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the first quarter above ₹1,000 crore revenue, up 6.5% QoQ and 32.8% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA rose 23.2% YoY to ₹1,889 million, but after a ₹241 million forward-contract hedge charge the reported EBITDA was ₹1,648 million. Reported Q4 PAT was ₹797 million after a ₹203 million one-time provision for a 2020 US TCPA class action; management says adjusted PAT grew 12.7% YoY for FY26. Management declined to give formal revenue guidance but said the pipeline is larger and better qualified than at any prior year end.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the moat is domain expertise plus proprietary data, with multiple frontier models and specialist AI partners orchestrated together. qa_highlights.answer: Cortex is a knowledge engineering platform for building agentic workflows for life sciences with enterprise security. It sits on frontier models plus specialist AI such as computer vision and large action models, with the domain layer decoupled from the technology layer.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 growth drivers and what would be different?

544172|2026-09.headline: Indegene Q2 FY27 revenue rose 39.5% YoY to INR11,223 million, with EBITDA margin at 16.7% and a 19%+ target for Q4.
544172|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR11,223 million, up 39.5% YoY and 5.6% QoQ in INR, the fifth straight quarter of more than 5% QoQ INR growth. EBITDA was INR1,873 million at a 16.7% margin, absorbing about 150 bps from the annual wage hike, which productivity and favourable exchange rates largely offset. PAT rose 10% YoY to INR1,123 million, though a sharp fall in interest income (down 44% QoQ) weighed below EBITDA. Management reiterated a quarterly EBITDA margin of 19%+ by Q4 and said H2 would be stronger than H1, while the largest client dipped slightly and the $10 million outcome-based contract is expected to peak in Q4.

financial_highlights.change: +39.5% YoY, +5.6% QoQ in INR; +27.5% YoY and +4.4% QoQ in USD

Organic growth for FY27 expected to be better than FY26; management says FY27 will be organically stronger than last year and H2 stronger than H1.
Wage hike is fully in the base; productivity, workforce transformation and operating leverage expected to add to EBITDA in Q3 and more in Q4.

Amortisation charge to decline from Q3 onward; yields expected to rise with higher rates and a shift to held-to-maturity instruments. Together these add about 90-95 bps to PBT, helping PAT margin expand faster than EBITDA margin.

Tectonic run rate grew from about $1 million a quarter to $1.7 million this quarter; contracts now exceed $2 million a quarter.
Approximately 75% of the next two quarters' forex exposure is already hedged.
Dedicated tech partnership team in the US and India to work with frontier model and other technology companies.
demand_pricing: Q2 deal wins: 9 deals with ACV around $1 million or more, including one $5 million-plus win (expansion of the top-5 client's content migration outside the US), one $3-5 million global content factory win with a top-20 pharma, and one win with a top-30 pharma replacing an incumbent.
Four further deals in the $1-3 million range, split evenly between Enterprise Commercial and Enterprise Medical; Tectonic extended to Canada, the first market outside Europe.
Top 5 accounts grew 9.2% QoQ in INR; top 20 grew about 6.7% QoQ. Active clients 107 (31 more YoY); clients above $1 million rose to 59 from 54; clients above $10 million at 13.

Most Q2 wins were output- or outcome-based rather than FTE-based. The company is converting FTE contracts to hybrid contracts at renewal.
A $10 million ACV outcome-based contract (calendar-year threshold) recognised only a small amount in Q2; the bulk is expected in H2, with a true-up in Q4 after customer confirmation in Feb/Mar.
BioPharm: cost synergies of about $1.5 million a year reinvested in expanding BioPharm's go-to-market team from 3 to 9. Transition services closed by end-February, ahead of the March target.
Management sees competition from agencies and CROs, not IT services firms, in the deals it pursues.

544174|2026-03.headline: TBO Tek Q4 FY26 grew YoY on top and bottom line despite Middle East war; Q1 FY27 guided better than Q4 and last year, with no figures given.
544174|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 showed YoY growth in revenue and profit despite the war that began at end-February 2026, which hit the Middle East and Israel, TBO's largest source markets. January and February showed strong operating leverage, margin expansion and EBITDA growth YoY, but March was a washout and erased the quarter-level leverage. Management expects Q1 FY27 to beat Q4 and last year on both GTV and gross profit, while declining to quantify it. Cash flow from operations was negative in FY26, which management attributed mainly to timing items (Brazil anticipation discontinuation, war-related receivable delays, PLB payouts and deposits classified as working capital) and expects reversion to over 100% cash conversion by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any reason for Q4's strong hotels and ancillary growth despite geopolitical shocks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to market-development investment starting January 2025, with new travel agents becoming productive after 6-9 months; some large partners went live in Q4. Majority of growth is market share gain.

qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were PLB payouts (Jan-Dec for hotels, April-March for air), delayed Middle East collections around Eid, bank deposits over 12 months classified in working capital, and Brazil anticipation reversal; expected to normalise by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How is management handling competitive pressure on take rates?
qa_highlights.answer: No downward pressure today; management intends to hold take rates at current levels and not raise them, as TBO operates an aggregation model.

qa_highlights.answer: Full-year YoY FX impact estimated at 4-5%, primarily on hotel GTV. Management will consider constant-currency reporting after an analyst suggestion.

544174|2026-06.headline: TBO TEK Q1 FY27: EBITDA-to-GTV of 1.3% and operating leverage shown despite Middle East disruption; 24% Europe growth, 15% organic CC growth.
544174|2026-06.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 (quarter ended June 30, 2026) as the toughest in two years due to Middle East-driven travel disruption, yet reported top-line and bottom-line growth. Europe grew 24% YoY and Middle East was flat (1% CC growth), with Classic Vacations (acquired about six months ago) adding North America scale. EBITDA margins expanded faster than gross profit, which management cited as evidence of operating leverage. Management began reporting constant-currency numbers because a roughly 11% INR-vs-CC gap in hotel GTV distorted YoY growth. Management declined to give a timeline for Middle East normalisation or a long-term margin target.

rows.label: Classic Vacations platform integration and cross-sell

rows.why: Integration hiring largely complete and enterprise CRM being implemented, but reverse cross-sell has not started and standalone enterprise growth is a few quarters away.

rows.label: Disclosure: GTV split and constant-currency reporting
rows.why: Retail vs B2B/API split is about 50-50 with management only committing to review API disclosure, and CC reporting continues directionally against an 11% INR gap in hotel GTV.

rows.label: Take rate pressure from share competition
rows.why: Take rate was slightly lower in Q1 as regions competed for share, the organic hotels GP/GTV fell 30 bps, and management said it will selectively accept lower margins to win business, though it expects bigger players to gain share as smaller ones attrite.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating leverage (EBITDA-to-GP about 26%, Europe +24%, organic CC growth 15%) but declined to forecast Middle East normalisation, a long-term margin target or EBITDA-to-GTV; analysts pressed on sustainability of the 1.3% EBITDA-to-GTV, the 30 bps drop in hotels GP/GTV,

544174|2026-09.headline: TBO TEK Q2 FY27: GTV up 16% while adjusted EBITDA rose 27%, but management expects a tough Q3 with Middle East and Europe disruption.
544174|2026-09.overview: Management reported 16% GTV growth and 27% adjusted EBITDA growth for Q2 FY27, its second consecutive quarter of operating leverage. Middle East grew 10% in constant currency and Europe and APAC grew over 30%, despite conflict and October disruptions in Saudi Arabia and European cities. Management said Q3 will be tough and is aiming only for year-on-year growth in top line and bottom line, with the U.S. elections seen as an inflection point. Classic Vacations (acquired about a year ago) is expected to weigh on reported growth, and a Rs. 8.1 crore fraud loss in the UAE subsidiary was flagged as exceptional.

segments.name: Middle East
segments.commentary: Most impacted market due to conflict; grew 10% in constant currency (about 20% reported), still below prior-year baseline; management believes it is gaining share.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: Now the largest source market, growing about 36% and about 36% of total GTV; newer markets such as Germany and Eastern Europe grew triple digits on small bases, while UK and Ireland grew on a much larger base.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: Grew north of 30% in the quarter, per management.

segments.name: Classic Vacations (North America)
segments.commentary: Acquired about one year ago; about 20 sales hires added, with about half under six months tenure. Management expects it to be a drag on reported growth near term; TBO sales into Classic rose to about 8% of Classic GTV from about 5% last quarter.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Monthly transacting buyers grew 1% in the quarter and 4% in H1 across about 24,000 quarterly active agents; management is pushing non-air business, which has higher profitability.

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Management expects hotel GP margins in Q2 levels to hold if conditions stay stable, but may need to change stance if supply rises and demand falls.

guidance_outlook: Q3 expected to be tough; internal aim is year-on-year growth in both top line and bottom line, with constant-currency growth hoped for and currency benefit additional.
Operating leverage expected to hold over the next two to eight quarters if SG&A growth stays below GP growth; trailing 12-month margin suggested as the better guide given seasonality.
No incremental investment needed for operating leverage; upside in GP expected to flow to bottom line.
Classic Vacations expected to show better results over next two to three quarters, with demonstrable results likely by next summer season (Q2 FY28) if macro clears.
Organic air GP take rate guided to range between 1% and 1.2%.
Classic Vacations beta launch of TBO platform for Classic in late November, followed by gradual rollout over several months.
Market development investments to stay unchanged for the rest of FY27; FY28 budget planning to begin in a few weeks.
Working capital release expected to continue positively through end of calendar year.
capex_capacity: Classic Vacations: sales team expanded by about 20 hires; US sales org previously ran with 10-12 staff covering about 10,000 travel advisors, now being scaled up.
Classic: CRM implemented for back-office processes; TBO supply tech integration into Classic completed; TBO platform for Classic in progress.
Supply organisation integrated: Americas and Europe supply teams for TBO and Classic now under common heads.
Pause on new market development for now; AI and automation investment continues in sales and operations tools.
Post-quarter, insurance claim initiated for the UAE fraud loss; additional oversight and automation of processes planned.
demand_pricing: Demand pressure intensified in October after attacks on Saudi airports hit Saudi inbound and outbound travel, with prior bookings cancelled; rioting in European cities (Paris, Madrid, Barcelona, Italy) raised cancellations.
Management is prioritising market share gains via agent penetration, and focusing on dollar revenue stability and high-value transactions over volume.
Organic air take rate fell to about 2% from about 2.3-2.4%, mainly lower airline incentives and lower refund income; management said more than 50% of the impact was passed to travel agents.
Hotel and air GP margins held; organic gross profit margin held at 5.5-5.6% despite lower take rate due to supplier mix (commission vs net models).
Business mix between API and B2A (smaller agents) remained about 50:50; B2A GP margin slightly higher than API.

Management views AI-driven B2C/OTA entry into agency as a threat but limited, citing credit-line knowledge and channel conflict with suppliers; sees complex, high-value itineraries as the defensible segment.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand holding up given elevated international airfares and geopolitical risk, especially at the premium end?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed pressure that intensified in October due to Saudi airport attacks and European rioting; the company is focusing on share gains and dollar revenue stability.

qa_highlights.question: Will H2 be lower than H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to forecast H2 precisely; internal aim is year-on-year growth in top line and bottom line for Q3, with U.S. elections seen as an inflection point.

qa_highlights.question: Will Classic be a drag on overall growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman-level answer: mathematically yes near term, since Classic is not yet growing near 30%; but Classic GP is about double organic GP per dollar of GTV, and its revenue reflects bookings made about a year earlier for groups.

qa_highlights.question: Classic integration milestones and timing of acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales team ramp and CRM are largely complete; TBO platform beta for Classic due late November, with gradual rollout over several months; results expected within the next couple of quarters, without a firm number.

qa_highlights.question: Rs. 8 crore fraud: what happened and what are the implications for the FEMA penalty?
qa_highlights.answer: Suspected employee collusion led to unauthorised bookings in a government travel agency account in the UAE subsidiary; police complaints filed in India and UAE, insurance claim initiated. FEMA adjudication order received after quarter-end; company will appeal and has not provided, citing high chances of winning.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the air take rate fall and is there reversal potential?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower incentives and refund income in H1; management expects GP to remain in a 1-1.2% range, with occasional quarterly dips and ad hoc airline incentives.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in FX loss and the working capital release?
qa_highlights.answer: FX loss reflects hedging premium costs plus losses on unhedged exposure (about 25% unhedged) versus last year's gain; working capital release reflected reversal of Middle East overdues and Brazil timing items, plus new credit lines replacing virtual cards, with positive impact expected through year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q3 Classic GTV seasonally weaker than Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is the weakest quarter for Classic because it books on check-in basis, so Q3 should be better than Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Hotel GP margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to maintain Q2-like hotel margins if conditions stay the same, but may adjust if supply rises and demand falls.

risks_watch: Q3 FY27 visibility is low: Saudi conflict, European rioting, Israeli election outcome and U.S. midterms; prior bookings can reverse on disruptions.
Classic Vacations integration: booking-to-check-in accounting means lumpy revenue; sales ramp and tech rollout timing unclear, and management gave no quantified synergy target.
Take rate compression in air (about 2% vs 2.3-2.5%) and dependence on airline incentives.
FEMA adjudication order received; appeal pending with no provision booked; worst-case outcome not quantified by management.
Fraud investigation at UAE subsidiary ongoing; agency involvement unknown; insurance recovery uncertain.
AI-driven B2C OTA entry into agency business and AI assistants (e.g., Meta and Instinct) as channel disruption risk; management says no imminent threat.
FX loss and hedging cost volatility (hedging about 75% of open exposure).
544174|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on long-term thesis, Classic and operating leverage, but cautious and evasive on Q3 and H2 outlook, declining to give numbers on currency-adjusted growth, Classic synergies or budget plans.

financial_highlights.metric: Organic air GP as % of GTV

financial_highlights.value: Rs. 8.1 crore (estimated net loss Rs. 8 crore)
about Rs. 9 crore this quarter vs Rs. 5.5 crore previous quarter
financial_highlights.change: Hedging cost and unhedged exposure losses

financial_highlights.value: up 1% in quarter; up 4% in H1

key_quotes: We do expect a tough Q3 because several headwinds in the industry right now.
Internally, what we are aiming for is that just still manage to deliver year-on-year growth both on top line and bottom line.
The investment thesis remains strong on Classic.
We do not see an imminent threat on our business right now, but we also acknowledge that travel is going to get impacted, and it may create some opportunities and maybe some threats as well.
Yes, it is the right interpretation, but we also need to take into account that on organic business, basically we account for basis the bookings made per se.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Adjusted EBITDA grew 27% vs GTV up 16% with constant-currency SG&A growing high single digits, and management expects operating leverage to hold for 2-8 quarters if SG&A growth stays below GP growth; organic GP margin held at 5.5-5.6% but air take rate fell to about 2% from 2.3-2.4%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Classic Vacations sales team added about 20 hires (half under six months tenure) and TBO platform beta due late November with gradual rollout over several months; no physical capacity or plant capex discussed, and market development investments held flat for rest of FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 GTV grew 16% with Europe and APAC over 30% and Middle East 10% constant currency, but India monthly transacting buyers grew only 1% in the quarter and October disruptions in Saudi and Europe hit bookings; Q3 aim is only YoY growth, with no numeric guide.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the brief reports no utilisation figure and no new plant or land plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to forecast H2 precisely and only aims for YoY growth in Q3 on top and bottom line, with October disruptions in Saudi and Europe already hitting bookings.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management called Q3 tough with low visibility from Saudi conflict, European rioting and prior-booking cancellations; the Q3 aim is only YoY growth, and a rise in cancellations could push it below that.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: TBO platform beta for Classic Vacations is due late November, followed by gradual rollout over several months, with demonstrable Classic results targeted by summer season Q2 FY28 if macro clears.

rows.label: Classic Vacations results acceleration
rows.why: Management expects Classic to show better results over the next two to three quarters, with demonstrable results likely by summer Q2 FY28 if macro clears, but gave no firm number and Classic is not yet growing near 30%, so it remains a drag on reported growth near term.

rows.label: FEMA adjudication penalty outcome (UAE fraud)
rows.why: A FEMA adjudication order was received after quarter-end with no provision booked; the company will appeal, and the worst-case outcome is not quantified, while the Rs. 8 crore UAE fraud loss has an insurance claim initiated.

rows.label: Air take rate recovery
rows.why: Organic air take rate fell to about 2% from 2.3-2.4% on lower airline incentives and refunds; management guides air GP to 1-1.2% and expects only occasional quarterly dips, so no clear reversal.

tone.note: Management was confident on operating leverage, Classic's long-term thesis and the Europe/APAC growth, but cautious and evasive on Q3 and H2, declining to quantify currency-adjusted growth, Classic synergies or FY28 budget; analysts pressed on the Q3 outlook, Classic drag, demand at the premium end

544176|2026-03.headline: Aadhar Housing Q4 FY26: AUM crossed INR30,571 crore (+20% YoY), FY26 PAT INR1,096 crore (+20%), GNPA eased to 1.08%.
544176|2026-03.overview: Aadhar closed FY26 with AUM of INR30,571 crore, up 20% YoY, and record Q4 disbursements of INR3,087 crore (+20% YoY). FY26 disbursements were INR9,556 crore (+17%) and PAT was INR1,096 crore (+20%), or INR1,108 crore before the one-time Labour Code charge. GNPA was 1.08%, down 30 bps QoQ but up slightly from 1.05% a year earlier, with 1+ DPD improving 78-80 bps QoQ. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of about 20% AUM growth, about 20% profit growth and 17-18% disbursement growth, with spreads expected to contract 8-10 bps.

financial_highlights.change: -30 bps QoQ; vs 1.05% in Q4 FY25

financial_highlights.metric: Exit cost of funds / exit spread

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: 73% of AUM; home loan disbursements grew about 26% YoY in Q4, helped by PMAY subsidies (about INR50 crore to about 15,000-16,000 customers) and a push on emerging markets.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP / non-housing)
segments.commentary: 27% of AUM; LAP disbursement mix was about 24-25% in Q4 versus 28-29% typical, deliberately held back since the tariff shock. Management is open to lifting it to 27-28% of disbursements, but not in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Emerging and urban geographies
segments.commentary: Average ticket about INR10.9 lakh on the book. Emerging C is about INR8.5-8.6 lakh, emerging B INR10 lakh, emerging A INR12 lakh, urban INR17-18 lakh. Urban traction is 'encouraging' per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: about 20% AUM growth, about 20% profit growth, and 17-18% disbursement growth.
Spreads expected to contract by about 8-10 bps YoY, given incremental yields of about 13% against a book yield of about 13.52%; partly offset by LAP mix and self-employed shift.
Cost-to-income ratio expected to fall by about 50 bps in FY27, driven by productivity and AI-led sales tools.
Cost of funds expected to hold broadly flat for the next 2-3 quarters; management would be 'very happy' to hold the 7.7% exit rate through FY27.
Direct assignment (DA) volume expected to grow 10-15% in FY27 from about INR1,725 crore in FY26.
Long-term AUM milestone of INR50,000 crore targeted in about 3 years.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 626 across 22 states and more than 550 districts, after 5 branches added in Q4 and 46 in FY26.
Four branch categories: ultra micro (50-60 sq ft), micro, small and main. Small branches take 9-12 months to turn productive and urban branches 12-15 months.
Undrawn sanctions of INR1,687 crore, of which INR246 crore from NHB.
Liquidity of INR1,425 crore at end-Q4 FY26.
Employees: on-roll about 5,400-5,430 and off-roll about 3,900-3,965 at March 2026, versus 4,600 on-roll and 4,300 off-roll a year earlier.
Management expects Uttar Pradesh to be the largest contributor to growth; West Bengal flagged as a potential new state.
demand_pricing: Demand described as end-user driven, with first-time homebuyers prominent. Competition from banks is elevated in urban markets but steady in low-income segments.
Management cited state-level BLC and AHP pipelines (for example, 25,000+ units in Odisha) as supporting demand.
Bounce rates stable for six quarters and unaffected by West Asia conflict; collections team of about 2,000 briefed to be careful.
Low-income segment: management says about 18% share of the low-income HFC peer group, up from 16-17%.
Borrowing mix at March 2026: banks 51%, NHB 22%, NCD 19%, ECB 5%, others 4%. 76% of borrowings are floating; 73-74% of assets are floating.
NCDs are 22% of borrowings, of which 68% are fixed. NHB funding is roughly 50% fixed and 50% floating.

qa_highlights.question: Why has LAP growth lagged, and what is the outlook for other income and ESOP cost?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP slowdown was deliberate since the tariff shock; LAP is 27% of AUM and LAP mix in Q4 was about 26%. Assignment income reflected spreads 80-85 bps better, not larger volumes. About INR6-7 crore of Q4 fee income was one-time. ESOP charge of INR13.5 crore is a Q4 item.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for yields and spreads in FY27 given the rate environment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects a 2-3 quarter rate hold. Spread contraction of 8-10 bps is guided at the current 25-26% LAP mix. Each 5 percentage points shifted from HL to LAP adds about 400 bps on that portion.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 1+ DPD improvement and the sequential jump in disbursements?
qa_highlights.answer: 1+ DPD fell about 80 bps (not risen, as the analyst framed it) over 18 months of focus on collections. Sequential disbursement strength came from Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Delhi, Karnataka and Uttarakhand. Incremental borrowing cost rose about 10 bps QoQ because bank drawdowns were deferred into Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why did opex-to-AUM rise sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 always carries sales contests and one-time incentive costs. Cost-to-income improved YoY from 37.9% to 37.1% in Q4. Full-year cost-to-income was 35.9%, down from 36.4%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ticket size trends and the sources of the home loan growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental ticket size ranged INR12.5-13.5 lakh over recent quarters, against INR10.9 lakh on book. Management aims to hold book ticket size at INR10-11.5 lakh, and to hold non-home loans to about 70:30 with home loans over the medium term.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the funding book can still reprice, and how far has cost of funds fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Incremental cost fell from 8.4% to 7.6% YoY, with banks passing on 70-75 bps. Exit cost of funds moved from 8.14% to 7.72%, with 15 bps passed to customers. NCDs (22%) are mostly fixed, so the remaining repricing is limited to bank and floating NHB funds.

risks_watch: Geopolitical (West Asia) stress on borrowers; bounce rates and collections are the early indicators to watch.
Spread compression of 8-10 bps YoY if LAP mix stays at about 25-26%; cost of funds could rise given the 76% floating-rate liability book.
Competitive pressure from banks in urban markets.
Ticket size drift: management targets INR10-11.5 lakh, with construction-cost inflation expected to push it higher.
LAP usage is a lever to protect yields but is deferred; delinquency on LAP is about 0.7-0.75% higher on GNPA and must be watched when mix is raised.
Labour Code exceptional charge of INR16 crore taken in Q3; ESOP cost of INR13.5 crore in Q4 is a one-time item per management.
544176|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and execution, with guidance reiterated. Cautious and deliberate on LAP and rates, explicitly holding back on LAP and expecting a 2-3 quarter rate hold. Some answers were loose on numbers, with corrections made live (for example, 1+ DPD fell rather than rose).
key_quotes: On all the 3 critical parameters, we have stood by our guidance and commitment to the market.
We don't want to do something in haste, which will go out and look at our delinquency numbers.
Our view is that the interest rate cycle has stagnated and to a certain extent, will be stagnant for at least two, three quarters.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided spreads to contract 8-10 bps YoY in FY27 on incremental yields of about 13% vs book yield of 13.52%; cost-to-income down about 50 bps is the only offset, and cost of funds is expected flat for 2-3 quarters at a 7.7% exit rate.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Network at 626 branches after 46 added in FY26 (5 in Q4), undrawn sanctions of INR1,687 crore and state BLC/AHP pipelines support growth, but no forward branch count or capacity target was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guidance held at about 20% AUM growth and 17-18% disbursement growth after FY26 disbursements of INR9,556 crore (+17%) and Q4 record of INR3,087 crore (+20%).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% AUM, 20% profit and 17-18% disbursement growth without raising it, and expects spreads to contract 8-10 bps.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Spread compression of 8-10 bps YoY and 76% floating-rate borrowings expose margins if rates move, and West Asia stress is a watch item, though bounce rates were stable for six quarters and GNPA eased to 1.08%.

rows.label: LAP mix lift to 27-28% of disbursements
rows.why: LAP is 27% of AUM but only 24-25% of Q4 disbursements vs 28-29% typical; management is open to lifting it to 27-28% but not in Q1 FY27, and each 5 pp shift from HL to LAP adds about 400 bps on that portion.

rows.label: Direct assignment volume growth
rows.why: DA volume guided to grow 10-15% from about INR1,725 crore in FY26, with Q4 assignment income lifted by spreads 80-85 bps better rather than larger volumes.

rows.label: Cost-to-income down about 50 bps in FY27
rows.why: FY26 cost-to-income was 35.9% vs 36.4% in FY25 and management guides another 50 bps via productivity and AI-led sales tools, with on-roll staff down to about 5,400-5,430 from 4,600 a year ago.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, asset quality (GNPA 1.08%, collections above 99.8%) and reiterated FY27 guidance, but was deliberately cautious on LAP and expects a 2-3 quarter rate hold; analysts probed spreads, LAP mix, DPD trend and ticket size, and some answers were corrected live.

544176|2026-06.headline: Aadhar Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 19% YoY to INR282 crores on AUM of INR31,364 crores (+18%), with disbursements hit by a switch to cheque-clearance recognition.
544176|2026-06.overview: AUM reached INR31,364 crores, up 18% YoY, and exit spread held at 5.8% despite a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026. Disbursement was INR2,036 crores on the new cheque-clearance basis, against INR2,359 crores (+19% YoY) on the old cheque-handover basis, as the company moved recognition to clearance from Q1 FY27. Asset quality was stable YoY, with GNPA at 1.31% (down 3 bps) and Stage 2 at 3.3% (down 40 bps), though Q1 credit cost rose seasonally. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth and 17-18% disbursement growth, with the next three quarters targeted above 20%.

segments.name: Home loans
segments.commentary: 73% of AUM; non-home loans 27%. Incremental disbursement mix currently 76:24 home vs non-home, versus a historical 70:30.

segments.name: Non-home loans
segments.commentary: Disbursement growth slowed to about 22% in the quarter by the analyst's read; management called the slowdown a deliberate choice linked to the West Asia situation and the riskier profile of these loans.

segments.name: Emerging vs urban branches
segments.commentary: About 450 of 628 branches are in emerging locations. Emerging yields are 14-14.8% versus 11.5-12% in urban; average ticket size rose only from INR10.4 lakh to INR11 lakh.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance held: 20% AUM growth, 20% PAT growth, 17-18% disbursement growth for the full year.
Disbursement growth above 20% targeted for each of the next three quarters; management expects Q2 to close the Q1 shortfall, with Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more.
July 2026 disbursement close to INR900 crores, per management.
Spread floor of 5.5% reiterated; over 2-3 years spreads expected to end near 5.5%, ROA 4.3-4.4% steady state, and ROE around 17% in a couple of years.
Cost-to-income expected to fall 30-40 bps a year; cost-to-AUM about 6-7 bps a year.
Credit cost expected to settle at 23-25 bps for the full year, with GNPA targeted at about 1.1% at year end.
Branch openings of 45-50 planned for Q3; Q1 had only 2 openings versus a 40-50 annual pace.
capex_capacity: Network at 628 branches across 22 states and 550+ districts as of June 2026.
New branches target productivity within 9-15 months; Q1 opened only 2 branches, with 5-7 planned and pushed into July.
Capital adequacy of 42.9% Tier 1 gives room for growth; the IPO's INR1,000 crores primary raise is meant to fund growth for the next 3-4 years. No plan to return capital.
Operational-risk capital set aside at about 6-7% of capital; balance-sheet risk weight about 45%.
demand_pricing: Demand described as healthy and end-user, first-time-buyer driven, particularly in emerging markets; management reports no demand-side issues in urban locations.
Spreads held at 5.8% after a 15 bps RPLR cut in February 2026; management says it protects spreads over chasing yields.
Management expects 5-7% overlap with new affordable-segment entrants; Aadhar sits one notch below in low-income housing.
Incremental yields flat QoQ; management expects no decline if the urban/emerging mix moves toward 50:50.
NRI-linked exposure described as minimal; state-level rule caps any state at 15% of AUM, incremental disbursement or distribution.
Delhi's share rose slightly, a lower-yield state, yet yields held.

financial_highlights.change: includes ~INR14 crores quarterly ESOP cost; ~33-34% excluding it

qa_highlights.question: How is the company sustaining asset yields despite the 15 bps RPLR cut and competition, and is it due to pricing, mix, or segment changes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited the urban/emerging strategy (about 450 of 628 branches in emerging locations) and a ticket size that moved only from INR10.4 lakh to INR11 lakh. Delhi's share rose slightly though it is a lower-yield state, and yields still held. No major state-mix shift was reported.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to sustain 20% growth and the 5.5% spread floor amid new affordable-segment entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Book spread is about 5.8%. Management expects a 5-7% overlap with new entrants, since Aadhar sits one notch below them in low-income housing, and says the emerging tilt will keep spreads above 5.5%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the July disbursement number and how will the cheque-clearance change be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: July disbursement is close to INR900 crores. Management expects Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more, with Q2 substantially covering the Q1 shortfall as the carry-forward business is recognised over a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is the cheque-clearance change affecting interest income, and what drove the sequential employee cost increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Interest income is affected by only 2-3 days, which management called immaterial. Sequential employee cost rose on the annual increment of about 10-12%. Year-on-year, the 27% rise is mainly INR14-15 crores of quarterly ESOP cost; excluding it, employee cost growth is about 14-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 rise in GNPA and Stage 2 seasonal, and what is the full-year credit cost outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 credit cost is seasonally high at 40-45 bps for the last 2-3 years. Management expects the year to end with credit cost of 23-25 bps and GNPA near 1.1%. Q1 rose 25 bps versus a usual 30-35 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the liquidity buffer and cost-of-funds outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquidity was INR2,371 crores at quarter end, above 10% of borrowings, but management targets 7-8% intra-quarter and this rises at quarter end from drawdowns. Cost of funds moved little in Q1. Management sees no near-term impact from rate rises and says 75% of assets can be repriced.

risks_watch: Disbursement and PAT growth depend on Q2 catching up on the cheque-clearance shortfall; management targets Q2 growth of about 23-24% or more and above 20% for the next three quarters.
Non-home loan disbursement growth slowed to about 22%, and the home/non-home mix stood at 76:24 against a historical 70:30; management expects normalisation from Q3 once West Asia uncertainty eases.
Credit cost and GNPA: Q1 credit cost rose seasonally by 25 bps; the year-end GNPA target of about 1.1% and credit cost of 23-25 bps must hold.
Competitive pressure from affordable-segment entrants with a 5-7% overlap; spread floor of 5.5% and incremental yields flat QoQ.
Branch expansion slowed to 2 openings in Q1 against a 40-50 annual pace; 45-50 openings are planned for Q3 and 5-7 were pushed into July.
Cost of funds and interest-rate risk, with management expecting no imminent pass-through in the current or next quarter.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with fire profitability, citing better commission in fire and engineering and profit commission on earned premium. Crop: will bid directly in tenders this year, pending government scheme structure.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fairfax keep its stake after the reverse merger?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not spoken to Fairfax and said there is no news on the amalgamation timeline. Fairfax holds about 58%; going below 51% would trigger an open offer, and management does not expect a sale.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size of the new specialty commercial lines and what is the motor pricing outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialty lines could reach about INR1,000 crores of premium in 3-5 years. Motor market correction in April 2026 on price and commission; overall motor loss ratio to be held flat or lower YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did motor OD loss ratio rise and what is the retention and renewal data?
qa_highlights.answer: Management delayed corrective OD pricing to test retention and sold more SAOD in FY25. Motor retention fell to 89.6% from 95.9%. Renewal rates rose in private car across channels.

qa_highlights.question: How will EOM compliance be managed at company level and how does Indian acquisition cost compare internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said line-of-business mix explains the EOM gap and expects regulation to ease expense limits within 2-3 months. Management said Indian acquisition costs have risen over 20 years and cited RBI and Economic Survey commentary.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is the discounting benefit and will long-run Ind AS investment yield match IGAAP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discount-rate effect is stable unless rates move sharply; it moved to 7.09% from 6.9%. Management said investment decisions should be judged on ROE, not on mark-to-market, and that risk-based capital may favour companies with high equity allocation.

544179|2026-06.headline: Go Digit's Q1 FY27 GDPI fell 8% and loss ratio rose to 73.3%, with management choosing profitability over growth.

Motor own damage, mainly private car, drove the loss ratio up from 70.3% to 73.3%, and management said it had made the wrong call on the stand-alone OD renewals. On its internal KPI basis (NEP with DAC, excluding MTM and discounting), PAT was INR190 crore versus INR200 crore a year ago and combined ratio was 107.2%. Under Indian Accounting Standards (IFRS-style prescribed format), PAT rose to INR372 crore from INR325 crore, helped by unrealised gains and discounting.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GDPI slowdown since listing size-driven or structural from industry and competitive change, and does it require investment in other channels or lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman attributed it to EOM rules pushing commissions up and low-priced crop, group health and fire business written to meet EOM; said Q1 is the first quarter Digit lost market share, and that bancassurance, institutional and digital/B2C channels are growing well. Management is assuming soft conditions persist until at least 31 March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the impact of the 11 June 2026 Supreme Court TP ruling on TP loss ratio and reserving, and is the step-up recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said reserving is based on loss ratio plus legal inflation and frequency, with no separate provision; it is comfortable with reserves and takes no bet on judgment interpretation. Two High Court rulings (2 July Allahabad, 16 July Karnataka) were cited as narrowing the ruling; underwriting and claim-settlement actions were planned for around the third week of August 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Are there one-off or large losses in fire, marine and engineering this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman confirmed one large fire claim in Q1, but said gross fire loss ratio was 67%; he argued loss ratios are assessed on a gross basis because 80% of fire risk is ceded to reinsurers, and the company gives up treaty commission on some business to protect treaty profitability.

qa_highlights.question: Is the IRDAI-driven TP hike needed, and what would be the quantum? What is the dividend policy given solvency and IFRS?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 90-95% of vehicles need a TP premium hike, with a view that only about 5% of segments could see reductions; it is running the book without assuming a hike. On dividends, IGAAP solvency is about 242% and the Board will consider a dividend in the last quarter, subject to RBC norms (expected possibly this financial year).

qa_highlights.question: Is the TP claim-settlement approach (83% by compromise) adequate given 17% court awards, and will reserve releases be lower after the Supreme Court ruling?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 36,000 TP claims settled since inception, 83% by compromise and 17% by court award; it reported reserve release of INR204 crore for FY18-19 falling to INR132 crore over later years, said no MAD concept is used, and declined to guide on future releases. Motor actuarial review of frequency was expected in 3-5 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the OD loss ratio increase, and why was it not anticipated?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said he took the wrong call by holding stand-alone OD renewals and new-car business written in FY24-25; the problem is in private car, not 2W or CV, and the portfolio was cut sharp from March. OD loss ratio is expected to stabilise in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did group health loss ratio rise, and what drove NEP retention and EOM trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Group health rise was attributed to one large bank-driven personal accident policy, with claims provided for. Retention rose from a mix of higher retention in commercial lines and lower fire mix; EOM rose slightly at motor level due to exits from low-EOM fire and commercial business and non-renewal of group health and crop inward reinsurance.

544179|2026-09.headline: Go Digit Q2 FY27 CISR combined ratio rose to 99.8% from 94.9%, driven by Rs 63 crore Gujarat flood losses; ex-flood it was 97.4%.
544179|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 on Indian Accounting Standards for the first time, with comparatives restated. Insurance revenue rose to Rs 2,720 crore from Rs 2,675 crore, and PAT excluding mark-to-market was Rs 208 crore versus Rs 277 crore a year earlier. Excluding flood losses, PAT was Rs 255 crore, up sequentially from Rs 239 crore in Q1. GDPI fell 1.2% against industry growth of 7%, with private car standalone own damage premium down 40% after April-May price corrections. Management said private car own damage attritional loss ratio improved from 85.3% in Q1 to 81.1% in Q2.

segments.name: Motor
segments.commentary: Motor premium fell 4.1%, driven by private car down 10.7% and standalone own damage premium down 40%. Two-wheeler grew 18.6% and commercial vehicles fell 20%; school bus and auto-rickshaw writing was cut on weak commissions. Motor market share was 5.68% in Q2 vs 5.58% in Q1; own damage share was 4.99% vs 4.76%.

segments.name: Fire
segments.commentary: Fire gross written premium fell 29.9%. Gross earned loss ratio was 59% in Q2 (61.5% for H1) after flood losses, with engineering at 62.4% and liability at 25.7% in Q2.

segments.name: Health, travel and PA
segments.commentary: Retail health is under 6-7% of the book; the rest is group health. Group health growth was held back by Rs 95 crore of government and health reinsurance premium not renewed. Management estimates employer-employee business at about 80% of the health and PA book.

segments.name: Investments
segments.commentary: Equity and REIT/InvIT allocation is 9.6% of AUM on book value, excluding AT1 bonds, with unrealised equity gains of about Rs 148 crore. Duration was 4.8 years in September and 4.9 in October, against 5.2 in March 2025. Fixed-income reinvestment yield was about 8% in October, and overall yield is about 7.4%.

guidance_outlook: Management is not giving formal guidance; it said Q3 will show how the festive-season month-on-month trend develops.
Management expects growth declines to keep reducing, with pricing discipline returning in fire from mid-September.
Equity allocation may move toward 12.5% of AUM including REITs, subject to the capital allocation model.
Duration may be extended back toward 5.2 years depending on interest rates.
The company will hold an analyst day in February covering Indian Accounting Standards in more detail.
Management said the Indian Accounting Standards transition for the whole industry takes effect from 1 April 2027.
capex_capacity: Private car own damage attritional loss ratio fell to 81.1% in Q2 from 85.3% in Q1; the reported Q2 loss ratio was 93% including floods.
The commercial lines product has been launched with a full pricing and rating model; quotes are currently below 20 and management will wait about six months before judging scale.
Long-term advance premium was Rs 3,556 crore at 30 September 2026.
Solvency is 2.40x, with additional net worth of about Rs 3,300 crore that management said cannot currently be distributed or used to write business.
demand_pricing: No TP price hikes yet; the market is soft except property, where rates have firmed since mid-September.
Industry GDPI grew 7% while Digit's GDPI fell 1.2%; GWP fell 3.6%, or was flat excluding health reinsurance inward and government health.
Management attributes the higher expense ratio mainly to a rising two-wheeler mix, where commissions are higher, and says operational expenses are among the industry's best.
Management said it had lost TP market share this year and would not match commission levels it considers uneconomic.
Group health employer-employee loss ratios are above 100% for the industry, according to management, and it wants a 5% group health price increase.

qa_highlights.question: How will the distribution paper (EoM and commission changes) affect TP profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the discussion paper acknowledges that the current EoM guidelines have not produced the intended outcome. It declined to speculate on final guidance and suggested analysts run their own models using the commission and opex split on the website.

qa_highlights.question: What are the loss ratios without discounting, and what discount rate was used?
qa_highlights.answer: Discounting affects about 20% of TP outstanding claims plus IBNR. The risk-free rate is set at each quarter end plus 25% of the gap to the AAA yield as illiquidity premium; September discount rates were about 6.2-6.6% for liabilities up to one year and about 7.5% beyond eight years. Management declined to publish a non-discounted combined ratio, citing the Rs 171 crore finance expense offset.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the expense ratio rise in a soft market?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to the growing two-wheeler mix, which carries higher commissions than other lines.

qa_highlights.question: How will Digit compete if commissions and TP pricing are fixed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said commission and price are the only two levers and it will write business only where commissions are economic. It added that distribution will rely on existing partners and new channels.

qa_highlights.question: What is the market share of Gujarat flood losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its fire loss share is likely below its market share, and that motor is hard to judge because of EV battery write-offs and salvage values. Flood losses were Rs 63 crore net, against Rs 10 crore a year earlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is health loss ratio improving, and what is the group employer-employee mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said group health loss ratios are broadly unchanged. It estimated employer-employee at about 80% of health and PA, with retail around 6%. It cited a 5% group health price rise as enough to support growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IDBI Bank transaction's potential impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no information beyond Fairfax's announcement that it will sell its Digit stake to IDBI Bank. It said a bancassurance tie-up would be welcome if the bank became a corporate agent, since bancassurance is typically more profitable.

qa_highlights.question: Which products carry the onerous contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said onerous contracts arise in motor TP and group health; testing is done at a granular line-of-business level with the auditors.
