544192|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 PAT rose 91% YoY to INR32.1 crores on flat contribution margin of INR121.4 crores; GTV up 9% to INR4,798 crores against a high Kumbh base.
544192|2026-03.overview: ixigo reported Q4 FY26 GTV of INR4,797.7 crores (+9% YoY), revenue from operations of INR308.1 crores (+8%), contribution margin of INR121.4 crores (+0.4%, 39% margin) and adjusted EBITDA of INR30.3 crores (+4%). PAT was INR32.1 crores versus INR16.8 crores a year earlier. For FY26, GTV grew 25% to INR18,692.7 crores, revenue 34% to INR1,228 crores, adjusted EBITDA 28% to INR120.9 crores, and operating cash flow 60% to INR195.7 crores. Trains saw volume and GTV compression from policy changes and a Kumbh-inflated base, while flights and buses carried growth, and management spent much of the call on ixigo NEXT, its AI layer.

segments.name: Buses
segments.commentary: Q4 GTV INR696.8 crores (+26%), passenger segments 7.22 million (+32%), revenue INR80.4 crores (+22%), CM INR42.8 crores (+7%) at 53% margin; largest segment by CM at 35% share. FY26 GTV INR2,620.7 crores (+46%), CM INR153.2 crores (+18%).

segments.name: Flights
segments.commentary: Q4 GTV INR2,018.6 crores (+18%), 2.74 million segments (+14%), revenue INR95.7 crores (+9%), CM INR38.3 crores (-3%); now largest by GTV at 42.1% share. FY26 GTV INR7,514.6 crores (+33%), revenue INR390.7 crores (+54%), CM INR160.3 crores (+39%, 41% margin).

segments.name: Trains
segments.commentary: Q4 GTV INR2,002.4 crores (-5%), 24.18 million segments (-8%), revenue INR124.4 crores (-2%), CM INR39.7 crores (+1%) at 32% margin; 32.7% of group CM. OTA market share reported at 62% vs 60% a few quarters earlier. FY26 GTV INR8,278.9 crores (+12%), CM INR155.5 crores (+2%).

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Not disclosed separately; management will report only once product-market fit and scale are reached. Launched HELLO AI extranet for direct supplier onboarding; hotel build-out is a cost drag on EBITDA.

guidance_outlook: No formal numerical guidance; management declined to guide on bus growth ('secular growth engine' with higher CM than the rest of the business).
Q1 FY27 lacks the Kumbh base effect seen in Q4 FY26, which management expects to show up in growth.

Trains: near-term headwinds expected from policy changes; upgraded PRS system expected August or September 2026 could help, as could any reversal of policy or opening of unreserved ticketing for OTAs. Europe business acquisition (Trenes) may add positive impact.
Contribution margin: management is comfortable running flights and buses at 1-2% lower CM to chase market share; focus is on absolute rupee CM and EBITDA growth, not margin percentage.
AI capitalisation: a portion of core AI platform spend is capitalised and amortised over 5 years; experimentation and operations stay in P&L. No hotel-related capitalisation.
capex_capacity: Capitalised a portion of core AI infrastructure (orchestration layer and platform capabilities) with 5-year amortisation; management did not quantify the amount.
Hotels: small on-ground onboarding team; HELLO extranet launched to accelerate direct supplier onboarding. Hotel costs sit within group EBITDA.
Bus network: 6,000-plus operators onboarded, with more than 4,500 transacting monthly; management says inventory is at parity with peers.
Use of Prosus fundraise proceeds: about two years remain in the timeline; part used for AI build-out and one acquisition (Trenes, Europe); hotels supply expansion ongoing.
demand_pricing: Domestic flight demand described as strong in peak summer season; international demand hit by Middle East situation, higher fares on many routes and airline route cuts.
Outbound was above 20% of flight GTV in Q3; management estimates Q4 was not far from that level.
Substitution: international trips shifting to domestic flights, and some demand moving to buses and trains because of high flight fares and constrained train availability.
Train demand constrained by Indian Railways policy changes (Tatkal window restrictions for OTAs, reduced waitlist inventory, repeat-user re-verification, Aadhaar norms) and tight 2S supply.
Bus online penetration cited at roughly 22-23% (from about 20%), so a large offline pool remains.

qa_highlights.question: Can growth resilience be quantified given 50 days into Q1, and how did past demand shocks affect growth and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 FY27 lacks the Kumbh base, domestic demand is strong, and international is affected by fares and route cuts. Past shocks produced substitution from international to domestic flights and from flights to buses and trains.

qa_highlights.question: What share of flight business is outbound, and what is at risk from curbs on foreign travel?
qa_highlights.answer: Outbound was more than 20% of flight GTV in Q3; management believes Q4 was similar. Volumes were hit more than value, and convenience fees depend on volume.

qa_highlights.question: How sustainable is bus growth and is there scope for share gains from inventory gaps?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a growth multiple but cited consistent outgrowth of the OTA bus market for three years, low offline penetration, and product innovation. It said inventory is at parity with peers.

qa_highlights.question: Why was AI spend capitalised, what is the amortisation period, and is any hotel spend capitalised?
qa_highlights.answer: Only long-term foundational AI infrastructure is capitalised, amortised over 5 years. Experimentation and operations are expensed, and no hotel costs are capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for train growth beyond FY27, and what could change it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said policy changes are one-time and will weigh on YoY comparisons for some quarters. Share gains are being held at the current level, and an upgraded PRS or unreserved ticketing could help. Management declined to give numerical guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Should contribution margin hold at 36-37% and will EBITDA margin expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said flights and buses are run within guardrails, with margins of roughly 30%, 40% and 50% for trains, flights and buses. Hotel build-out eats into operating leverage, and the focus is on absolute rupee CM and EBITDA growth.

risks_watch: Train volumes and GTV continue to decline under policy changes; watch for PRS upgrade timing (August or September 2026) and any Tatkal policy revisions.
International flight exposure to Middle East disruption, higher fares and route cuts; outbound was over 20% of flight GTV in Q3.
Hotel investment dilutes EBITDA; hotels will not be disclosed separately until scale is reached.
Rising technology and AI costs; capitalisation policy and 5-year amortisation could shift the P&L profile.
Q1 FY27 growth comparisons are expected to ease from Q4's Kumbh-inflated base, so monitor the reported step-up.
544192|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the core and on AI strategy, but cautious and non-committal on trains and guidance. Management repeatedly declined to give numbers on bus growth, train growth and EBITDA trajectory, and framed the quarter as in line with plan.
key_quotes: We are in the Peace of Mind business and that is now visible in the operating metrics.

So it is AI. What we've done is we've capitalized a portion of the core usable AI investment, which is related to building the foundational infrastructure orchestration layer and platform capabilities that we expect to deploy across the multiple use cases within the OTA ecosystem.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The upgraded PRS system is expected in August or September 2026 and ixigo NEXT AI layer and HELLO extranet are already live, but no specific consumer product launch date was given.

rows.label: Indian Railways PRS upgrade and Tatkal/unreserved ticketing policy
rows.why: Trains GTV fell 5% and segments fell 8% in Q4, and a PRS upgrade in Aug/Sep 2026 or a policy reversal could restore train volumes, though neither is confirmed.

rows.why: Management says the Europe business acquisition may add a positive impact, but no size or timing was given beyond it being part of the Prosus fundraise use of proceeds with about two years remaining.

rows.why: A portion of core AI platform spend is already capitalised and amortised over 5 years, which shifts reported cost timing, though the amount was not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on the core flights and buses and on the ixigo NEXT AI strategy, but cautious and non-committal on trains and numerical guidance, declining to quantify bus, train or EBITDA trajectory; analysts pushed on outbound flight exposure, bus growth sustainability, AI capitalisation

544192|2026-06.headline: ixigo Q1 FY27: record GTV of Rs 5,524 crore (+19% YoY) and PAT of Rs 34.24 crore (+81%), while adjusted EBITDA fell 7% to Rs 29.24 crore as hotels and AI were funded.
544192|2026-06.overview: Management described the quarter as one where the core businesses (buses, trains, flights) kept growing and gaining share despite the Iran conflict's effect on oil and airfares and train policy constraints on OTAs. Revenue from operations rose 13% to Rs 356.75 crore and contribution margin rose 13% to Rs 144.94 crore at 40.6%. Management said it chose to reinvest part of the core operating leverage into hotels (Brevistay 54.66% acquisition) and AI (ixigo NEXT, TARA, busGDS.ai), which lowered adjusted EBITDA and the 'Others' contribution margin to negative Rs 3.06 crore. Flights volume growth was muted as capacity cuts by Air India and IndiGo weakened the new-to-flying funnel, and management declined to guide on near-term flight growth.

Share of loss from associates (Fresh Bus, Sqaas)

segments.name: Flights
segments.commentary: Segments 0.29 crore (+4%); GTV Rs 2,341.84 crore (+27%); revenue Rs 104.56 crore; contribution margin Rs 41.04 crore at 39% vs 42% last year. Domestic ATV +22% YoY and international ATV +38% YoY; contributed 28% of group contribution margin.

segments.name: Buses (AbhiBus)
segments.commentary: Passenger segments 0.89 crore (+33%); GTV Rs 947.43 crore (+39%); revenue Rs 102.55 crore (+34%); contribution margin Rs 54.22 crore (+28%) at 53%. Now the largest contributor at 37% of group contribution margin. Management cited GDP growth of 39% YoY.

segments.name: Others (hotels, Zoop and other businesses)
segments.commentary: Contribution margin negative Rs 3.06 crore vs positive Rs 1.86 crore last year, reflecting hotel build-out spend. Management said hotel investment is showing up above the contribution margin line, deliberately.

guidance_outlook: No formal guidance on brand marketing spend; management said customer inducement cost (brand performance plus discounts) is targeted at around 4% of GTV where possible, with some quarters above that.
Management expects hotels to have a longer gestation period; the ambition is to become the number one discovery and booking platform for mid-market and budget hotels within four to five years.
Management expects technology cost growth rate to moderate as initial AI platform investment matures, with the long-term aim of technology cost falling as a percentage of revenue year on year.
Management expects flight capacity to recover only around the festive period in Q3, so it remains cautious on near-term aviation passenger growth.
Management said other income (around Rs 29 crore) should not rise substantially.
Management declined to guide on Q2 FY27 flight growth or on margin trajectory, saying growth depends on ATV and supply.
capex_capacity: Brevistay: 54.66% stake acquisition to add direct hotel relationships and flexible-stay inventory; management expects double-digit gross take rates from the combined platform.

Hotels: more than 10,000 directly partnered hotels across nearly 700 towns; several thousand onboarded every quarter; about 0.5 million room-nights (heads on beds) in Q1; HELLO extranet supports conventional and flexible stays.
Budget-hotel Peace of Mind products and a PMS to be tested on select properties, with rollout over the subsequent quarters of FY27.
Capitalisation of AI/platform costs stated to be in the same range as the prior quarter, per the CFO; no absolute number given.
Metro bookings live in five cities; busGDS.ai launched at Prawaas 5.0 for bus operators (setup in as little as 30 minutes).
demand_pricing: Domestic ATV on the platform +22% YoY and +13% QoQ; international ATV +38% YoY and nearly +30% QoQ. DGCA industry passenger growth was about 2% YoY per management.
Air India capacity cut about 20% and IndiGo about 10% for the July-September quarter, per management, with overall domestic capacity shrinking.
Bus net take rate fell QoQ to 10.8%; management said discounting was range-bound over the last 6-8 quarters, and gross take rate is 11-11.5%.
Bus category described as a near-duopoly; management said the company was more disciplined on discounts and marketing this quarter than peers.

Train volumes pressured by Tatkal access changes for OTAs, lower waitlist inventory and extra authentication; management is hopeful about OTP-based authentication for OTAs but is not planning on relief.
AI customer-query resolution by chatbot rose to 92% from 88%; app downloads 3.27 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~80% sequential jump in advertising spend one-time or ongoing, and where should margins go from here?
qa_highlights.answer: Aloke said Q1 brand spend is seasonal (IPL activity, AbhiBus push) and no brand marketing guidance is given; customer inducement (brand plus discounts) is targeted around 4% of GTV where possible. Saurabh said Q1 spend followed a similar pattern last year and higher take-rate businesses should lift EBITDA over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why did flight GTV grow 27% when volume grew only 4%, and will Q2 flight volumes decline sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Aloke attributed the gap to fares: domestic ATV +22% YoY and international +38%, with DGCA industry passenger growth about 2%. He said Air India capacity was cut about 20% and IndiGo about 10% for the July-September quarter and gave no forward call on Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 0.5 million hotel room-nights comes from the existing user base, and how much investment sits in hotels and AI below contribution margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Aloke said about 90% of hotel bookings come from already-registered users, and that the 'Others' line moved by roughly Rs 5 crore YoY. Management did not split hotel and AI investment, and Saurabh declined to give a margin guardrail or a multi-year EBITDA path.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs rise while technology costs were flat QoQ, and what is the AI capitalisation figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh said hotel costs sit across technology and employee lines, and that capitalisation is in the same range as last quarter, with no absolute number given.

qa_highlights.question: Are train contribution margin gains from the Spanish or consolidated business, or organic?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh said train is a small part of the business and that the margin should not be projected forward; costs were cut during the quarter, and the 'Train is Part' initiative is early, with a clearer read in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the easier base support flight growth acceleration?
qa_highlights.answer: Saurabh said growth is a function of ATV and supply, and he cannot forecast macro conditions; he would expect improvement only if the geopolitical situation clears.

qa_highlights.question: Bus net take rate fell QoQ to 10.8%: is discounting rising and will it recover to 11-11.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Aloke said 11-11.5% is the gross take rate and that discounting has been range-bound over the last 6-8 quarters, with no intention to get aggressive. The Q1 dip reflected the seasonal AMJ peak with more marketing and discounts, and the company was more disciplined than peers.

risks_watch: Flight growth depends on fares and supply: Air India (about -20%) and IndiGo (about -10%) capacity cuts for July-September, with management expecting recovery only around Q3 festive period.

544192|2026-09.headline: ixigo Q2 FY27 GTV rose 22% to INR 5,304 crore and PAT hit a record, but adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to INR 23.6 crore on a stepped-up hotel investment.
544192|2026-09.overview: Consolidated GTV grew 22% YoY to INR 5,304.47 crore and revenue from operations rose 13% to INR 320.96 crore, with contribution margin up 14% to INR 124.86 crore. Adjusted EBITDA fell 17% to INR 23.58 crore from INR 28.48 crore as management deliberately funded hotel people and technology spend. Reported PAT was an all-time high of INR 63.42 crore, aided by a INR 40.66 crore exceptional gain on the partial sale of Freshbus. Flights were weak: GTV grew 37% on higher fares, but revenue fell 8% as take rate compressed from 9.4% to 7%. Hotels were disclosed as a separate segment for the first time.

financial_highlights.change: All-time high; includes Freshbus exceptional gain of INR 40.66 crore
vs INR 5.17 crore a year ago; treasury income, excluded from adjusted EBITDA

financial_highlights.metric: Net cash incl. FDs and MFs, net of borrowings

segments.name: Trains
segments.commentary: Passenger segments up about 7% to 2.9 crore; revenue up 16% to INR 149.14 crore; CM up 29% to INR 47.23 crore (32% of revenue). OTA rail market share close to 64%. Food on trains moved into trains segment.

segments.name: Buses
segments.commentary: GTV up 32% to INR 752.65 crore; revenue up 24% to INR 81.04 crore; CM up 27% to INR 43.14 crore (53% of revenue).

segments.name: Flights
segments.commentary: GTV up 37% on higher fares, but revenue down 8% to INR 82.66 crore; CM down 10% to INR 35.68 crore, held at 43% of revenue. Take rate fell from 9.4% to 7%. International flight GTV up 59%.

segments.name: Hotels (new disclosure)
segments.commentary: GTV up 2.6x YoY to INR 111.34 crore (up 39% QoQ), about 4.7 lakh room nights, take rate above 12%, revenue INR 8.1 crore. Contribution loss INR 1.21 crore vs INR 0.71 crore a year ago; CM -15% of revenue vs -55% a year ago. Brevistay consolidated from this quarter, so part of growth is inorganic.

guidance_outlook: Hotel investment (above and below CM) was about INR 11 crore this quarter; management expects a similar range of INR 10-12 crore per quarter over the next couple of quarters, not a firm guidance.
Hotel take rate expected to edge up over the next 3-4 quarters; no guidance given on the level for next year.
Hotel room night ambition to keep growing at triple digits over the next four quarters; aim to be largest budget-to-mid-market hotel OTA by room nights in 4-5 years.
Flights: management is not guiding to aggressive growth; October started softer than expected with capacity not yet back, and festive demand is a shade below expectations.
Management says it will not step up flight discounts beyond current fare levels.
Profitability for hotels not targeted near term; investment expected for 2-3 years, with company-level EBITDA kept around mid-single-digit levels.
capex_capacity: Hotel direct supply: over 12,000 directly contracted hotels across about 1,100 towns, up from 10,000 last quarter, out of about 70,000 hotels sold.
Management says it is not in a rush to grow the directly contracted base faster than its own growth.
Hotel share of GTV is about 2.1%; management targets hotels as one of the top two GTV contributors in 4-5 years.
Freshbus stake partly sold on August 13, resulting in a INR 40.66 crore gain; company describes itself as asset-light.
Acquisitions: selective, only where there is strategic fit, team, technology or distribution synergy, and reasonable pricing; will disclose when they crystallise.
demand_pricing: Overall flight market volume down nearly 6% in the quarter; ixigo flight segment grew 7%.
Flight fares up about 30% YoY on several routes due to oil prices; capacity slow to return; load factors edging down.
Flight take rate compression attributed to higher discounts for NBU users, growing international mix and convenience fees forming a larger share of income.
Hotel take rate above 12% blended, versus the 16-17% level seen at other OTAs; higher take rates in mid-tier and independent hotels are the structural argument.
About 86% of hotel bookings came from existing platform users; 94% of transactions involve Tier 2 and 3 cities.
Hotel ATV around INR 2,200 per room night; management does not guide to a specific ATV level.
Trains: festive advance bookings helped; management wants to see momentum persist beyond the festive season before calling the recovery sustained.
Bus growth described as ahead of the overall OTA bus market for close to three years.
AI platform traffic is a low single-digit percentage of traffic for the category; agentic booking flow demoed at GFS, launch awaiting regulatory clarity.

qa_highlights.question: Why did flight revenue per ticket fall 13-14% against the recent average; is this a permanent share-gain strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher discounts were needed to keep NBU flight users affordable given the 30% fare rise, and international mix and convenience fees also compressed take rate. It said it would not step up discounts further at current fares.

qa_highlights.question: Is there early visibility on Q3 flight trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Festive demand is a shade lower than expected; management is cautious on flights and not guiding to aggressive growth, but says it will keep growing.

qa_highlights.question: When will hotel take rate reach 16-17% and when will the segment be profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Take rate will edge up over the next 3-4 quarters as direct supply grows, with no next-year guidance. Profitability is not targeted near term; investment is expected for 2-3 years, with spending tied to observed returns and payback periods.

qa_highlights.question: How should investors frame hotel investment within guardrails?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment was INR 1 crore-plus above CM and about INR 10 crore below CM this quarter. Guardrails are customer payback periods and keeping company-level EBITDA in the mid-single-digit range, with a near-term range of INR 10-12 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What GTV mix can be expected over 3-4 years, and will rail share gains continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Hotels could be the second-largest GTV contributor in 4-5 years. Management expects rail GTV share to decline from the early 40s given 4-5% annual capacity growth; buses to be the second-fastest growing line after hotels.

qa_highlights.question: How much of a threat do consumer AI agents pose, and which segments are most exposed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI-platform traffic is still a low single-digit share and sees specialist vertical agents, and ixigo's proprietary data and peace-of-mind products as differentiators. Building products is easy; trust and distribution are the hard parts.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus growth of about 28% too slow given supply and rail constraints?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is comfortable with the current pace, trading growth for margin and a sustainable business, and noted bus CM is about 53% of revenue.

risks_watch: Flight recovery: capacity has not returned, fares are up about 30%, and October started softer than expected.
Hotel economics: blended take rate of 12% is well below the 16-17% at peers; contribution loss is widening in absolute terms and profitability is 2-3 years away.
Adjusted EBITDA down 17%; the reported PAT includes a one-time Freshbus gain, so underlying earnings are weaker than headline.
Rail: management says recovery is not yet proven beyond the festive season; rail GTV share may decline.
AI agents: consumer AI platforms could disintermediate bookings; the agentic booking flow awaits regulatory clarity before launch.
Inorganic: Brevistay consolidation adds to hotel growth; future acquisitions are unspecified.

544198|2026-03.headline: DEE Development FY26 revenue rose 38% to Rs 1,142 Cr and PAT 76.9% to Rs 77.2 Cr; order book Rs 2,040 Cr with FY27 inflow guided above Rs 2,000 Cr.
544198|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the first year after most of the growth capex cycle, with Anjar fabrication and the seamless pipe plant commissioned. Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 361.6 Cr (+26.3% YoY) and PAT Rs 27.7 Cr, against a high Q4 FY25 base that included Q3 spillover. Management split the business into core (piping, heavy fabrication) and non-core (power, biomass pallets), with core EBITDA of Rs 210.5 Cr (+64.2%) excluding non-core losses. The company guided to a Rs 1,500 Cr revenue commitment for FY27, a Rs 2,500 Cr revenue target by FY30, and a consolidated EBITDA margin above 19%, while the Malwa Power tariff revision and the Thailand HRSG job-work order were the main new items.

segments.name: Non-core power (Malwa Power)
segments.commentary: Tariff revised to Rs 5.22/kWh from Rs 3.5/kWh with retrospective recovery of about Rs 5.52 Cr; Rs 5 Cr of the retrospective benefit is in the quarter per analyst Q&A. Appellate challenge pending; plant still carries a qualified audit opinion.

segments.name: Non-core biomass pallets
segments.commentary: Biomass pallet facility recently commissioned, expected to offset current cash burn. Combined power and pallet revenue guided at about Rs 47.71 Cr in FY27.

segments.name: DEE Thailand (HRSG job work)
segments.commentary: Unit works purely on job-work basis; about 60% of its roughly 14,500 capacity reserved for HRSG orders, with revenue of about Rs 150 Cr per year implied. Management said no capex is needed for this order beyond minor machinery.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Thailand HRSG order linked to the GE/Siemens/Mitsubishi gas turbine backlog, and does the Rs 150 Cr revenue need capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most orders are linked to the overseas HRSG market. Thailand works on job-work basis, so the Rs 150 Cr figure is mostly value-add rather than full revenue, with EBITDA margin above 20% and only minor capex.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the gross margin decline is commodity inflation versus mix, and what are the alloy and job-work splits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a quarterly split, citing project-based business, and pointed to trading activity at 95-100% material value in Q4. Job-work orders are about 30% of the book; about 55-60% of thermal and HRSG work is alloy steel.

qa_highlights.question: Are order flows and margins sustainable with the new Anjar and seamless plants?

qa_highlights.question: Why is order book up about 50% while guidance is 20-25% growth, and why did inventory stay flat?

qa_highlights.answer: Management is on the drawing board for new capacity, aiming for assets sustainable over 10-15 years, and will publish a blueprint soon.

qa_highlights.question: Malwa Power: how will the qualified audit opinion be resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects both plants to be slightly positive at current tariffs, so no impairment or contingency is needed. Audit finding expected to clear by Q3 FY27, per the CFO.

544198|2026-06.headline: DEE Development Engineers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 31.6% YoY to Rs 294.5 crore and EBITDA margin hit 16.9%, despite ~Rs 25 crore of dispatches slipping into Q2.
544198|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was Rs 294.5 crore, up 31.6% YoY, with operating EBITDA of Rs 49.7 crore (16.9% margin vs 16% a year earlier). Management said about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches, deferred by export customers amid Middle East disruption, moved into Q2. Profit after tax was Rs 16.1 crore, and the Rs 300 crore preferential issue (net ~Rs 293 crore, ~Rs 225 crore earmarked for debt repayment) closed in July. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ revenue, EBITDA margin above 19%, and order inflow of at least Rs 2,000 crore.

segments.name: Piping and heavy fabrication (core)
segments.commentary: Management guides Rs 1,150-1,250 crore from piping for FY27, with the balance from subsidiaries including Thailand. Piping and heavy fabrication are the large majority of revenue and order book.

segments.name: Thailand subsidiary
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about Rs 130 crore; target Rs 170-200 crore. Management says it is practically 100% booked for three years and no expansion is planned.

segments.name: Power PPA / non-core (Malwa, biomass pellets)
segments.commentary: Pellet plant (72,000 MT p.a., Muktsar) commissioned mid-Q1 FY27, so only partial contribution this quarter. Target combined non-core revenue around Rs 80 crore. Management said PPA EBIT went slightly negative (about Rs 1 crore) as fuel was diverted to the pellet plant; full operation expected from October.

segments.name: Seamless pipe plant (Anjar)
segments.commentary: Commissioned in FY26. Existing orders include about Rs 68 crore from L&T and a Rs 200 crore BHEL order, of which Rs 80-90 crore is expected to use in-house pipe. Management targets about 20% EBITDA on seamless pipe.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance of Rs 1,500 crore+ reiterated; management called it a minimum and said the plan is to exceed it. Q1 is the weakest quarter, with Q4 typically the strongest.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided above 19%; management said it is 'absolutely on track'.
FY27 order inflow expected at least Rs 2,000 crore; Rs 700 crore already received, with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the rest of the year.
Net debt expected to be no more than Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end; no plans for new debt this year.
Anjar plant utilisation expected at 60-65% this year and near 100% by end of FY28. Anjar revenue target of about Rs 1,500 crore by FY28-29.
Inventory days targeted at 150-160 by Q2 and 180-200 days for the overall working-capital cycle.
capex_capacity: Anjar pipe fabrication facility fully operational; seamless pipe plant commissioned in FY26. Plan is roughly 50-50 split between captive and outright-sale use of Anjar capacity.
Biomass pellet plant (72,000 MT p.a.) at Malwa Power Plant, Muktsar, commissioned in Q1 FY27.
Nuclear sector entry planned via a partner; management aims to finalise the partnership agreement in Q2 FY27.
No capex or capacity expansion planned at Thailand facility.
Preferential issue proceeds of about Rs 293 crore net: about Rs 224-225 crore for debt or working-capital repayment, balance for general corporate purposes.
demand_pricing: Revenue slippage: about Rs 25 crore of oil and gas dispatches deferred to Q2 as export customers delayed take-offs due to the Middle East situation; material is ready.
GE: GT orders continuing; HRSG order from GE yet to come, though an agreement exists for around 15-16 units. A GE meeting is set for 14 September.
Siemens: MoU for GT piping starting at 10 units next year, then 15, then 25-30 units. Each GT unit is about EUR 1-1.5 million. Siemens team to visit Anjar in the third week of August.
BHEL: slower than expected, but about Rs 200 crore order received last quarter and more tenders expected to be finalised next quarter. L&T has awarded all orders offloaded so far.
Export mix: about 50% export and 50% domestic for FY27. The order book includes about Rs 400 crore of India HRSG work and about Rs 200 crore from Thailand.
Gross margin pressure attributed to higher material content in power-sector jobs (versus job-work) and the mix shift. Management said conversion costs are lower for power jobs.
Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited domestic order of Rs 386.82 crore received in the quarter, described as one of the largest single orders in recent history.
Gulf reconstruction: inquiries are coming via OEMs; not yet direct, and not included in projections for five years.

qa_highlights.question: Status of GE HRSG orders and Siemens GT piping?
qa_highlights.answer: GE GT orders continue, HRSG order yet to come despite agreement for 15-16 units. Siemens MoU for 10 units next year, 15 the year after, then 25-30. Each GT unit about EUR 1-1.5 million.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Rs 2,000 crore order inflow guidance still valid given delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; management said inflow may exceed Rs 2,000 crore. Rs 700 crore already received, with Rs 1,300-1,800 crore expected in the remainder of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PPA EBIT turn negative?
qa_highlights.answer: Limited fuel meant the company prioritised the pellet plant over the power plant. Full operation of both is expected from October when new fuel arrives.

qa_highlights.question: Net debt trajectory and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt Rs 718 crore at Q1 close versus Rs 733 crore at FY26 close, expected to fall to Rs 400-425 crore by FY27 end. Rs 224 crore used for working-capital limits reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher material content in power-sector jobs and a mix shift away from job-work. Management still expects EBITDA above 19%.

qa_highlights.question: Tax rate for modelling?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone rate 25.17%; consolidated effective rate about 20-21% because of the Thailand subsidiary and subsidy income.

rows.why: Net debt fell to Rs 718 crore at Q1 from Rs 733 crore at FY26 close, and about Rs 224-225 crore of preferential issue proceeds are earmarked for debt or working-capital repayment.

rows.why: Inventory days are 174 versus 243 a year ago, and the overall cycle is targeted at 180-200 days, but debtor days rose to 123 from 99 and creditor days fell to 34 from 66.

544202|2026-03.headline: Stanley Lifestyles FY26 gross margin rose 151 bps to 57.5%, but Q4 revenue fell on B2B export pull-down and management guides only conservative FY27 growth.
544202|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year spent acquiring franchise markets (Chennai, Hyderabad, Pune) into company-owned stores and consolidating subsidiaries into one listed entity. Q4 FY26 saw a decline in B2B demand from mid-Q4, with roughly Rs. 15 crore of B2B revenue pulled down due to West Asia conflict disruptions to a large export client. Gross margin for FY26 improved to 57.5% from 56.3%, while cash was about Rs. 200 crore versus Rs. 215 crore a year earlier despite capex above Rs. 60 crore. Management opened 11 stores and closed three over 12 months, and guided to aspirational double-digit growth but a conservative stance for FY27.

financial_highlights.metric: Order book at start of FY27
Higher depreciation and finance cost (lease front-loading under Ind AS)

financial_highlights.value: about 4% for mature stores (over 3 years); Stanley Level Next +11.6%, Sofas & More +3.5%, Stanley Boutique -8.1%

segments.name: B2C (retail, COCO and FOFO)

segments.name: B2B / export
segments.commentary: About 30% of Q4 FY26 revenue. Around Rs. 15 crore pulled down in Q4 due to delays from West Asia conflict on exports to a large global furniture brand; management expects recovery around Q2 FY27 and is targeting high-end B2B and some exports.

B2C and B2B supply chain and export disruptions expected to flow into FY27; B2B export recovery hoped for by Q2 FY27.
QCO regulation on furniture imports effective 15 August 2026, expected to deter imports, the main competition.

capex_capacity: Capex in FY26 exceeded Rs. 60 crore, the highest ever; management says investment will continue for some time while consolidating mature markets.

Marketing spend has historically stayed below 10% of revenue; management plans to increase event and fair participation (AD, ELLE Decor) and possibly social media influencers from 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Growth of stores open over three years and why company-owned store revenue looks flat since 2023 despite more stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Mature stores have grown about 4% a year; the flat revenue reflects a 35% drop in franchisee business and about Rs. 18-20 crore lost from leather trading moved to cash-and-carry, plus Rs. 24 crore cited in total.

qa_highlights.question: What were the short-term disruptions in the last quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A large global furniture brand's B2B exports to the Middle East were halted by the war-related logistics standstill; orders were postponed and recovery is expected by Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why not pursue low-end B2B inquiries given low plant utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its back-end is built for premium B2C and it cannot compete with unorganised low-end B2B; it is pursuing high-end B2B inquiries from MNCs and considering exports.

qa_highlights.question: Store economics and when stores start generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says ROI, including interest on capex, is about 3 years; some catchments take 15-18 months and Bangalore micro-markets 24-36 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin down sequentially in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed Q4 to raw material delays due to the US-Iran war and about Rs. 15 crore B2B revenue pull-down; it said full-year gross margin improved and B2C margins are secure.

qa_highlights.question: Digital discovery, website and pricing policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management admitted it has been slow on digital, said SAP is implemented, and promised a new AI-assisted website, with AR/VR tools, by end FY27.

risks_watch: Q4 FY26 revenue decline and continued B2B export disruption from West Asia conflict; management expects recovery only from Q2 FY27.
Franchisee business down 35%, and conversion of franchise markets to COCO adds capex and lease-related depreciation and finance cost.
Store ramp-up: over half of stores are immature and 3-year ROI is management's own metric; watch for store closures and relocations.
Subsidiary merger into a single listed entity, with the Rs. 3.3 crore labour code exceptional charge and KMP compensation overlap.
Effectiveness of QCO from 15 August 2026 in curbing imports, and Hyderabad flagship going live around July 2026.

544202|2026-06.headline: Stanley Lifestyles Q1 FY27 revenue fell to INR 9,935 lakhs (from 10,861 lakhs) and PAT was just INR 65 lakhs, on delayed handovers and B2B shipment disruption.
544202|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations declined about 8.5% YoY to INR 9,935 lakhs in Q1 FY27, driven by slower retail conversions as residential handovers slipped 12 to 18 months and by B2B billing that stalled due to West Asia freight disruption. Management said gross margin was maintained and EBITDA was INR 1,722 lakhs (17.3% margin), with PAT of INR 65 lakhs. The company opened 3 Bangalore stores and closed 4 (3 Bangalore, 1 Mumbai), entered Sri Lanka via a JV, opened a Jaipur store, and announced a store-format overhaul (Stanley Superlative Living) plus a proposed amalgamation of subsidiaries. An internal audit flagged a fraud by the company secretary, under investigation.

544203|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 EBITDA rose 21.2% to a record ₹182 crore with margin up 179 bps to 17.9%; FY27 margins guided flat to FY26 at 14.4%.
544203|2026-03.overview: Consolidated income from operations for Q4 FY26 was ₹1,020 crore, up 9.1% YoY, with P&A volume up 20.5% to 4.4 million cases. Gross margin expanded 480 bps YoY to 48.2%, partly reinvested in brand-building. For FY26, consolidated revenue grew 11.5% to ₹3,949 crore, EBITDA rose 25.8% to ₹568 crore and reported PAT was ₹220 crore (adjusted ₹266 crore after ₹45.45 crore of tax items). Management guided FY27 mid-teens top-line growth, with a Q1 and early Q2 margin squeeze from the West Asia conflict before recovery from FTA, Telangana price hike and backward integration.

segments.name: P&A (Prestige & Above)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume up 20.5% YoY to 4.4 million cases, 57.7% of sales. FY26 share was 47.2% of volume and 57.3% of value. ICONiQ White sold 10.7 million cases in FY26 (up about 88%).

segments.name: Mass premium and other
segments.commentary: Q4 volume up 5.6% QoQ, driven by South and East, but flat YoY as management prioritised profitable state brand mix. Officer's Choice brandy has begun in Andhra Pradesh.

segments.name: ABD Maestro (super premium to luxury)
segments.commentary: Launched 10 brands, now in about 11 states and 4 travel retail locations. FY27 target to cross ₹100 crore revenue; year 1 EBITDA negative.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: FY26 export revenue up 14.1% to ₹235 crore; markets rose from 23 to 36. Q4 was partly hit by geopolitical disruption.

P&A expected to grow at high teens by FY28; mass premium and other to grow low to mid-single digits.
FY27 overall EBITDA margin guided to be at least equal to FY26 (14.4%); Q1 and early Q2 to see margin pressure from West Asia conflict.
Phase 1 and 2 backward integration expected to add about 300 bps to EBITDA margin by FY28 and about 100 bps more by FY29; FY28 EBITDA margin target raised to 18% from 17%.
UK FTA expected in Q2 FY27; Telangana price increase planned for H2 FY27 base case.
Management expects leverage to stay within guardrails on an annualised basis through the capex cycle; does not intend to breach covenants.
ESOP charge of about ₹5-6 crore per quarter in FY27.
capex_capacity: Phase 1 PET bottling facility in Telangana commissioned in Q2 FY26 and EBITDA accretive from Q3; it meets about 70-75% of requirement.
Malt distillery in Telangana (4 million litres, 12 KLPD per Amar Sinha) expected operational in H1 FY27.
ENA distillery expansion in Maharashtra expected operational in H1 FY28.
Phase 2 backward integration covers bottling and ENA in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh; UP bottling plant expected in H2 to avoid ₹27 franchise fee on own brands.
Accelerated depreciation on certain plant assets, including the PET facility, raised Q4 and FY26 depreciation.
demand_pricing: Telangana: receivables and overdue receivables fell QoQ in Q4; management says FY24 and FY25 dues are cleared. Telangana price increase committee formed; management hopes for Q2 but plans for H2.
Karnataka: slab reduction policy not yet implemented; management sees neutral to positive for Officer's Choice (about 300,000 cases a year), with ICONiQ a potential opportunity.
Price increases taken in several markets; management says gross margin gain came from price, trade-spend control, state brand mix and about 30 bps from PET unit.
The Prestige & Above whisky segment is about 120 million cases, with ICONiQ, OC Blue and SRB7 at about 18-20 million cases combined. Management acknowledges some cannibalisation.
OC Blue and SRB7 are over 10 years old; SRB7 test marketing showed low single-digit growth. OC Blue packaging refresh due Q2 FY27.
CSD industry size about 12 million cases a year; ICONiQ, SRB7, Kyron and Jolly Roger approved. Management says ABD Maestro's 1% volume share equals about 9% value.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 margin upside from UK FTA, Telangana price hike and backward integration, and will H1 margins hold given glass and fuel inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 margins to be broadly equal to FY26, with pressure in Q1 and early Q2 and expansion from H2. Telangana hike is seen as a significant upside.

qa_highlights.question: Amar Sinha's vision and leadership transition timing?
qa_highlights.answer: He outlined a 3-year plan: premium-and-above above 50% of volume, high-teens revenue growth, 48-50% gross margin, EBITDA margin above 20% and ROCE about 25%. Alok Gupta said the transition announcement is expected within this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ICONiQ expansion plan and ABD Maestro ARR?
qa_highlights.answer: ICONiQ is distributed nationally, approved in CSD, and exported to 9 countries. ABD Maestro is targeting over ₹100 crore in FY27 across 11 states.

qa_highlights.question: Will leverage stretch with accelerated capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex funded by internal accruals and borrowing; management does not intend to breach covenants.

qa_highlights.question: Why are OC Blue and SRB7 declining and when do they return to growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Both are over 10 years old in competitive segments. Management is resetting A&P and packaging, with SRB7 showing low single-digit growth in test markets.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 300 bps gross margin expansion comes from backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30 bps in FY27 from the PET unit; the rest is price increases, trade-spend control and brand mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Proactive scotch buying ahead of rupee depreciation against the pound, stored under FTWZ, plus smaller-batch ABD Maestro production.

544203|2026-06.headline: ABD Q1 FY27 revenue rose 5.8% to ₹984 crore and reported EBITDA was flat at ₹120 crore, as ₹24 crore of supply-chain disruption cost offset gross margin gains.
544203|2026-06.overview: Consolidated income from operations grew 5.8% YoY to ₹984 crore on 6.2% volume growth to 9 million cases, with Prestige and Above (P&A) volumes up 10.7%. Gross margin expanded 277 bps to 46%, but a ₹24 crore global supply-chain disruption hit profitability, leaving reported EBITDA at ₹120 crore (12.2% margin) versus ₹119 crore and PAT at ₹45 crore versus ₹56 crore. Management presented like-to-like EBITDA of ₹144 crore (14.7% margin, +21.4% YoY) excluding the disruption. Net debt fell ₹33 crore QoQ to ₹947 crore, with net debt to EBITDA at 1.7x.

segments.commentary: Volume 3.1 million cases vs 2.3 million in Q1 FY26 (+33.8%); monthly average above 1 million cases. Management targets close to 15 million cases in FY27 from 10.7 million in FY26.

segments.commentary: Volume share 48.2% (vs 46.2%) and value share 59.3% (vs 55.8%); segment volume grew 10.7% YoY. Management said ABD outgrew an industry where P&A grew low single digits.

segments.commentary: Volume grew 2.3% YoY, led by Northern and Southern regions in whisky and brandy.

qa_highlights.question: What are ABD Maestro's manpower, advertising and salary cost trajectory, and any long-term revenue or profit targets?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said expenses will not rise further and will be subsidised by distribution support. FY26 turnover was about ₹40 crore, expected to double in FY27. Management called it at least a three-year gestation luxury business and declined to give longer-term numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the guidance building in a Telangana price hike and a resolution to supply-chain and glass inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the two-year guidance and said it could be stepped up. Telangana price hike talks are ongoing with guardrails built in. Management expects the war-related pressure to last until Q2 and then ease.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Officer's Choice Blue, Sterling Reserve B7 and B10 declining, and what is being done?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed cash-flow constraints before the 2024 listing and said ICONiQ is the growth engine. OC Blue is being relaunched with new packaging in UP first; B7 gets a new look in H2 FY27 (packaging rollout targeted Q4 FY27). B10 was named as losing ground.

qa_highlights.question: How will the company reach mid-teens growth given weak non-ICONiQ brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited ABD P&A growth of 11.6% vs industry mid-single digits, the full-year benefit of ICONiQ, brandy push in AP, OC volume in Telangana and AP, and vodka and premium whisky launches in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does ENA capacity suffice for backward integration needs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said captive ENA capacity in Maharashtra and Telangana, plus planned Maharashtra expansion, covers requirements. Its ENA expansion plan is designed to meet needs from captive sources for the next four years.

Steel Cord has a 20,000-tonne pilot and received its first trial order from a leading Indian tire maker; four trials are expected, each taking about two to three months.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 20% for the rest of FY27, with EBITDA growth guided at a similar 20% or more.
EBITDA per kg is expected to stay around INR 7-8 a kg after the Q1 disruption.
Capex capped at INR 200-250 crore a year, including FY27; IHT and OHT utilisation targeted at 60-80% by year-end.
Speciality target of about INR 2 lakh tonnes of capacity, with EBITDA of INR 600-800 crore on INR 2,000-2,500 crore of investment (per management's math).
Target of 25% ROCE in the current business over a short period.
Operating cash flow target of INR 350 crore for FY27, per management.
capex_capacity: Total installed capacity is about 680,000 tonnes; FY27 started with 680,000 tonnes plus 60,000 tonnes that can be commissioned as needed.
Management aims to start each year with 20-25% spare capacity and historically runs at 85-90% utilisation.
Sanand facility wire expansion of about 90,000 tonnes is under way; some surplus land there may be sold in part.
Dadri greenfield facility had early hiccups that management says are resolved, and ramp-up is now under way.
OHT wire is expected to commission shortly and be fully operational by year-end.
demand_pricing: Demand is recovering across most sectors, including exports and automotive; management says 2Q and 3Q are seasonally weaker in infra.
Management says the industry grows 7-8% while Bansal has grown about 20% a year over the last two decades.
Speciality: India is 60-65% imported and Bansal targets 45-50% share of that market at full capacity; export is not seen as viable because of raw material cost gaps of INR 10-15 a kg.
IHT EBITDA is about INR 10-20 a kg at optimum utilisation, with 80% of customers already approving the product.
Gas costs rose about 1.5x on a blended basis and had not come down as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: How will margins and growth hold if the geopolitical and oil-price issue persists for several quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management absorbed about INR 5,000 a tonne of consumable cost on firm-price orders for the first 45 days, which took EBITDA down to about INR 2 a kg. Margins have been back at INR 7-8 a kg since about May 15.

qa_highlights.question: Does the company run a cost-plus model, and why did the quarter's margin fall so sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: The model is cost-plus, but about 30-40 days of inventory was tied to fixed-rate orders, so the cost rise hit immediately. New orders were booked at escalated prices from April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book from the first Steel Cord trial customer and when will a firm order come?
qa_highlights.answer: It is only a trial order with no firm order book yet. Four trials are expected, each taking about two to three months, so a firm order could take six to eight months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CFO guidance rise to about INR 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 from about INR 600 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 600 crore figure was a combined two-year target. FY26 delivered about INR 330 crore against a INR 250 crore target, and FY27's target is INR 350 crore, with INR 115 crore already generated in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: What are the IHT and OHT margins and utilisation path?
qa_highlights.answer: IHT is at 35-40% utilisation, targeting about 50% next month. Break-even is at about 60% utilisation, with decent margins at 70-80%. Combined IHT and OHT EBITDA is expected at INR 10-20 a kg.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is capped at INR 200-250 crore a year to support 20-25% volume growth. Management said there will be no unusually high capex year apart from Speciality.

risks_watch: Gas and consumable costs had not eased by the call, and a reversal could create inventory losses on the 30-40 days of stock held at cost.
Volume growth must reach about 145,000 tonnes a quarter over the next three quarters, which implies roughly 85% utilisation.
Receivable and payable days: the company used payables financing and vendor advances, and management plans to cut receivable days.
Speciality ROCE depends on the Steel Cord ramp, which is still in trial stages with no firm order book.
Sanand land: management clarified that the land is not being sold outright, which resolves the earlier confusion over asset-held-for-sale presentation.
544209|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on recovery and growth, with management saying the fundamental challenges are almost over. Management was cautious on Speciality timelines and on pricing, noting "a lot of uncertainty is still remaining" and that Steel Cord is still a long process.
key_quotes: Now as of today, even with all of this crisis today, we see that the demand is there.
We are operating at regular EBITDA with an escalated cost.
Once we reach an optimum capacity utilization, I would say that we can expect similar EBITDA, like we are thinking of Steel Cord or something like that in percentage.
We will cap our CAPEX at about INR 200 crore-INR 250 crore every year to give us runway for each year.

544209|2026-09.headline: Bansal Wire posted record Q2 FY27 revenue of Rs 1,308 crore (+24% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 105 crore, with EBITDA/ton near Rs 8,000 aided partly by inventory gain.
544209|2026-09.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as a record quarter for revenue, EBITDA, PAT and EBITDA per ton, recovering from a Q1 hit from industrial gas disruption and higher input costs. Sales volume was about 1,29,000 tons versus 1,14,609 tons in Q2 FY26, and operating cash flow was Rs 218 crore in the quarter and Rs 339 crore in H1. Management said about Rs 200/ton of EBITDA was a one-time inventory gain and guided to Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2. Raw material (wire rod) shortages hit October output, which management said is a short-term issue.

segments.name: IHT / OHT specialty wire
segments.commentary: IHT wire reached positive EBITDA last quarter; management cites Rs 15,000-20,000/ton EBITDA for the specialty wire group. IHT capacity is 9,000 tons, with 6,000 tons OHT being installed to reach 15,000 tons in one to two quarters.

segments.name: Steel tyre cord
segments.commentary: Current capacity about 20,000 tons, with a goal of 2 lakh tons. Pricing is about Rs 130-140/kg. First trial order received in Q2, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days; commercialisation possible within this year.

segments.name: Bead wire
segments.commentary: Nameplate capacity about 30,000 tons, with 10,000-15,000 tons currently run annually. Management cites Rs 12,000-15,000/ton EBITDA. Approvals not yet started; focus to resume in one to two quarters.

segments.name: LRPC
segments.commentary: Less than 1% of sales. Management said it earns modest margins (about Rs 5,000-8,000/ton typical) due to industry overcapacity.

segments.name: B2C (farming, fencing, poultry)
segments.commentary: About 10-12% of Q2 volumes; management says B2C EBITDA is at least 50% higher than B2B.

guidance_outlook: Volume growth of 20% YoY for H2 FY27 (Q3 and Q4 vs prior-year H2); management said Q1 losses cannot be recovered.
EBITDA per ton guidance of Rs 7,000-7,500/ton for H2 FY27; management said Rs 7,000-8,000/ton is achievable for FY27 barring major geopolitical change.
Operating cash flow target of about Rs 800 crore across FY27 and FY28 combined; about Rs 350 crore already generated in H1 FY27.
Capacity to rise from 6.8 lakh tons to about 8.3 lakh tons by end of next year (60,000 tons Dadri brownfield plus about 90,000 tons Sanand greenfield).
Indicative annual capex of Rs 200-225 crore (also cited as Rs 200-250 crore per year), funded from internal accruals.
Long-term EBITDA/ton target of Rs 8,000-10,000, and above Rs 10,000 as specialty wire scales.
capex_capacity: Dadri: 60,000 tons additional low and high carbon wire capacity, mostly built; capitalisation expected by end of Q3 or Q4 FY27. Also 6,000 tons OHT wire, expected in Q3 or Q4 FY27.

Sanand (southern Gujarat) greenfield: about 90,000 tons of stainless steel and low carbon wire, with about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land (land acquired about a year ago). Some capitalisation expected from next quarter or the quarter after.
CWIP closing balance Rs 177 crore.
Steel tyre cord: 20,000 tons current capacity, with a 2 lakh ton goal; a bigger capex will follow customer approvals.
Management expects 4-5x asset turnover on new capacity.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as healthy across automotive, infra, agriculture, power and transmission, and general engineering. Constraint is raw material supply rather than demand.
Wire rod shortage over the last 1.5-2 months as suppliers shifted output to TMT. Company holds about 1.5 months of inventory; October output was hit at some plants, which management says is now back.
Low carbon was about 55% of volume in Q2 (lower end of 55-60% target), supporting blended margin.
Gas prices are about 2.5x the regular level, passed through to customers. Availability has been stable for about one quarter.

Steel tyre cord India demand is 2.5-3 lakh tons, mostly imported. Management expects radialisation (about 60% in India truck/bus) to drive growth. Management says there is no Indian domestic competitor; Bekaert is the main competitor.
Management says it will cap any single customer at 20-25% of total sales for steel cord.

qa_highlights.question: When will steel tyre cord and IHT/OHT translate into revenue and EBITDA, and what is the EBITDA per ton for specialty wire?
qa_highlights.answer: Steel tyre cord is in trials, with a second trial order expected in 10-15 days and commercialisation possible within the year. Specialty wire EBITDA is about Rs 15,000-20,000/ton, and IHT has turned EBITDA positive.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 EBITDA/ton came from inventory gains, and is Rs 7,000-7,500 conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory gain was about Rs 200/ton, so underlying EBITDA was about Rs 7,800-7,900/ton. Management said its own strategy is Rs 7,000-7,500 and it is not guiding above that.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20% volume growth guidance for H2 only, and is it at risk from raw material shortages?
qa_highlights.answer: It applies to H2 FY27, meaning Q3 and Q4 volumes up 20% YoY. Management said raw material shortages are temporary and that lost days can be made up the following month.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of Sanand and Dadri CWIP and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CWIP is Rs 177 crore, mostly Dadri 60,000 tons. Sanand needs about Rs 150 crore capex excluding land.

qa_highlights.question: Steel cord capacity plan and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity is 20,000 tons, the target is 2 lakh tons, and realisation is about Rs 130-140/kg. Management said a major capex will follow customer approvals.

qa_highlights.question: Is Rs 7-7.5/kg the right base for H2 earnings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs 7,000-7,500/ton is the H2 EBITDA commitment, and a better outcome is possible but not guided.

risks_watch: Raw material (wire rod) availability: shortages in October and supplier breakdowns could cut Q3 and Q4 volumes below the 20% growth guidance.
Gas prices at about 2.5x normal; management says pass-through to customers is in place, but this is a margin risk.
Q2 EBITDA/ton includes about Rs 200/ton inventory gain, so sustainability of the Rs 7,800-8,000 level is uncertain.
Steel cord commercialisation depends on customer approvals; management expects the first two quarters of ramp-up to be slow.
Sanand greenfield and Dadri ramp-up execution; capex may move beyond the stated timelines.
LRPC is loss-making at the margin due to industry overcapacity; management says it is less than 1% of sales.
544209|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on results and guidance, with management saying it prefers to guide conservatively. It was candid about near-term raw material disruption and the Q1 gas hit. Answers on steel cord timelines were more hedged, using phrases such as "hopefully" and "if everything goes well".
key_quotes: We have achieved our highest ever quarterly revenue, EBITDA, and profit after tax.
So, we will rather be a little conservative than not delivering on our guidance.
Sir, our thought process is that we should maintain our margins at about Rs. 7,000 to Rs. 7,500.
In the long run, yes, we would definitely look at Rs. 8,000 to Rs. 10,000.

rows.label: IHT/OHT specialty wire scale-up to 15,000 t

544210|2026-03.headline: Emcure FY26 revenue crossed INR9,204 crore (+16.6%), but Q4 domestic growth slowed to 5.2% on Zuventus disruption; FY27 guided to low-to-mid-teen growth.
544210|2026-03.overview: Emcure reported FY26 revenue of INR9,204 crore (+16.6% YoY), with adjusted PAT up 41% to INR1,008 crore and EBITDA margin up 80 bps to 19.4%. Q4 revenue rose 16.7% to INR2,470 crore, but domestic growth slowed to 5.2% because of attrition and restructuring at the newly consolidated Zuventus business. International markets grew 25.7% in Q4, with Europe and Canada leading. Management said April is on plan and guided FY27 to low-to-mid-teen revenue growth and 75-100 bps of EBITDA margin expansion.

financial_highlights.change: +24.5% YoY; margin up from 18.4% in Q4 FY25
Up YoY due to Manx payouts and Zuventus minority stake buyout

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR4,027 crore (+10%), led by women's health, cardio, CNS and oncology. Q4 revenue INR977 crore (+5.2%) was hit by Zuventus. Management said ex-Zuventus Q4 growth was below 8% and the full-year ex-Zuventus base growth was high single digit.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR5,177 crore (+22.2%). Q4 revenue INR1,493 crore (+25.7%); currency added roughly 7-8% overall, about 11-12% in Europe.

segments.name: Europe
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,850 crore (+25.5%). Q4 revenue INR538 crore (+35.8%), helped by Manx and Amphotericin B. Management expects mid-teens CAGR over the next two years.

segments.name: Canada
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,487 crore (+18.7%). Q4 revenue INR399 crore (+28.6%), driven by market share gains and launches.

segments.name: Rest of World / Emerging markets
segments.commentary: FY26 ROW revenue INR1,840 crore (+21.8%), with ARV and non-ARV both contributing. Q4 emerging markets revenue INR556 crore (+15.5%).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at low-to-mid-teens.
EBITDA margin expansion of 75-100 bps in FY27, assuming stable regulations, macro conditions and no major geopolitical upheaval.
Domestic target: grow faster than industry (8-9% expected), at low double-digits.
FY27 capex guided at roughly INR400-425 crore.
FY27 average currency assumption of INR92/USD.
Gross margin expected to stay around 60% for the full year.
Employee expense growth expected at about 10% in FY27 versus about 7% in FY26.
Canada semaglutide launch via Dr. Reddy's partnership in Quebec, expected around Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at roughly INR400-425 crore.
Field force around 4,000 MRs; about 40% sit in Zuventus. Field productivity rose from INR5.4 lakh to INR7 lakh per MR over two years.
Amphotericin B launched in select European markets in H2 FY26; expansion to Europe and rest of world planned for FY27.
Bevacizumab ophthalmic biosimilar endorsed by CDSCO SEC; launch planned H1 FY27 pending approval.
Lenacapavir: DMF filed; product registration sought in FY27.
demand_pricing: Zuventus: Q4 restructuring (new management after October minority buyout, portfolio and team reorganisation) drove high field attrition; management says April is on plan. Normal MR attrition is 20-30%.

Poviztra (Novo Nordisk rDNA semaglutide, India exclusive): early uptake promising after April 2026 price cut; about 1,000 sales reps promoting it. Management says the product is differentiated versus synthetic generics.
In-licensed products make up about 15% of domestic sales. The Roche nephrology brands (2-3 key brands) are under INR50 crore annualised with no upfront payment.
Market share in covered markets was roughly flat for FY26 after the Q4 impact.

Raw material and solvent prices have risen with the Middle East conflict. Freight and insurance costs are also up. Company holds 1-2 quarters of inventory and says there are no supply issues yet. IPA is seeking a domestic price hike.
Canada: Dr. Reddy's partnership via Mantra subsidiary in Quebec, where pricing is expected to be more favourable. Apotex and Reddy's received semaglutide approvals recently.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify Zuventus impact on India growth and whether restructuring will weigh on the next few quarters.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said full-year ex-Zuventus base growth would have been 9-10%, and Q4 ex-Zuventus was below 8%. It expects the impact to fade, with April back on track.

qa_highlights.question: What operational synergies are expected from Zuventus?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said manufacturing synergies are limited because the plants serve different products. Gains are expected in sales and marketing organisation and support functions.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 domestic growth outlook and the currency assumption behind guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Industry growth is expected at 8-9% and Emcure aims for low double digits. The guidance assumes INR92/USD.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the raw material and geopolitical cost pressure is in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory covers 1-2 quarters, so impact is limited near term. Management said guidance includes current pricing, and the industry is facing solvent and freight cost increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Canada semaglutide path?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Quebec partnership with Dr. Reddy's aims for an early launch around Q2 FY27, and its own filing will target the rest of Canada in the medium term. Deal terms were not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is Emcure open to more in-licensing deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the focus is organic growth but in-licensing will continue where it is accretive.

risks_watch: Zuventus recovery: whether April's on-plan trend holds through Q1 FY27 after high attrition.
Poviztra price war and whether market share recovers after the April 2026 price cut.
Raw material, solvent, freight and insurance inflation if the Middle East conflict persists beyond the 1-2 quarters of inventory.
Rising debt (net debt INR1,054 crore) after the Manx and Zuventus payouts.
Q4 Mantra earn-out exceptional charge of INR43 crore, which was above initial expectations.
Currency: a weaker rupee supports international revenue, but the INR92/USD assumption needs monitoring.
544210|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and optimistic on FY27 and on the Zuventus recovery, though Q4 domestic softness was openly acknowledged. Management was noticeably evasive on monthly April growth and on the semaglutide market-share recovery. It was also cautious on cost pressures, saying the impact is hard to quantify.
key_quotes: FY26 marked the start of our 5-year strategy, focusing on turning last year's operational changes into measurable outcomes.
Ex of the Zuventus impact for the full year would have been close to the 9% - 10% base business growth that we have been talking about, that we delivered even in the first 9 months.
I think we continue to expect industry growth to be around 8% to 9% , and for us, the target, is to grow faster than the industry – probably at low double-digits.

In FY27, we project low to mid -teen revenue growth and as I have been explaining in the last meet and a few calls that I have had the privilege of addressing to you guys that EBITDA margin expansion will happen as committed between 75 to 100 basis points going forward, assuming stable regulations and macroeconomic conditions.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided 75-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion in FY27 after FY26 margin of 19.4% (+80 bps), with gross margin held near 60% and employee cost growth of about 10% vs about 7% in FY26; raw material and freight inflation is a watch item.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to low-to-mid-teens (midpoint about 12.5%) with domestic targeted at low double-digits vs industry 8-9%, and International +25.7% in Q4 led by Europe +35.8% and Canada +28.6%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex of INR400-425 crore is already guided, but no new capacity or utilisation figure was disclosed, so no further capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was set as a fresh low-to-mid-teen range with April described only as on plan; no sign of a beat that would prompt a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ex-Zuventus Q4 growth was below 8% with high field attrition (normal 20-30%), and raw material, solvent and freight costs are rising with only 1-2 quarters of inventory cover, while net debt rose to INR1,054 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Bevacizumab ophthalmic biosimilar launch planned H1 FY27 pending approval, Canada semaglutide via Dr. Reddy's in Quebec around Q2 FY27, and Amphotericin B expansion to Europe and RoW planned for FY27.

rows.label: Zuventus recovery after Q4 restructuring
rows.why: Ex-Zuventus full-year base growth was 9-10% and Q4 ex-Zuventus below 8%; management says April is on plan, but monthly April growth was not quantified and field attrition was high.

rows.label: Poviztra semaglutide uptake after April 2026 price cut
rows.why: About 1,000 sales reps are promoting Poviztra and early uptake is called promising, but management was evasive on market-share recovery and the price war risk is open.

rows.label: IPA domestic price hike for raw material inflation
rows.why: Solvent and freight costs are rising with the Middle East conflict and the industry body is seeking a domestic price hike, but no approval is confirmed and inventory covers only 1-2 quarters.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance, the Zuventus recovery and International growth, but was evasive on April monthly growth and semaglutide share recovery and cautious on cost pressures; analysts focused on Zuventus drag and quantifying it.

544210|2026-06.headline: Emcure Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, with EBITDA of INR 508 crore (19.7% margin) and PAT up 35-36%.
544210|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 22.8% YoY to INR 2,580 crore, led by international markets (up 34.2% to INR 1,485 crore) while India grew 10.2% to INR 1,095 crore. EBITDA rose 25.8% to INR 508 crore with margin up 50 bps to 19.7%, and PAT grew about 36% to INR 292 crore. Gross margin fell to 58.4% on geographic and product mix, and net debt rose to INR 1,103 crore. Management reiterated low-to-mid teens FY27 revenue growth (now toward the higher end) and 70-100 bps EBITDA margin expansion. Board changes were announced: Chairman Berjis Desai retires at AGM and CEO Satish Mehta becomes Chairman; Samit Mehta becomes COO and CEO of Gennova, which is now 100% owned.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,095 crore, +10.2% YoY. Ex-Sanofi OAD and Roche in-licensed brands, growth was about 6-7%. Price contributed about 4-5%, new launches 1-2%. Management says no channel filling in the quarter.

segments.name: Europe

544223|2026-03.headline: Ceigall Q4 FY26 standalone revenue rose 30.5% YoY to INR1,294 crores; FY27 guidance is minimum 15% revenue growth and 11-12.5% EBITDA margin.
544223|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's strongest execution quarter of the year, with standalone revenue of INR1,294 crores (up 30.5% YoY) and standalone EBITDA of INR183 crores (14.1% margin). Full-year standalone revenue grew 14.3% to INR3,869 crores, while FY26 order inflow of INR11,332 crores far exceeded the INR5,000 crore guidance, taking the order book to INR18,554 crores. Management guided FY27 to at least 15% revenue growth, 11-12.5% EBITDA margin and at least INR5,500 crores of order inflow. Working-capital stretch (trade payables and unbilled revenue days both up sharply) and a large pending equity commitment for HAM and renewable projects were the main analyst focus, alongside the INR13,000 crore Romania bid.

544224|2026-03.headline: Afcom Q4 FY26 revenue rose 87.8% YoY to INR191.88 crore and PAT to INR44.66 crore, on war-driven charter demand.
544224|2026-03.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR191.88 crore (+87.8% YoY), EBITDA of INR74.08 lakh per the call (+51.52%), and PAT of INR44.66 crore (+72.85%) under Ind AS. Full-year revenue was INR587.72 crore (+143.86%) and PAT INR121.90 crore (+230.05%), with PAT margin of 20.74%. Growth was driven by stranded-cargo charters after Middle East disruption in March 2026, with 415 of 602 Q4 trips being pure charters. Fleet expansion is the key near-term constraint: a third aircraft is operational, with fourth and fifth expected before the next quarter and wide-bodies (Boeing 777) planned from late 2026.

financial_highlights.change: +72.85% YoY; GAAP PAT was INR46.32 crore

segments.commentary: Q4 dry lease revenue INR160.49 crore; FY26 INR528.71 crore on 1,923 trips and 24,353 tons, with 1,129 pure charters (about one-third in Q4).

Two Boeing 777 wide-body aircraft: one expected operational in the last quarter of FY27 (per the call's timing), with the full four-777 plan expected to be fully operational by mid/second half of calendar 2027.

Management called a 777 revenue of about 3x a 737-800 at 14-15 rotations/month and 75% load factor, implying roughly INR75 crore/month per 777 as a conservative estimate; management said FY27 revenue could be at least double FY26 on existing resources.
ATF pass-through via fuel surcharge; designated carrier status cuts fuel-related VAT, adding about 5-7% benefit to overall fuel cost from the next financial year.

Funding: QIB and preferential allotment (INR200 crore each per analyst) stated to cover wide-body induction; fourth and fifth aircraft costs largely covered, with customs and minor expenses remaining.
demand_pricing: March 2026 saw a sudden capacity withdrawal from Middle East carriers; Q4 month-end revenue ran about INR42-44 crore per month, with March about 22-23% above the Jan-Feb average.

Management said April and May demand remained above average but below March panic levels; fuel prices (ATF) at INR2,24,000/KL were offered at INR1,69,000/KL under designated carrier status, versus INR85,000/KL before.
Q4 yield USD2.72/kg versus IATA industry average cited at INR222/kg; management said company yield per kg is better than the IATA average.
Chennai international cargo grew 12.5% YoY in FY26 versus 5.4% all-India, per management's data.
Over 60% of billing is in USD. Receivables about 60 days on recent billing (IATA norm 45 days); management said no receivables older than 6 months.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for fourth, fifth and wide-body aircraft induction?
qa_highlights.answer: Third aircraft operational; fourth and fifth to be operational before next quarter; one 777 targeted in last quarter of FY27, with four 777s in total per management's later clarification, fully operational by second half of calendar 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of ATF price surge and pass-through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fuel is passed through 100% via fuel surcharge; the market absorbed the April spike, which tapered in May and June; designated carrier status yields a fuel price benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 yield only USD2.72/kg despite higher freight rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher charter share (415 of 602 Q4 trips) and short-sector stranded-cargo flights lowered yield per kg; more weight-based cargo would have raised yield.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue potential of 777 aircraft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 777 can do 14-15 rotations per month at 75% load factor, giving about 3x a 737-800's revenue; an analyst's estimate of about INR75 crore per month per 777 was described as conservative.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 EBITDA margin lower than Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Ind AS adjustments, particularly a large forex loss charged to P&L, and maintenance reserve now expensed.

qa_highlights.question: Ideal FY27 revenue expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said resources would at least double FY26 revenue on a conservative basis; no numerical guidance given.

Revenue dependence on temporary war-driven charter demand; management acknowledged yields hardened in March and the sea-freight alternative is also rising in cost.
Ind AS restatement now shows large forex losses and maintenance reserve charges, which compress reported margins; Q4 EBITDA margin lower than Q3.

544225|2026-03.headline: Ola Electric Q4 FY26 consolidated gross margin rose to 38.5% and first positive operating cash flow (Rs 91 crore CFO), but revenue was low on depressed deliveries.

Revenue was weak because deliveries were depressed by internal service and operations fixes, with FY26 consolidated revenue at Rs 2,253 crore on 173,794 deliveries. Management says registrations have recovered for three months, orders are running ahead of registrations, and Q1 FY27 guidance is 40,000-45,000 orders and Rs 500-550 crore revenue. The Gigafactory's first 3 GWh is in ramp-up with the remaining 3.5 GWh slated for June, and the company is pushing Shakti and Roadster bike growth.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bridge from current volumes to the 20,000 units/month breakeven?

qa_highlights.question: Advantage of own cells versus imported cells?

qa_highlights.question: Why not advertise in print media, and is the Rs 2,000 crore cell monetisation progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Company prefers word-of-mouth and does not do TV or IPL sponsorship; may advertise in coming months. Cell monetisation requires a subsidiary-level capital raise; management has inbound PE interest but gave no timing beyond 'in due course'.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the one-time ASP change and will prior quarters be restated?
qa_highlights.answer: Extended warranty packages moved from upfront to deferred revenue recognition after discussion with auditors, a Rs 20-30 crore impact already baked into published numbers; no restatement of prior quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why are service issues linked to parts unavailability, and why NMC for Shakti?
qa_highlights.answer: Parts were not stocked at service centres and procurement was reactive (20-30 day fulfilment); now stocked locally and procured on forecasts. Shakti uses NMC today and will move to LFP next quarter; Shakti ramp is slower because NMC 46-series goes to Auto.

544226|2026-03.headline: FirstCry Q4 FY26: consol revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr for FY26; Q4 adjusted EBITDA up 18% to ₹118.7 Cr amid India gross margin pressure.
544226|2026-03.overview: Brainbees (FirstCry) reported Q4 and FY26 with consolidated FY26 revenue up 12% to ₹8,547 Cr, adjusted EBITDA up 24% to about ₹486 Cr, and free cash flow positive for the full year. India multi-channel grew 11.4% in Q4 but gross margin fell on diaper price competition from quick-commerce and horizontal players, plus a transitory manufacturing hit from rupee depreciation and crude-linked inputs. Management says the offline channel grew about 15% in Q4 after a product-mix shift, and that RocketBees and Qwik delivery initiatives are lifting service levels, with the benefit expected to show in FY27. International losses fell 35% in FY26 and GlobalBees core categories grew 28%.

segments.name: International (UAE and KSA)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue above $100 million, growing about 10% in FY26; Q4 revenue +9%. Gross margin rose 240 bps for FY26 (470 bps in Q4). Management did not give a timeline for reaching break-even.
