Sambhav affordable ticket size INR17-18 lakh; overall Sambhav ticket size may drift down to INR26-27 lakh from INR28 lakh, with a downward bias of INR1-2 lakh by year-end.
capex_capacity: Network of 224 branches across 182 locations.
Sambhav Housing operational in 73 urban and 72 rural locations; geographic expansion into non-metro markets is a stated strategy.
Assignments run at 12-13% of AUM on a trend basis; Q1 included a large assignment of about INR2,300 crore, which released Stage 1 provisions.
Sambhav mix: 84:16 prime to Sambhav in home loans now, targeted at 80:20 by year-end FY27.
Borrowing mix: money market 52%, bank 38%, NHB refinance 10%; relationships with 18 banks.
demand_pricing: Management sees the industry demand as muted; growth may fall short of the 11-12% usually assumed. Home loan industry grew 9.4% in FY26. Management calls this a stabilisation phase as price momentum has paused.
Acquisition pricing in prime housing has been stable for some time; the company does not expect large-scale upward pricing moves and has not factored them in.
Portfolio attrition in prime home loans is running at a historical book at a higher yield than new business, which pushes yield lower in a stable rate environment.
Balance-transfer-out rate eased slightly in Q1 but remains under watch; the company is holding off on a more confident view until Q2 data.
Fee and commission income growth is linked to disbursement growth through insurance income and foreclosure, bounce and penal charges.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-25 bps FY27 NIM compression, and is there any pricing relief or PLR hike possibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the compression mainly to yield decline: high-yield book is running off while new business comes in at lower yields in a stable rate regime. Acquisition pricing has been stable, and no large-scale upward pricing move is assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q1 credit cost drop to 5 bps? Are there one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, two one-offs: a Q4 FY26 Stage 2 provision build that was not repeated, and a roughly INR2,300 crore assignment that released Stage 1 provisions. Management said to treat it as about 5 bps; the FY27 guide stays at 10-15 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM fall 13-14 bps when spreads were flat and cost of funds fell 7 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: The spread is computed on period-end portfolio yield versus average cost of funds, so it moved only 3-4 bps. The margin decline is from portfolio yield compression, which will continue through FY27 and offset the cost-of-funds benefit.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds outlook for Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds is expected to be sideways in Q2 FY27 with a downward bias, helped by hedging, repayment of older high-cost borrowings and resets of some older borrowings to lower rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the LAP and DF Stage 2 to Stage 3 movement not raising provisions, and is there stress in LAP?
qa_highlights.answer: LAP provisions are formula-based on DPD, so roll-backs and roll-ins net off; the LAP movement was INR18 crore in total, not one account. DF provisioning was already held at 48-49% on the account. Management cited LAP GNPA in a 46-76 bps range over seven quarters and said there is no segment or geography concern.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 provisions stay flat despite a INR7,500 crore rise in Stage 1 assets?
qa_highlights.answer: The annual January ECL recalibration lowered Stage 1 rates on most portfolios because credit performance was stronger, and the mix of new and attrited customers also shifted. Management said there is no simple pool-to-pool calculation.

risks_watch: NIM compression of 20-25 bps for FY27 with Q2-Q3 further declines of 6-10 bps; watch yield on new disbursements vs run-off.
Balance-transfer-out trend in home loans; a sustained easing would support AUM growth, but a reversal would pressure growth.
LAP GNPA at 62 bps, above the 50-70 bps corridor's midpoint trend; check whether the one-week account resolves.
Stage 1 provisioning appears light relative to the Stage 1 book; the credit cost guidance may need to rise to 10-15 bps as one-offs unwind.
Industry demand is muted and the company has said it is not assuming a rise in acquisition pricing; a rise in borrowing costs (MCLR, NCD) could pressure margins.
Opex to net income is expected to remain at 19-20%, so operating leverage is limited in FY27 as margins compress.
Sambhav ticket size and Tier 2/3 expansion may dilute average ticket size and yield; the affordable segment is ramping.

544252|2026-09.headline: Bajaj Housing Finance Q2 FY27: PAT up 18% YoY to INR757 crore, AUM at INR1.58 lakh crore growing 25%, with management flagging ~25 bps NIM compression ahead.
544252|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed AUM crossing INR1.5 lakh crore, disbursements up 25% YoY to INR19,900 crore, and stable asset quality (GNPA 29 bps, NNPA 12 bps). Cost of funds fell 17 bps QoQ to about 7.0% from fixed-to-floating NCD conversion, offsetting a 10 bps portfolio yield decline, so NIM dipped 2 bps to 3.7%. Management said the repo hike will pass through roughly 80% to both liabilities and assets, but acquisition pricing from banks is still unclear and is the main margin and attrition risk. Guidance on AUM growth (21-23%) and NIM compression (~25 bps for the year) was not revised.

segments.commentary: AUM growth 26% YoY. GNPA down 1 bp QoQ to 61 bps; NNPA down 4 bps to 21 bps.

segments.commentary: AUM growth 13% YoY and the book declined QoQ on higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements. GNPA flat at 12 bps; NNPA down 3 bps. Management targets 15-17% of portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Why did developer finance decline QoQ, and what is the strategy for the DF book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said higher repayments from project cash flows plus slower disbursements drove the decline, not a conscious strategy. DF sanctions rose sharply in H1, and the target is 15-17% of the portfolio, with recovery expected in Q3-Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will the repo hikes compress margins and how much pass-through is possible on the prime side?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80-82% of repo hikes flow through to cost of funds and to portfolio pricing, so the main margin risk is on acquisition pricing. If prime acquisition pricing lags, attrition and BT-out rise and the company shifts toward non-prime.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the fall in fee income?
qa_highlights.answer: Fee income rose on higher insurance income (attachment rates higher with Sambhav growth) and higher foreclosure income in the quarter, not a decline. Fee-related expenses are marginal and range-bound.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20 bps cost of funds decline a one-off, and what is the exit COF?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a starting point, not a one-off, though part came from one-time maturity of high-priced borrowings. Three 25 bps hikes would take COF up about 61 bps, from roughly 7% in September to about 7.6% by March.

qa_highlights.question: Why did home loan originations decline QoQ, and what is the YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly movements are seasonal and the company tracks AUM rather than disbursals. Home loan disbursal growth was 24% YoY, close to the company's 25% disbursement growth.

qa_highlights.question: Will guidance be revised given NIM expansion this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no revision for now. NIM compression of about 25 bps is still expected, and AUM growth could slow to 22-23% if acquisition pricing lags, given the rise in BT-out rates.

544253|2026-03.headline: Kross Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, with EBITDA margin at 14.9%; management guides 14-15% margins and FY27 growth near 22%.
544253|2026-03.overview: Kross closed FY26 with revenue of INR 673.2 crore (+8.5%) and PAT of INR 55.2 crore (8.2% margin), after a slow H1 and a stronger H2 (H2 revenue 49.2% above H1). Q4 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 225.4 crore, EBITDA rose 25% to INR 33.6 crore and PAT rose 31% to INR 22.4 crore. Management says the Middle East conflict caused LPG shortages and commodity and consumable cost increases in Q4, with steel price hikes of INR 3-5/kg expected from April and a retrospective OEM pass-through lagging by about one quarter. The company has raised prices about 5% in trailer axles and suspensions and says it has fully deployed IPO proceeds.

544253|2026-09.headline: Kross Q2 FY27 revenue rose 80% YoY to INR235 crore with EBITDA margin of 13%, but reported PAT was a loss of INR19.7 million.
544253|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was INR235 crore, up 80% YoY, with EBITDA of INR30.6 crore (13% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was INR419 crore versus INR270 crore a year earlier, with H1 EBITDA of INR53 crore. Management attributed growth to trailer and CV demand after monsoons, share gains with larger customers, and exports; margins were pressured by steel and consumable cost inflation, with price compensation expected in Q3 and Q4. The seamless tube backward-integration project (budget ~INR170 crore) is progressing, with production trials targeted for Feb-March 2027 (or end Q4 per another answer).

Price revisions with OEMs and Tier 1s on conversion costs expected to support Q3 and Q4; steel compensation partial, with further steel increases expected in Q3.
Receivable days expected to fall to around 80, with working capital cycle below 90-95 days.

demand_pricing: CV demand strong since GST rationalisation; monsoon-related deferment ended around July, with demand picking up in August per management.
Chhattisgarh market recovered after a long gap, contributing to trailer order growth; share gains with larger customers cited.

Rising steel and consumable costs compressed Q2 gross margin versus Q1 despite some price escalation; management says settlements with most OEMs/Tier 1s are underway with retrospective compensation expected.

qa_highlights.question: What drove growth above the industry for trailer axles and component segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited the post-monsoon demand pickup from August, share gains with larger customers, new regional demand (e.g. Chhattisgarh), and export growth (~7.5-8% of component business).

qa_highlights.question: Volume and value growth for axles and suspensions in Q2 and H1?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 trailer axles above 10,500 and H1 nearly 20,000, up about 50-55% YoY; trailer value ~INR115 crore in Q2 vs ~INR58-60 crore a year earlier. Suspension volume not disclosed; to be shared later.

544254|2026-03.headline: Tolins Tyres FY26 consolidated revenue rose about 12% to INR327.12 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR47.8 crore and PAT to INR35.69 crore.
544254|2026-03.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR327.12 crore, while EBITDA (excluding other income) declined to INR47.8 crore from INR57.91 crore, with margin at 14.6%. PAT fell to INR35.69 crore from INR38.67 crore, and basic EPS was INR9.03. Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 12% to INR77.99 crore, but Q4 EBITDA fell to INR11.22 crore (14.4% margin) from INR13.57 crore, with PAT of INR8.94 crore. Management attributed the pressure to a GST rate mismatch on retreading materials, higher inventory, longer receivable cycles and West Asia disruption, and gave only a soft FY27 outlook of maintaining FY26 performance.

segments.name: Retreading materials (tread rubber, PCTR)
segments.commentary: Management said about 60% of sales come from tread rubber; retread margins were hit by the GST mismatch (18% on retread materials vs 5% on new agricultural tyres), and dealer off-take fell. Industry association has sought a 5% GST rate on retreads, which the government is reportedly considering.

segments.name: Tyres (incl. agricultural, two-wheeler, tractor rear)
segments.commentary: Tyre production rose to 5,35,870 units in FY26 from 3,93,253 in FY25, about 36% growth, while top-line growth lagged. Utilisation in the Indian tyre segment was about 45%. A new heavy-duty tractor rear tyre has received an encouraging dealer response.

segments.name: UAE operations (Ras Al Khaimah)
segments.commentary: Plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; management said margins are better than India, but GCC demand fell from the last quarter of FY26. Utilisation is expected to drop to 30-40% in the near term before recovering to 40-50%. Receivables are rising in the UAE.

segments.name: Exports, precured tyres and US business
segments.commentary: Management said US business started last year and repeat orders are slowly coming in, with a Europe push under way. Logistics are impacted by the Middle East war. No quantified export revenue was given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: management expects to at least maintain FY26 levels of performance, and will review this after Q2 FY27 depending on how the situation evolves.
Management expects West Asia and India-related disruptions to normalise by end of Q2 FY27 (pricing, raw material and shipping), which would support better Q3 and Q4.
EBITDA margin: management said 10% to 13% is an acceptable range, with a further 2-3% from waste and scrap reduction and operational efficiency.
Management expects a Terra Rubber recycling-linked margin benefit in FY26/FY27 through in-house offtake; no quantified synergy was given.
Management expects capex to be limited this year because existing capacity is sufficient to meet demand, and says the government is likely to correct the GST imbalance.
capex_capacity: Ras Al Khaimah (UAE) plant capacity is 1,200 metric tons, with utilisation below 50%; the plant has been operating for about 10 years.
Indian utilisation is about 45-55%: retread segment about 55% and tyre segment about 45%.
Gujarat depot commenced operations on December 1, 2025, serving tyre and retread products in Western India.
No significant capex is planned for FY27, as existing capacity is sufficient; cost reduction is focused on automation and AI-based planning tools.
Terra Rubber has started manufacturing and processing scrap into products trialled on road; management is scouting acquisitions but nothing is finalised and no numbers were shared.
demand_pricing: Tyre production volume grew 36% YoY in FY26 (5,35,870 vs 3,93,253 units) and PCTR grew about 10%; bonding gum and flaps grew 56%.
The GST cut on new commercial and agricultural tyres (from 28% to 18% and 5%, respectively) left retread materials at 18%, which narrowed retreading's 30-40% price advantage to about 20%.
Q4 tyre volumes fell QoQ due to dealer off-take hesitancy amid war-related uncertainty in March 2026.
Dealer credit was extended by about one month to 4-5 months, with a stated plan to revert to 3-4 months; China dumping in GCC is extending credit terms up to a year.
Management said competition is intense with tyre majors in retreading materials, but it believes its 40-year expertise gives it an edge.

qa_highlights.question: Why was top-line growth only about 12% against the 20% growth previously guided, and how do gross current assets of INR309 crore compare with revenue of INR327 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 20% was an optimistic projection and that actual growth was about 12%. It pointed to 36% growth in tyre volumes, with the gap explained by selling prices.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating cash flow turn positive, and what is the sales and marketing strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said credit periods were extended by about one month due to GST and geopolitical uncertainty, with the aim of reducing them over a few quarters. Management said branding spend is small and that it relies on a strong marketing manager team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and margin of the Ras Al Khaimah UAE plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is 1,200 MT with utilisation below 50%. The CFO said UAE margins are better than India's, and utilisation could fall to 30-40% in the next three months before recovering to 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did margins decline in Q4 and FY26, and when will GST be corrected?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the decline to margin pressure in retreads from the GST imbalance and weaker dealer off-take. The industry body has asked for a 5% retread GST rate, and the government is considering it.

qa_highlights.question: What are the three biggest growth drivers beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to higher tyre production volumes, precured tyres (Europe and the US, where repeat orders are starting), and Terra Rubber integration for in-house raw material offtake.

qa_highlights.question: Why did tyre volumes decline QoQ, and why did working capital rise from about INR230 crore to near INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volumes fell because of March uncertainty. Working capital is driven by 3-4 months of dealer credit, about 4-5 months of inventory across more than 1,200 SKUs and seasonal rubber prices, and government retentions. IPO proceeds were partly used to fund inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 top-line guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects at least to maintain FY26 performance and will review after Q2 FY27, preferring to commit less and perform better.

tone.note: Management was confident on long-term tyre demand (36% volume growth) and the expected normalisation of West Asia and GST issues by Q2 FY27, but cautious on near-term growth and was evasive on specific numbers; analysts pressed on the 20% growth guidance miss, the gap between revenue and working cap

544256|2026-03.headline: P N Gadgil FY26 consolidated revenue crossed INR10,000 crore to INR10,739 crore (+40% YoY); Q4 gross margin fell to 9.7% on a 40% bullion mix.
544256|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR10,739 crore, with full-year gross margin up 280 bps to 12% and EBITDA margin up 180 bps to 6.6%. Q4 revenue grew 123% YoY to INR3,544 crore, but gross margin fell to 9.7% (about 230 bps down YoY) as gold bars and coins rose to 40% of sales, plus one-time discounts and franchise mix. Management attributes the Q4 margin dip to mix and one-offs, and it guided FY27 revenue of INR13,500 crore, EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin 4%, with a review next quarter given the import duty hike.

financial_highlights.change: about -230 bps YoY; gross profit +80% YoY

segments.name: Retail (COCO)
segments.commentary: FY26 retail revenue INR8,131 crore (+51% YoY), SSSG 43%; Q4 retail INR2,600 crore (+102% YoY). Stud ratio for FY26 at 9.9%.

segments.name: Franchise (FOCO)
segments.commentary: FY26 franchise revenue INR1,292 crore (+83% YoY); Q4 INR430 crore (+132% YoY). Franchise gross margin cited at 2.5-3%.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR529 crore (+105% YoY); Q4 INR152 crore (+67% YoY).

segments.name: Other segments
segments.commentary: Q4 contribution INR357 crore; includes gold bars and coins, which carry roughly 0.5-1% gross margin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance INR13,500 crore, versus the earlier INR12,000-12,500 crore reference; retail AOP about INR9,800 crore (+23% on about INR8,000 crore).
FY27 EBITDA margin 7-7.5% and PAT margin about 4%; gross margin guidance 12-13%, which management says is unchanged.
Guidance to be updated next quarter depending on how market conditions evolve.
Bars and coins expected at about 25% of sales in FY27 (FY26: about 32%); the import duty hike is expected to cut that segment by 20-22% of total sales.
FY27 store plan of 25 new stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO (about 20 franchise), mostly outside Maharashtra (Gurgaon, Lucknow/UP, Gujarat).
Hedging target raised to 75-80% in FY27 (67% at end-Q4 FY26, about 60% average for FY26).
capex_capacity: 78 stores across 36 cities at 31 March 2026; 25 stores added in FY26, including 12 in Q4 (8 COCO, 4 FOCO).
Non-Maharashtra stores contribute about 10% of business; UP, Bihar and MP stores reached about 1x annualised stock turn in year one, against a 0.8x guidance.
Average revenue per store INR137.7 crore; revenue per sq ft INR4,51,000; net profit per store INR5.25 crore; inventory turnover 3.8x.
Management says it does not plan many COCO stores in FY27, favouring the asset-light franchise model.
QIP enabling board resolution valid until end of August 2026; management says the QIP is not needed for growth. Promoter shareholding must reach 75% by September 2027.
demand_pricing: Q4 event sales: Foundation Day INR365 crore, Gudi Padwa INR171 crore (+38% YoY), Gratitude Day INR225 crore.
Q4 volumes: gold +27% YoY, silver +37%, diamond +125%, despite a sharp gold price run.
Old gold exchange about 40% of business, targeted at 50%+; make-to-order about 30-35% (22% outside Maharashtra vs 30-32% in Maharashtra).
Average transaction value above INR1 lakh in FY26.

Q4 gross margin hit by about 150 bps from bars and coins (INR450 crore to INR1,400 crore; Q3 INR1,100 crore), about 100 bps from lower stud mix, and INR40-45 crore of making-charge discounts (INR399/gram), plus INR50 crore+ of promotional and trade discounts. Franchise sales rose about INR200 crore QoQ.
Gains from the unhedged portion: INR7.4 crore in Q4 FY25, INR45 crore in Q3 FY26, INR20 crore in Q4 FY26.
Management says the import duty and the advance authorisation scheme do not apply to its domestic business; the duty is passed to consumers.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the customs duty hike and advance authorisation on sales and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the advance authorisation targets exporters, so it does not apply. The duty is passed to consumers, with no margin impact; it may shift demand from bars and coins toward exchanging old gold for jewellery.

qa_highlights.question: Hedging levels for FY26 and the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedging was 57% in Q4 FY25, 63% in Q3 FY26 and 67% in Q4 FY26, averaging about 60% for FY26. The target is 75-80% in FY27, held back by MCX margin and premium costs of 15-20% that tied up cash.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY27 revenue guidance raised from INR12,000 crore to INR13,500 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FY26 beat the INR9,500 crore guidance by about INR1,000 crore. Management cites non-Maharashtra demand (about 10% of business) and strong same-store growth, which pushed the range up to INR13,500 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why are the margin drivers one-off rather than structural, given likely repeat discounts and franchise growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the discounts were one-time events worth about 0.5% of Q4 sales. Bars and coins (40% of Q4 sales) drove most of the dip, and it expects that mix to normalise to about 25%.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin split between bars and coins and jewellery?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins earn 0.5-1% gross margin; plain gold jewellery earns 12.5-13%. Franchise gross margin is about 2-3%, nearly net margin since the franchisee bears all costs.

qa_highlights.question: Inventory turnover decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributes the 3.8x FY26 turnover to about 8 COCO stores opened in Q4 that have not matured. It says turnover has been broadly flat, declining slightly over two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 store additions and non-Maharashtra plans?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan of 25 stores: 5-7 COCO and the balance FOCO, mostly outside Maharashtra (UP, Bihar, MP, Gujarat, Gurgaon). Demand for franchises is strong and under evaluation.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year bars and coins share and promoter shareholding timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Bars and coins were about 32% of FY26 sales. The promoter must reach 75% by September 2027, three years after the September 2024 listing.

risks_watch: Q4 gross margin at 9.7% versus 12-13% guidance; management says the mix shift will normalise, but its explanation of one-offs has been challenged.
Import duty hike may reduce bars and coins demand (20-22% of sales); whether jewellery exchange offsets it is unproven, and management said it is too early to quantify FY27 volume.
Hedging at 67% is short of the 75-80% target; MCX margin costs and unhedged gains affect margin volatility.
Franchise mix rising (FOCO margins about 2-3%) could weigh on gross margin as the network expands.
Inventory turnover fell to 3.8x as new stores ramp; the new-market ramp needs watching.
Promoter shareholding must reach 75% by September 2027; the QIP enabling resolution lapses end-August 2026.
544256|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the full-year result and the FY27 guidance, but defensive on Q4 margins: management repeatedly ties the drop to bars and coins and one-off promotions and says it is not structural. It was less specific on FY27 volume, the QIP and hedging costs, and said it would update guidance next quarter.
key_quotes: So, the three factors primarily which can identify to this are higher share of gold bars and coins in the overall sales mix.
We therefore view the gross margin impact as largely one-time and mix-driven, not structural, and remain focused on improving product mix and margins as our stores mature.
So, we feel looking at these positives, you know, we feel that INR12,500 can be stretched to INR13,500, and that's where the guidance is coming from.
The business is self-sufficient.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 gross margin guided 12-13% and EBITDA margin 7-7.5% versus FY26 EBITDA margin of 6.6%, but Q4 gross margin was 9.7% and management will review guidance next quarter after the import duty hike, with bars and coins expected to fall from about 32% to about 25% of sales.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: FY27 (25 new stores: 5-7 COCO, about 20 FOCO)
rows.why: 78 stores at 31 March 2026 after 25 added in FY26 (12 in Q4); FY27 plan of 25 stores, mostly outside Maharashtra, though management says it does not plan many COCO stores and favours asset-light franchise.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided to INR13,500 crore (about +26% on INR10,739 crore) with Q4 same-store sales growth of 86% YoY and Q4 gold volumes +27%, though bars and coins are expected to drop 20-22% of total sales after the duty hike and management said it is too early to quantify FY27 volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says the QIP is not needed for growth, does not plan many COCO stores in FY27 and favours asset-light franchising, so no major capex is signalled; capacity utilisation is not disclosed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance was already raised to INR13,500 crore from INR12,000-12,500 crore, and management will update guidance next quarter depending on market conditions, with the import duty hike a headwind.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q4 gross margin of 9.7% sits below the 12-13% FY27 guide, bars and coins fell 20-22% of sales after the duty hike, and hedging is 67% against a 75-80% target with MCX margin costs of 15-20% tying up cash.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or molecule launch was discussed in the brief.

rows.label: Q4 margin one-offs (bars/coins mix, making-charge and promo discounts) reverse
rows.why: Bars and coins rose to INR1,400 crore in Q4 from INR1,100 crore in Q3 (about 150 bps of margin hit), plus INR40-45 crore making-charge discounts and INR50 crore+ promotional discounts; management expects bars and coins to normalise to about 25% of sales, but this is unproven.

rows.label: Franchise mix drag on gross margin
rows.why: Franchise revenue rose 83% to INR1,292 crore in FY26 with gross margin of 2.5-3%, and about 20 FOCO stores are planned for FY27, which dilutes blended gross margin.

rows.label: QIP enabling resolution lapses and promoter stake to 75% by Sept 2027
rows.why: Board QIP resolution valid only until end-August 2026 and management says it is not needed for growth, while promoter holding must reach 75% by September 2027.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY26 results and FY27 guidance of INR13,500 crore and 7-7.5% EBITDA margin, but defensive on Q4 gross margin of 9.7%, attributing it to bars and coins mix and one-offs; it was less specific on FY27 volume after the duty hike, the QIP and hedging costs.

544256|2026-06.headline: PNG Jewellers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, with EBITDA up 57% to INR192.4 crore and PAT up 52% to INR105.3 crore.
544256|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 41% YoY to INR2,413 crore, driven by retail (up 56%, with 46% SSSG), franchise (up 8%) and e-commerce (up 20%). EBITDA margin expanded 80 bps to 8.0% and PAT margin rose 40 bps to 4.4%, with gross margin flat at 13.2% reported. Management kept FY27 guidance (around 25 store additions to 103 stores, about 7% EBITDA margin, about INR400 crore other expenses) and flagged that Q1 other expenses were low due to cuts in marketing and no store launches. Hedging gains and lower other income were discussed in detail, and the promoter stake and franchise economics drew scrutiny.

financial_highlights.change: Reported gross margin flat YoY; adjusted ex-hedging up ~40-50 bps per CFO
vs ~INR12 crore in Q4 FY26 (analyst cited INR31 crore, CFO disputed); lower FD balances on mortgage

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Grew 56% with 46% SSSG; now about 78% of total revenue, with jewellery about 78-79% of retail and bars/coins about 20-21%. Newer North and Central India stores run 15-18% studded ratios.

segments.name: Franchise
segments.commentary: Grew 8% YoY; management attributed the slowdown to B2B billing timing and stock replenishment, with franchise openings expected to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle planned).

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: Grew 20% YoY; company is deliberately shifting mix towards jewellery and away from bars/coins, so management expects better margins but slower total sales growth.

segments.name: Litestyle by PNG
segments.commentary: Studded ratio 32.9% in Q1; current litestyle gross margin of about 18-20%, with management targeting about 50% studded ratio in two years and 30-35% margin later.

guidance_outlook: Open around 25 stores in FY27, taking network to about 103 by March 2027 (63 COCO, balance FOCO); a few launches in Q2, bulk in Q3-Q4.
Network targets: about 140 stores by March 2028 and about 177 by March 2029 (about 113 legacy and 64 litestyle; about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO by March 2029).
EBITDA margin guidance of about 7% for full year FY27; other expenses about 3% of sales or roughly INR400 crore for FY27.
PAT margin underlying (ex-hedging gains) targeted at 4.1-4.25% in FY27 per CFO, versus 4.2% per CEO; 4.5-4.7% by FY29.
Hedging coverage to reach about 80% around Q3 FY27 (Q2 around 80% per CEO), and fully hedged in FY28; currently 70%+.
Gold metal loan of INR1,500-1,550 crore to be reduced by INR500-600 crore by FY29, non-GML borrowing about INR1,200 crore; targeted debt-free in four to five years.
Gross margin guidance for retail mix of 13-14% (CFO: 12.5-13.5% at 10-11% studded ratio), including hedging gains shown separately.
capex_capacity: Store count 78 at end-Q1 FY27 (57 COCO, 21 FOCO).
FY27 plan: 25 new stores, bulk in Q3 and Q4, franchise-led; deepening Maharashtra and expanding UP, Bihar, Central India and NCR.
UP stores running 18%+ studded versus 15% projection; 8-10 UP franchise openings planned in FY27; Ayodhya store opening soon.
Capital allocation focused on store expansion, franchise network, digital and operational excellence, funded from internal accruals.
Management plans a QIP at a suitable time to reduce promoter holding (above 75%); board enabling resolution already in place.
demand_pricing: Management said demand held up through April-June despite record gold prices, supported by weddings and Akshaya Tritiya; Adhik Maas was muted due to high silver prices.
Weddings postponed by Adhik Maas expected to benefit Q2 and a large part of Q3.
Customers shifting towards lightweight jewellery, studded products and old gold exchange, favouring organised players.
Hedging gains: Q3 FY26 about INR45 crore, Q4 FY26 about INR20 crore, Q2 FY26 about INR5.5-6 crore; gains shrinking as hedging coverage rises.
Marketing kept within 1.5% of sales; 250-300 hoardings cut versus last year. FY26 other expenses included about INR40-50 crore for UP launch and one-time campaigns that are not expected to recur.
Inventory turns stabilised at about 3.5-4x after refinery and B2B sales wound down (previously about 7x).

qa_highlights.question: Why is gross margin flat YoY despite mix shift toward retail, and what is the ideal retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Reported gross margin is flat because hedging gains are shown separately; ex-hedging adjusted gross margin is up about 40-50 bps YoY. Management targets 12.5-13.5% retail margin at a 10-11% studded ratio, and 13-14% overall retail gross margin including hedging gains.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow only about 5% despite store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited conservative spending amid demand uncertainty, lower scheme-redemption discounts, marketing kept within 1.5% of sales with 250-300 hoardings cut, and no store launches in Q1. Spending will rise in Q3-Q4 with expansion, but EBITDA guidance is still expected to be met.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 other expense guidance and why was other income so different between Q4 and Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses are guided at about 3% of sales, roughly INR400 crore for FY27. Other income was about INR10 crore in Q1 versus about INR12 crore in Q4 per the CFO, who said lower fixed deposits placed on mortgage drove the decline; cash and hedging margin money also hold some balances.

qa_highlights.question: What is the store expansion and COCO/FOCO mix plan through FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Plan adds 25 stores in FY27 to reach 103 (63 COCO, balance FOCO), then 37 each in FY28 and FY29 to reach 140 and 177. By March 2029, about 75 COCO and 40 FOCO, with 113 legacy and 64 litestyle stores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory and hedging plan?
qa_highlights.answer: PAT margin underlying ex-hedging is targeted at 4.1-4.25% in FY27 per the CFO, versus about 4.2% per the CEO; 4.5-4.7% by FY29. Hedging is about 70%+ now, targeted at about 80% around Q3 FY27 and fully hedged in FY28. Hedging gains were about INR45 crore in Q3 FY26, INR20 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR5.5-6 crore in Q2 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: How is Litestyle progressing on studded mix, gross margin and store count?
qa_highlights.answer: Studded ratio is about 32.9-34% now, targeted at about 50% in a couple of years. Current litestyle gross margin is about 18-20%, versus 30-35% for the format once studded mix rises. Litestyle store target is 65-70 by March 2029 and about 100 over the longer term.

qa_highlights.question: Why are franchise revenue growth (8%) and e-commerce growth lower than company-operated stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Franchise sales are booked as B2B, so initial stocking and replenishment timing affect quarterly numbers; management expects franchise openings to pick up in Q2-Q3 (about 10 legacy and 5 litestyle). E-commerce is deliberately shifting mix away from bars and coins toward jewellery, so margins should improve but total sales growth may slow.

risks_watch: Reported gross margin flat YoY; expansion of hedging gains is shrinking as hedging coverage rises toward 80% by Q3 FY27 and full coverage in FY28, so reported margin depends on underlying retail mix.
Other expenses are guided to rise in Q3-Q4 with store openings; Q1 spend (about 5% growth) was unusually low, so H2 cost run-rate against about INR400 crore guidance needs monitoring.
Franchise revenue growth of 8% versus company-operated retail growth of 56%; visibility into franchise B2C sell-through is still being built and management has only recently gained system access.
Promoter holding above 75% with a QIP planned at a suitable time; timing and size are not specified and the stock overhang remains.
Gold metal loan of INR1,500-1,550 crore to fall by INR500-600 crore by FY29; execution of the debt-reduction path and the litestyle studded-mix shift (from about 34% toward 50%) are key checkpoints.

Other income fell to about INR10 crore from about INR12 crore in Q4 per the CFO, after the analyst cited INR31 crore; the figure was disputed on the call and should be reconciled against the filed numbers.
key_quotes: Their confidence has enabled us to deliver our highest ever first quarter, beginning FY27 on a strong note.
Despite elevated gold prices, our performa nce remains in line with our previously communicated guidance.
So franchise apple-to-apple on a quarter-to-quarter, these differences which will come, but having said that, we understand because franchise is our focus now, will be becoming big.
Eventually, we plan to take it to 80% studded inventory at a store le vel and 20% gold inventory and that would also enable us to reach a 50% to 60% studded ratio in that category.
544256|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on demand, store expansion and the long-term plan, with precise targets given across FY27-FY29. Cautious and somewhat evasive on the reasons for flat gross margin and the other income gap, leaning on adjusted (ex-hedging) figures and deferring some answers to later quarters.

rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 80 bps to 8.0% in Q1 and ex-hedging gross margin is up 40-50 bps, with FY27 EBITDA guided at about 7% and PAT margin targeted at 4.1-4.25% ex-hedging for FY27 and 4.5-4.7% by FY29, but hedging gains (Q3 FY26 about INR45 crore, Q4 FY26 about INR20 crore) are shrinking as coverage rises toward 80%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: bulk in Q3-Q4 FY27, a few in Q2 FY27
rows.why: Store count of 78 at end-Q1 FY27 with about 25 openings guided for FY27 to reach 103 (63 COCO, balance FOCO), a 32% addition to the network, and a roadmap to 140 by March 2028 and 177 by March 2029.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail revenue grew 56% with 46% SSSG and store adds are coming in H2, though franchise grew only 8% and e-commerce 20%, and management is deliberately trading total e-commerce sales for margin.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed beyond store expansion funded from internal accruals, and no utilisation figure is given, so a new capex announcement is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

rows.why: Other expenses are guided to about INR400 crore for FY27 and are back-end loaded with store openings, and gains from hedging shrink as coverage moves from 70%+ to about 80%, so the reported margin path depends on the retail mix.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Litestyle studded ratio is 32.9% against a 50% target in two years, and Ayodhya store opening is soon, though no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Gold metal loan reduction and debt path

rows.label: QIP to reduce promoter holding above 75%
rows.when: at a suitable time, not specified
rows.why: Board enabling resolution is in place, but timing and size are unspecified and promoter holding is above 75%.

rows.label: Festive and wedding-led demand recovery in Q2-Q3
rows.why: Weddings postponed by Adhik Maas expected to benefit Q2 and much of Q3, and Akshaya Tritiya bars and coins sales rose 80.3% to INR251.4 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, store expansion and the FY29 targets, but cautious and somewhat evasive on flat reported gross margin and the other income gap (INR10 crore vs analyst's INR31 crore), leaning on ex-hedging figures; analysts pushed on hedging gains, franchise economics and promoter

544256|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR2,666 crore and EBITDA 57% to INR224.6 crore, with margin up 186 bps to 8.4%.
544256|2026-09.overview: P N Gadgil reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR2,660-2,666 crore (up 22% YoY), EBITDA of INR224.6 crore (8.4% margin) and PAT of INR121.1 crore (4.5% margin), with profit growing roughly twice as fast as revenue. Retail grew 31% with SSSG of 25.5%, while e-commerce fell 84% after the company cut low-margin coin sales. Management said about INR200 crore of Navaratri sales shifted from Q2 into Q3 this year, and the company completed the Silvostyle acquisition on 1 October. Gross margin was down 50 bps QoQ, which management attributed to franchisee share rising to 17% from 12%.

financial_highlights.change: +32% YoY; margin +89 bps YoY, -50 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (excl. INR5 crore unhedged inventory gain)

financial_highlights.value: Revenue INR5,079 crore; PAT INR226.5 crore

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail revenue INR2,061 crore, 77% of total (72% a year ago); stud ratio 11.9% vs 9% a year ago and 10.96% in Q1. Gold bars and coins fell to 15.8% of retail revenue from about 22%.

segments.name: Franchisee
segments.commentary: Franchisee revenue grew 35% YoY; franchisee share of revenue rose to 17% from 12%.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-com revenue fell 84% YoY as low-margin coin sales were deliberately reduced in favour of jewellery.

segments.name: Diamond and gold jewellery
segments.commentary: Diamond jewellery value +21% and volume +11%; gold jewellery value +47% and volume +4%. Gold bar and coin value -24%, volume -48%.

segments.name: Northern and Central India
segments.commentary: Share of retail revenue from these regions rose to 2.7% from 0.7%; seven company-owned stores there show a stud ratio of 17.4%.

guidance_outlook: Open about 23 new stores in FY27 (8-10 in Q3, rest in Q4), taking the total to about 103 stores by year-end; 80 stores at quarter end (79 India, 1 US).
FY27 company revenue target of INR13,000 crore-plus; PAT margin guidance of 4.0-4.2%.
Three-year aspiration of about INR17,000 crore revenue by FY29 (25% CAGR FY27-29); another estimate of about INR21,000 crore by FY29 was given in the Q&A.
Stud ratio to rise to 17-18% at company level and newer geographies to reach 30-35% of sales by FY30 (Maharashtra currently about 91%).
Debt to fall 20-25% by FY29-FY30; the 170-odd store target by FY29 to be funded from internal accruals.
Hedge coverage raised to about 80%.
From FY28, store openings to split 50-50 between COCO and FOCO (franchise-owned); about 30-35 stores planned for the next year.
capex_capacity: Ayodhya store operational; Prayagraj store scheduled to open 4 November 2026.

UP stores (about 4 COCO stores in Lucknow, Kanpur, Gorakhpur, Banaras, plus Patna and Indore) averaging 11-12 months old, with stock turn about 1.1x and revenue run-rate about INR60 crore per store versus INR50-55 crore plan; target 8-10 UP stores by end FY27.
Mature-store targets for new regions: 2.5-3x stock turn, rising to 3.5-4x after year 4; revenue about INR200 crore per mature store; stud ratio 22-25%.
Inventory for new-region stores is about 10% of Maharashtra gold volume because they are stud-led.
Typical Maharashtra store carries gold inventory of about INR50-55 crore, roughly 30-32 kg.
Silvostyle acquired 100% on 1 October; it already runs 18 stores and about 68 shop-in-shops.
demand_pricing: Q2 is seasonally subdued (Chaturmas), but management said demand stayed healthy; customers shifted to lightweight, studded and old gold exchange.
Footfalls above 1.78 lakh, conversion 88.6%, average transaction value INR1.22 lakh.
Management said Navaratri was good, Diwali bookings are strong and prices are soft, which should lift volumes.
Gold-bar-to-jewellery conversion improved to 68% from 53% in Q1.
Made-to-order share is 22-25% in UP versus 30-32% in Maharashtra.
Management said without gold price increases mature-store SSSG is in the single digits (7-8%).

qa_highlights.question: Was there a festive shift affecting gross margin, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Navaratri moved from Q2 last year into Q3 this year; about INR200 crore of revenue from the 10 days shifted. The 50 bps QoQ gross margin dip was attributed to franchisee mix rising to 17% from 12%.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be allocated across franchise, COCO and new brands?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is FOCO-led in Q3-Q4; from FY28 the split is 50-50 COCO/FOCO for both legacy and YOOU. Internal accruals are expected to fund COCO expansion, and debt is to fall 20-25% by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: How mature stores in UP are performing (turns, stud ratio, margin)?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock turn is about 1.1x (plan was 1x), revenue about INR60 crore per store (plan INR50-55 crore), stud ratio above 17% (plan 15%), gross margin about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path for YOOU inventory turn and why did legacy turn fall to 3.7x?
qa_highlights.answer: YOOU is about 70% diamond and 30% gold, with a target of 1.8-2x turns at maturity against 0.8x now. Management said legacy turns of 3.7-4x are well above the 2-2.5x industry norm and are sustainable as new stores mature.

qa_highlights.question: How will the QIP proceeds and borrowing be deployed?

544258|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, but EBITDA margin slipped to 5.0% as Middle East crisis cut EXIM volumes 11% QoQ.
544258|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew about 4% QoQ to INR496 crore, the fourth straight quarter of sequential growth. EBITDA fell from INR27 crore to INR25 crore, with margin down from 5.6% to 5.0%, and PAT dropped from INR10.8 crore to INR8.3 crore. Total containers handled were 57,754, up 4.3% YoY but down 7% QoQ, with EXIM down 10.96% QoQ and domestic almost flat. For FY26, containers rose 6.14% to 2,26,578, and management attributed the shortfall from double-digit growth to the March disruption from the Strait of Hormuz closure.

segments.commentary: Q4 volume 23,350 containers, up 17.79% YoY and down less than 1% QoQ, helped by pivots to chemicals, FMCG, aggregates and salt. FY26 volume 86,353, up 8.16% YoY.

544258|2026-06.headline: Western Carriers Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% YoY to INR465 crores, with PAT of about INR9 crores and domestic TEUs up 37%.
544258|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew about 12% YoY to INR465 crores from INR416 crores, with EBITDA of about INR19 crores (4.1% margin) and PAT of about INR9 crores, up about 13% QoQ. Total container throughput of 58,261 TEUs beat Q4 FY26 (57,754) for the first time, driven by domestic volumes up 37% YoY while EXIM grew only 3.2%. Management attributed EXIM weakness to Middle East war-linked vessel disruption and freight rate spikes, and said working capital days fell from 120 to about 111 and debt declined from INR217 crores to about INR197 crores since March. Analysts pressed on the lack of price pass-through, weak cash generation and receivables; management did not commit to a price hike.

544260|2026-03.headline: Northern Arc posted record Q4FY26 PAT of INR133 crore (up 251% YoY) and FY26 PAT of INR406 crore, with AUM at INR16,594 crore (up 22% YoY).
544260|2026-03.overview: Northern Arc reported its highest-ever quarterly profit of INR133 crore in Q4FY26, taking FY26 PAT to INR406 crore (up 33% YoY). AUM grew 22% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR16,594 crore, with direct-to-customer (D2C) at 59% of AUM. Credit cost fell to 2.2% in Q4 (from 3.5% in Q3) and 2.8% for FY26, helped by the RBI's FLDG-related ECL clarification, which management said contributed a one-off benefit. Management guided FY27 AUM growth of 22-25% and ROA above 3%, with ROE in the mid-to-late teens over 8-10 quarters.

FY26 -48 bps YoY; incremental vs 9.3% a year ago

segments.commentary: AUM above INR5,000 crore, growing about 50% in the year per analyst; 70% repeat customers; risk-adjusted yield targeted at 15-16%; ROA stated as upward of about 4%. Short-tenure book reduced to near zero, and an APR cap introduced.

segments.commentary: Portfolio INR3,691 crore, up about 43% YoY, with 17 new branches in FY26. X-bucket collection efficiency 99.4% in March 2026; average ticket INR11-15 lakh; yield 17-18%.

segments.commentary: AUM INR1,009 crore (+8% QoQ); record quarterly disbursement about INR305 crore (+17% QoQ); 64 branches added, network about 342; X-bucket collection efficiency 99.6%. MFI is 6% of AUM; 84% of MFI book covered under CGFMU.

segments.commentary: FY26 placement volume INR11,834 crore with placement fee income up 22% YoY to INR31 crore; credit fund AUM INR3,092 crore earning about INR38 crore fee in FY26. Securitisation placed about INR10,000 crore last year.

Target ROA of 3%+ and ROE of mid-to-late teens within 8-10 quarters (analyst recap of 15-17% in about two to two and a half years was accepted by management as 15-17%).
FY27 credit cost guided at 2.7-2.8%, after adjusting for FLDG benefit and INR66 crore management overlay.

qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 22-25% AUM growth (about 3x GDP) and a 3%+ ROA target, with mid-to-late teens ROE in 8-10 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk building in MSME merchant lending and consumer finance, which grew about 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer finance is underwritten via scorecards with a 15% risk-adjusted return; MSME average ticket is INR11-15 lakh, yield 17-18%, all with 100% registered mortgage. Management acknowledged the small base inflates growth rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ECL coverage fallen, particularly Stage 2 and Stage 3?
qa_highlights.answer: The RBI FLDG clarification (Feb 2026) let the company count FLDG cover in ECL; over 50% of Stage 2 is FLDG-covered. Stage 3 is now mainly secured MSME, given 100% write-off of unsecured loans at 90 DPD.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cost of funds and NIM given rate movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-rate share rose from about 30% to 40%; incremental CoF 8.7% vs 9.3%; management expects to hold 8.5-8.6% and NIM to expand as D2C mix rises to 65%. Management expects RBI rate increases in the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield is 15-16% risk-adjusted; short-tenure book cut to near zero; APR cap introduced; no partner concentration figure given in the call.

544263|2026-03.headline: KRN Heat Exchanger FY26 standalone total income rose 57.36% to Rs.689.95 crore; Q4 standalone net profit up 22.69% to Rs.16.87 crore.
544263|2026-03.overview: FY26 standalone total income grew 57.36% YoY to Rs.689.95 crore, with EBITDA up 19.41% to Rs.84.79 crore and net profit up 42.11% to Rs.71.31 crore. Consolidated FY26 total income was Rs.609.81 crore (+38.06%), EBITDA Rs.112.48 crore (+59.52%) and net profit Rs.76.47 crore (+44.62%). Q4 consolidated EBITDA rose 77.56% to Rs.33.55 crore, while Q4 standalone total income rose 55.06% to Rs.204.93 crore. Management said the new Neemrana HVAC facility is still ramping up, with working capital building in inventory and receivables, and a board-approved enabling fund raise of up to Rs.500 crore whose objective is not yet finalised.

financial_highlights.value: Around 3x YoY (per analyst question, not disputed)

segments.name: Heat exchangers (fin and tube, KRN Heat Exchanger)
segments.commentary: Management said the old facility was fully utilised in FY26; fin and tube still accounts for about 95% of revenue, with other products about 5%. Fin and tube growth expected above 80-90%, mainly from data centres.

segments.name: HVAC / new facility (KRN HVAC Products)
segments.commentary: Utilisation of the new facility was about 15% in FY26 for HVAC. Management targets 50% in FY27 and 80% in FY28 across about eight new products and new geometries.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Data centre was about 16% of revenue in FY26 per one answer and about 18.7-19% in Q4 per another answer; management expects this to rise quarter on quarter. Top-10 customers include three data centre customers.

segments.name: Bus AC
segments.commentary: Bus AC revenue was about Rs.10 crore in FY26; management targets at least 15% market share in FY27 and has a Rs.150 crore revenue target shown in the presentation, with two to three OEMs onboarded.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export was about Rs.100 crore in FY26 and management aims for roughly double in FY27; export order book is about Rs.120 crore including data centre orders. Geographies cited: UAE, US/North America and Europe.

segments.name: Railways / refrigeration
segments.commentary: Bar and plate heat exchanger approved by Indian Railways for field trial; company says it was L1 in three recent tenders. Full HVAC system for railways needs about 6-8 months of approvals, so limited FY27 contribution expected.

guidance_outlook: New facility utilisation targets: about 50% in FY27 and about 80% in FY28; old facility to stay fully utilised.
Management expects next eight quarters to be the highest ever, with Q4 described as an average quarter and quarter-on-quarter improvement expected.
Export to roughly double in FY27 versus about Rs.100 crore in FY26.

Margins expected to improve slightly, helped by a 5% PLI benefit in FY26, a likely RIFS state incentive of about 1.56% of top line for 10 years on the new facility, export mix and solar power savings, offset by higher depreciation and overheads.
Inventory expected to come under control within about three quarters; minimum six months to normalise per management.
Analyst cited a Rs.2,250-2,850 crore revenue target; management did not confirm the target or its timing.
capex_capacity: New Neemrana facility inaugurated 11 March 2026; production commissioning began May 2025 and the plant was shifted to fully in the week before the call.

Current facility is fully commissioned; about eight new products added, including WOT condenser, roll-bond evaporator, frost-free evaporator, skin condenser, bar and plate, dry air cooler, ammonia evaporator and bus AC, plus new fin geometries.
Further capex on existing facility is about Rs.30-40 crore over the next two years, mainly for line balancing for data centre geometry, per management's rough estimate.
Micro-channel (MCHX) product expected by end 2026 or early 2027; plate-and-plate heat exchanger (CDU) under study for next year.
Solar plant installed and operational.
demand_pricing: Raw material pass-through: management said copper LME, aluminium LME and USD-INR changes are passed to customers on a quarterly basis, with freight and logistics also passed through; it said close to 100% pass-through is possible.
UAE dispatches were disrupted in March 2026 due to the geopolitical situation; dispatches restarted in May 2026. Freight costs rose and are being passed on.
North America and Europe dispatches unaffected per management; Europe is early-stage and North America is larger than Europe for data centre exports.
Company says it competes with European and North American suppliers, not Chinese players, given customised, low-volume products.
Data centre demand: some Indian customers issue one-month firm orders on a rolling basis; one long-lead customer booked six to seven months.
Vertiv vendor approval received after QA audit; billing expected to start in coming weeks or months; Schneider Electric is the biggest domestic data centre customer.

qa_highlights.question: Are new products for liquid-cooled AI data centres in development?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said liquid cooling is early in India; fin and tube remains the core product for chillers and dry coolers, with micro-channel due by end 2026 or early 2027 and plate heat exchanger for CDUs under study.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company pass raw material costs to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said copper, aluminium and USD-INR movements are passed through quarter on quarter and close to 100% can be passed on under current contracts; there is a one-quarter lag.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory up about 3x and receivables up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited about Rs.15-20 crore of UAE material held after March dispatch was blocked, about Rs.8 crore of export dispatched in March but not billed, minimum stock for new products, BIS-related pre-buying of inner groove tube, and new customer onboarding. Normalisation expected in about six months, with inventory days around two and a half months currently.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise equity when internal cash flow may suffice?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the IPO proceeds were exceeded by investment in the current facility and working capital will be short; the board approved an enabling resolution up to Rs.500 crore, with objectives not yet concluded. Bank funding is also an option.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 revenue share from products other than fin and tube?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not have the figure on the call; it said non-fin-and-tube business is about 5% of revenue overall.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bus AC Rs.150 crore target backed by orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two to three OEMs have been onboarded and regular supply has started, with about 15% market share targeted; no specific Rs.150 crore order book was quantified.

Concentration of data centre revenue (about 16-19%) and dependence on a few large customers such as Schneider Electric.
Depreciation and overhead rising ahead of revenue.

544264|2026-03.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 38.08% YoY to INR1,415.74 million, with FY27 revenue growth guided above 20%.
544264|2026-03.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was INR1,415.74 million (+38.08% YoY) and EBITDA excluding other income was INR206.89 million (+39.96%), at a 14.61% margin. Consolidated FY26 revenue was INR4,066.28 million (+21.28%) with PAT of INR504.1 million (+39.87%). Standalone growth was weaker: Q4 revenue +12.18% and Q4 PAT down 3.05%, which management attributed to capacity constraints in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering running at about 85-90% utilisation. Order book stood at about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores a year earlier. New Unit 4 capacity is being commissioned from Q1 FY27 onward.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Roughly 10% of revenue per management. Covers on-site breakdown repair, hot kiln alignment and bulk deposition, with about 50-60 welding technicians deployed. UAE subsidiary set up for service and overlay work is now operational and expected to contribute from FY27.

segments.commentary: L1 in multiple contracts and some letters of intent received for Vande Bharat ecosystem components; execution 6-9 months, with substantial revenue expected from next year at likely lower initial margins.

segments.commentary: Investment made in February 2026 for VSHORADS work; still in prototype stage with a DRDO sanction order for 200 launchers and 1,200 rockets. No revenue expected in FY26 or in FY27 in any significant amount.

Medium-term aspiration of INR650 crore-plus revenue at 15-16% EBITDA margin, expected to be reached in under 3 years (2-3 years on annual run-rate basis).

International revenue share expected to rise to about 15%, with international sales growing above 20%.
capex_capacity: New 10 tons-per-day electrode plant commissioned around November-December 2025, along with an in-house strip-slitting line for flux-cored wires.
Wear plate capacity expanded by about 25% and now commissioned.

Unit 4 (about 170,000-180,000 sq ft) for wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering: partial utilisation from May 2026, most capacity live by end of Q1 FY27 (quarter ending June 2026), with the facility expected to be fully commissioned by end of Q1 2027 per management.

New wire line expected to be delivered in July 2026.
demand_pricing: Order book about INR200 crores as of 30 April 2026, up from about INR100 crores on 31 March 2025; management expects 80-90% to execute in FY27, with staggered power-project deliveries extending beyond.
Over 80% of revenue from repeat customers; end-market demand from cement, steel, power, mining and engineering described as steady, with no project holds despite the West Asia crisis.

Raw material volatility (tungsten, nickel, cobalt, molybdenum, chromium) is affecting margins; price variation clauses cover under 10% of the order book, with the rest fixed-price contracts. Management books raw materials on order and gives short offer validity on volatile items.
Price increases are ongoing, linked to input costs; management says customers are aware of raw material conditions.

Exports reach more than 35 countries including Southeast Asia, Middle East and Africa; Turkey operations are maturing, a new West Africa partner has been identified, and Singapore sales rose significantly in FY26.
Competitors named: Ador Fontech (merged into Ador Welding) and EWAC Alloys (now part of ESAB) in welding consumables and wear plates; ThyssenKrupp, ISGEC and Walchandnagar in heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone growth flat relative to consolidated, and will it normalise in FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said standalone plants were already at about 85% utilisation, capping execution in wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering; new capacity from Q1 FY27 should lift standalone growth to match consolidated.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin volatility (13% to 14.8%) driven by?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to raw material price lags on fixed-price contracts; gross margin may fall, but fixed and operating costs have been consolidated, so net margins improved with scale.

qa_highlights.question: How is the debtor-day gap versus Ador Fontech explained?
qa_highlights.answer: Debtors are at 98 days for FY26 due to large heavy-engineering shipments in March (about INR140 crores of Q4 sales, including roughly INR20 crores of rollers). Target is 80-85 days for FY27; welding consumables are cash-and-carry; heavy engineering is typically 60 days contractually but extends to 75-90 days in practice.

qa_highlights.question: Will the INR650 crore revenue target be reached faster, with growth accelerating above 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects growth to rise as new facilities come online and expects INR650 crores in 2-3 years on run-rate basis; no additional capex is needed for that level, and INR100 crores of capex could support INR800-900 crores.

qa_highlights.question: When will railway and defence businesses contribute meaningful revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Railway developmental orders take 6-9 months to execute, with substantial revenue from next year after approved-vendor listing. Tejorup defence revenue is not expected in FY26 or significantly in FY27, pending prototype approval.

qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, citing confidentiality; said steel mill roller revenue was significant last year, a first VRM order has been won, and shredder spare parts are under development.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone margin fall from ~18% peak to ~13%, and is Q1 the bottom?

544264|2026-09.headline: Diffusion Engineers Q4 FY25 revenue rose 38.55% YoY to INR1,024.48 million; FY25 revenue INR3,351.96 million, up 20.51%.
544264|2026-09.overview: Q4 FY25 was the company's first earnings call after its October 2024 listing. Revenue grew 38.55% YoY to INR1,024.48 million, with EBITDA (ex other income) up 82.55% to INR147.01 million and margin up 346 bps to 14.35%. FY25 revenue rose 20.51% to INR3,351.96 million, EBITDA ex other income rose 21.12% to INR470.76 million, and PAT rose 17% to INR360.40 million. Management is roughly doubling capacity with a INR100 crore capex programme, with the new capacity targeted by end FY26 and utilisation currently around 85%.

segments.name: Heavy engineering
segments.commentary: One of three product baskets, each stated to contribute roughly one-third of revenue. Management expects it, and wear parts, to grow faster than consumables; ~50-odd customers. Divisional EBITDA margins not disclosed.

segments.name: Wear plates and wear parts
segments.commentary: One of three equal-weight baskets; management says growth in FY25 was strong, alongside heavy engineering. Serves close to 1,000 customers. Replacement cycle is 18-24 months.

segments.name: Welding and anti-wear consumables
segments.commentary: One of three equal-weight baskets, said to carry higher margins than wear plates and heavy engineering, but grew more slowly in FY25. Flux core wire is ~7% of turnover and cold repair compounds ~3%.

segments.name: Services and rental
segments.commentary: Industrial services (on-site breakdown repair, kiln alignment) are ~1-2% of revenue. A new wear-part rental model has two ongoing contracts, already fully paid, with NBFC lease tie-ups planned.

guidance_outlook: Capacity to roughly double by end FY26 with INR100 crore capex: Nimji heavy engineering unit ~INR70 crore, B33 MIDC unit ~INR30 crore.
Target asset turnover of about 3x, in line with historical 3-3.25x; 80-85% utilisation expected within 2-3 years of commissioning.
Management aims to grow faster than the market and to improve margins; no forward revenue numbers given.
ROCE is about 15% at present, with an aspiration to match or beat pre-IPO levels.
Working capital to stay around 90-100 days given 6-9 month heavy equipment cycles and 90-100 day payment terms.
Planned 1.1 MW captive rooftop solar on the Nimji unit, funded from IPO objects.
capex_capacity: INR100 crore capex for FY26: Nimji heavy engineering unit ~INR70 crore and B33 MIDC unit ~INR30 crore.
Current utilisation about 85% on the existing capacity base; capacity to roughly double by end FY26.
Capex adds machining capability for larger and more precise parts, which management says few Indian suppliers offer.
Abu Dhabi service and manufacturing plant was due to go live in Q1 FY26 (this quarter).
Unit 4 has started flux-coated wire and wear plate production.
demand_pricing: Revenue growth attributed to timely execution of high-value orders and demand from cement, steel, power and engineering, with growth across all sectors.
Order book was cited as roughly INR100-120 crore; management says it keeps growing daily, and over 50% of orders come from repeat customers.
Around 23-25% of revenue goes through OEMs; the rest is direct to end clients, with a small channel-partner share.
Exports were 12-13% of FY25 revenue, down from 13-14% in FY24, though absolute exports are rising. Export margins are higher due to less competition.
About 80% of OE business is new projects and the rest is maintenance, which management describes as recurring.
Margin gains were attributed to volume-driven purchasing scale and low metal and raw-material prices in prior years.
Customers are moving to ready-to-fit and complete solutions rather than buying consumables themselves.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be split across the three verticals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not disclose product-wise EBITDA margins. It said consumables and anti-wear carry higher margins than wear plates, wear parts and heavy engineering.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and manufacturing costs rise sharply?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said recruitment was started to gear up for the capex, and that gross margin should be read across raw material, stock purchases, inventory change and manufacturing expenses together.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth stagnant until new capacity comes online?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth will continue, with the new capacity making it more significant. It noted lead times differ by order mix.

qa_highlights.question: How much of heavy engineering is made in-house from own consumables and wear parts?
qa_highlights.answer: On average 20-30%, with a range of 15-50% depending on the order, excluding machining.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status and use of IPO capex funds?
qa_highlights.answer: The funds are held in fixed deposits with scheduled commercial banks and not in mutual funds. The mutual fund holdings come from free cash flow, mostly in equity.

qa_highlights.question: What is the other income of about INR5 crore in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: It is largely interest on IPO proceeds. Management said EBITDA excluding other income rose 21% to INR470 million in FY25.

UK associate (21.5% stake, nickel and cobalt powders) booked losses from inventory revaluation; management says no similar losses are expected.
Metal price volatility, notably nickel, affects costs and margins.

Margin expansion depends on exports and more complex parts; management declined to quantify.

544274|2026-09.headline: Hyundai India Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record ₹20,696 Mn (+18.5% YoY), but EBITDA margin fell to 9.5% from 13.9% on commodity headwinds.
544274|2026-09.overview: Domestic volumes rose 18.8% YoY to 165,772 units and total sales hit a record 219,072 units, with exports up 3.7% YoY and 38% QoQ. Revenue reached a record ₹206,961 Mn, but raw material inflation of roughly 400 bps YoY and 250 bps QoQ compressed EBITDA to ₹19,745 Mn and PAT to ₹11,962 Mn (5.7% margin vs 8.9%). Management guided to 8-10% domestic growth and high-double-digit export growth in H2, and a sequential margin recovery toward an 11% full-year EBITDA margin. Bayon launched two days before the call and a dedicated mass-market EV is slated for early CY27.

segments.commentary: 165,772 units, +18.8% YoY; record rural share of 26.6% and record CNG share of 19.1%. Overall ASP up about 2% YoY; localisation at tier-1 reached 84%.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Volume up 3.7% YoY and 38% QoQ, 24% of total volume. Q2 mix: Middle East and Africa 52% (Middle East 34%, Africa 18%), Latin America 26%, Mexico 20%.

segments.name: EV
segments.commentary: CRETA Electric drove EV contribution to double QoQ; dedicated mass-market EV due early CY27 (Jan/Feb 2027). Industry EV share about 6-6.5%.

Third shift at Pune started, bringing output closer to 170,000 units per year.

Localisation at tier-1 level 84% in Q2 FY27, up from 82% last year.
PLI: provisional compliance certificate received for Creta; final certificate pending. New EV aims for PLI compliance.
demand_pricing: Management said demand is strong; Shradh plus Navratri sales up 31% YoY and Onam up 75%. Bayon waiting period 2 to 6 months depending on variant, which the company is trying to shorten.
Industry growth expected at about 5-5.5% in H2; company targets 8-10%.
Commodity impact about 400 bps YoY and 250 bps QoQ in Q2; partly offset by localisation, value engineering and price hikes.

Export interest from about 50 countries for Bayon (about 34 in Latin America, 14-15 in Middle East).

qa_highlights.answer: Bayon and the EV will both be built in Chennai, taking utilisation above 90%. Creta plus Bayon seen at 250,000 annual volume, described as conservative. EV launch expected early CY27 (Jan/Feb 2027).

qa_highlights.question: How will export growth reach the guided level, given geopolitical and shipping disruptions?
qa_highlights.answer: H2 high-double-digit export growth is supported by demand, new products (Venue volumes to at least double, Exter at least 50% growth), new markets like Mexico, and alternate Middle East routes and ports with logistics partners.

qa_highlights.question: Q3 discount trend and incremental commodity headwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Discounts 2.9% vs 3.2% YoY; QoQ increase marginal and seasonal. Q3 commodity outlook is hard to quantify given volatility, with copper and plastic rising and precious metals falling.

qa_highlights.question: Demand outlook for H2 and rural trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Demand described as very strong; dealers asking for more cars. Rural remains strong and expected to outpace urban; no major El Nino impact seen so far.

qa_highlights.question: Creta volume outlook and export contribution from Bayon?
qa_highlights.answer: Creta expected at about 170,000 this year. About 50 countries have shown interest in Bayon exports; more clarity expected by the next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: How will H2 EBITDA margin reach the guided level?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers: Tamil Nadu incentive (over 1% in Q3 and Q4), higher-margin exports, possible raw material softening after US mid-term elections, September and January price hikes, Chennai utilisation recovery, and third-shift fixed-cost leverage.
