544277|2026-03.headline: Waaree FY26 revenue rose ~84% to INR26,537 crore and operating EBITDA 117% to INR5,909 crore, but Q4 margin fell to ~18.6% on commodity, freight and mix pressures.
544277|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue from operations of INR26,537 crore (+84% YoY), operating EBITDA of INR5,909 crore (22.27% margin vs 18.84%) and PAT of INR3,884 crore (+101%). Q4 revenue was INR8,480 crore (+111% YoY) and operating EBITDA INR1,576 crore, with margin down sharply from the prior quarter as silver and copper costs, freight spikes, lower overseas mix and in-house DCR cell shortfall weighed. Management guided FY27 operating EBITDA to INR7,000-7,700 crore and framed the Waaree 2.0 capex (~$3.5 billion) as the driver, with most cell and module capex completing in FY27 and benefits from H2 FY27 onward. Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were stuck on logistics delays and inventory built up.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 production 12.6 GW (+77%), sales about 12 GW; Q4 production 4.2 GW (+104% YoY) and Q4 sales 4.1 GW. Capacity ~26 GW, described as the largest non-Chinese module maker.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational cell capacity 5.4 GW (largest in India); Q4 cell production 0.7 GW. A 10 GW cell facility is due in H2 FY27, taking cell capacity to ~15.4 GW.

segments.name: Revenue mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Utility/IPP/C&I 34.7%, overseas 33%, retail 20.8%, EPC 11.6%. Retail revenue INR5,515 crore (+84%). Q4 overseas share fell to ~21% from ~32% in Q3.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.6 GW plant ramped; 2.6 GW more to go live within six months, taking US capacity to 4.2 GW. IRA benefit ~$0.07/Wp, ~$40 million in FY26, to rise with new capacity.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: ~INR53,000 crore excluding retail (~20% of revenue), up from ~INR47,000 crore a year ago but down ~INR7,000 crore QoQ per analyst. ~65-70% is overseas, to be delivered over 3-4 years. More than INR8,400 crore delivered already.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at INR7,000-7,700 crore (about 20-25% growth on FY26 INR5,909 crore).
Management says the margin benefit from in-house DCR cells starts in H2 FY27 when the 10 GW cell line goes live; H1 is a transition.
Long-range planning assumption: 19-20% EBITDA margin sustained for a decade.
Cell utilisation assumed 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW capacity; 28 GW modules, 4 GW inverters, 20,000 MVA transformers and 1 GW electrolyser to run at full throttle in FY28.
Capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over the next two years; core module and cell capex complete in FY27, ingot wafer and part of battery in FY28; full Waaree 2.0 benefits seen in FY29.
Cell line transition from M10R to G12R expected to lift output and realisation by 10-12% within about a quarter; module output back to ~330 MW a month within two months.
Investor Day to be held; enabling board resolution for fundraise of up to ~INR10,000 crore approved, with shareholder approval to follow.
capex_capacity: Battery (BESS): 20 GWh planned, phase 1 of 3.5 GWh in FY27 (Gujarat), phase 2 of 16.5 GWh in FY28; capex ~INR10,000 crore.
Ingot wafer: 10 GW at Nagpur, capex ~INR6,200 crore (up from INR5,100 crore earlier with 6 GW to 10 GW); completion FY28.
PV glass: 2,500 TPD approved at ~INR3,900 crore capex, production expected within 24 months; supports ~16-17 GW of modules.
Inverters: 4 GW at Sarodhi, Gujarat (~INR180 crore); 3 GW commissioned, remaining 1 GW in FY27.
Transformers: current ~4,000 MVA; adding 16,000 MVA to reach 20,000 MVA at Alwar (~INR192 crore) in FY27.
Hydrogen: 1 GW electrolyser at Dungri, Gujarat (~INR676 crore capex); electrolyser PLI INR444 crore and hydrogen PLI ~INR510 crore.
Acquired ~55% of Associated Power Structures Ltd (APSL) for ~INR1,225 crore for T&D entry; Oman polysilicon stake acquired for non-Chinese supply.
Module lines: 3 lines converted to G12R (ramping), 3 lines remain Mono PERC, 5 lines still on M10R TOPCon, to convert over about one quarter.
demand_pricing: Domestic DCR module pricing INR21-22/Wp; non-DCR utility INR15-16/Wp, with retail carrying a premium; commodity increases are being passed through to new orders.
Silver and copper cost increases, freight spikes and a lower overseas share weighed on Q4 margin; management said customers are now accepting the higher commodity-linked prices.
ALMM-II (domestic cell mandate) takes effect June 2026; C&I and mid-market decisions were deferred pending clarity, which slowed local offtake.
India installed 44.6 GW of solar in FY26; module consumption was about 50-55 GW. Management sees DCR-compliant cell capacity at ~30 GW for ALMM-II.
US FEOC rules from April 2026 require non-Chinese cells and components, which management says is driving new US orders.
BESS pricing around $110-120/MWh cited for India and US; BESS margin guided at 18-20% before policy support.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating EBITDA margin fall sharply QoQ, and what are the DCR and non-DCR realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited silver and copper cost spikes, freight cost surge, a lower overseas mix and DCR cell shortfall. DCR modules INR21-22/Wp; utility non-DCR INR15-16/Wp, with a retail premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export mix low in Q4 and what is the order book composition?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were stuck on Middle East logistics delays, so inventory rose. About 65-70% of the INR53,000 crore order book is overseas, delivered over 3-4 years; retail (~20% of revenue) is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore be achieved, and what drives margin?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is a transition from 5.4 GW to 15.4 GW of cells; the 10 GW cell line in H2 lifts in-house DCR supply. Pre-startup costs for new projects are included in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ingot-wafer capex rise and its timeline move to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised from 6 GW to 10 GW and sites moved from Odisha to Gujarat and Nagpur, causing the delay. The new figure covers the full 10 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash conversion cycle and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up because overseas shipments were delayed. Customer advances stayed steady but production nearly doubled, diluting working capital days. Management expects cash conversion of 70-100% at normalised inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS unit economics and FY29 revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS margin guided at 18-20% without policy support. Management declined to give FY29 revenue guidance, pointing to the 20 GWh capacity and $110-120/MWh pricing.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the 10 GW cell line commissioning in H2 FY27 and on the G12R ramp; Q4 showed sharp margin compression.
Working capital and cash conversion (~27%) need to normalise as stuck export inventory ships.
ALMM-II timing uncertainty is deferring C&I and mid-market orders; order book fell ~INR7,000 crore QoQ.
Commodity (silver, copper) and freight volatility; pricing pass-through to new orders is unproven.
Execution risk on ~$3.5 billion capex across BESS, glass, ingot-wafer and US plants, plus fundraise of up to INR10,000 crore.
Overcapacity concerns in the module sector; management argues demand and supply balance once ALMM-II/III take effect.
544277|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term Waaree 2.0 story and on FY26 results. Noticeably defensive and detailed when explaining the Q4 margin drop, cash conversion and order-book sequential decline, often attributing them to temporary logistics and transition factors. Several answers on BESS economics, the fundraise, Indosolar and ALMM-II timing were deferred or left unquantified.

financial_highlights.change: Above prior guidance of INR5,500-6,000 crore
+70% YoY; margin fell sharply QoQ (analyst cited ~590 bps decline)
vs INR644 crore in Q4 FY25
Down from over 100% in prior period per analyst; management says 70-100% normalised

key_quotes: Our capital allocation follows a simple principle, book and build, which means every rupee we deploy is backed by confirmed demand and a clear path to returns.
The safest assumption there will be is your 19 %-20% margin consistent for a decade long at least.
So, we really don't foresee any scenario anytime next 5, 10 years of time will be the supply is going to be much higher than demand.
So, if you keep the inventory at normalized levels, the same number will go back to the normalized level of 70% to 100% conversion of cash from current 27%.

rows.why: Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were held up by Middle East logistics delays, and management expects 70-100% at normalised inventory, but this is unquantified on timing.

544277|2026-06.headline: Waaree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79.2% YoY to INR7,932 crore and order book hit a record INR61,500 crore, though operating EBITDA margin was 18.2%.
544277|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 79.2% YoY to about INR7,932 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44.4% to about INR1,440 crore at an 18.2% margin and PAT of INR892 crore (11% margin, up 15.4%). Management attributed margin pressure to higher global raw material costs, softer US exports from delayed clearances, and inventory built ahead of second-half-weighted dispatches. Order book rose to INR61,500 crore after INR16,000 crore of net inflows against about INR7,300 crore executed. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore, pinning the margin recovery on rising captive cell integration and US local manufacturing.

segments.name: Revenue mix
segments.commentary: Utility IPP and C&I 39.7%, retail 30.2%, overseas 21.2%, EPC and O&M 8.9% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Utility/IPP/C&I share was 52.1% in FY25.

segments.name: Retail (B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR2,289 crore, up 130% YoY; management guides INR9,000-10,000 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Overseas / US
segments.commentary: US domestic revenue INR1,322 crore and direct exports INR287 crore. US plant produced about 230 MW in Q1, earning roughly USD12-13 million of IRA incentives.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing (India)
segments.commentary: 5.4 GW capacity at 62% utilisation; about 800 MW of DCR cell made in Q1. Integrated cell lines show 35-40% margin per management.

segments.name: Modules (India and US)
segments.commentary: India module capacity 24.2 GW at about 50% annualised utilisation; US module capacity 1.6 GW at about 59%. Management expects US utilisation of 75-80% in coming quarters.

segments.name: BESS / storage
segments.commentary: Automated BESS container capacity of 5.15 GWh started, versus 3.5 GWh originally planned. A 1,520 MWh BESS EPC order was won.

segments.name: Transmission and transformers
segments.commentary: Waaree Transpower began commercial production of a 17.6 MVA inverter-duty transformer. WRTL acquired about 55% of Associated Power Structures for about INR1,225 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
FY28 ballpark of about INR7,000 crore EBITDA mentioned by Varun Goenka; FY28 expected to see about 16-18 GW module and about 10 GW cell production.
Cell-to-module integration ratio to rise from about 20% to about 65% within 2-3 quarters.
Cell production to rise from about 800 MW in Q1 to about 1.2 GW in Q2 and about 1.5 GW in Q3.
Module utilisation to reach 70-75% in Q3 and Q4; management expects 80-85% over 2-3 quarters as integration rises.
US IRA incentive receipts expected quarterly from Q3-Q4 FY27 via refund or sale of credits; US production of 400-500 MW per quarter from Q3.
Management aspires to a near INR1 lakh crore revenue vision in less than 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex programme about INR31,500 crore; about INR9,450 crore deployed as of 30 June. Phasing is about 30% in FY27, 40% in FY28 and 30% in FY29.

FY27 additions: 2.6 GW US modules, 10 GW Indian cell (Gujarat, ALMM-II applied, equipment on site, commercial start expected from about Q3), 100 KTPA T&D EPC, 20 GVA transformers, 4 GW inverters, 1 GW electrolysers.
FY28: 10 GW ingot and wafer at Nagpur, construction started. FY29: 2,500 TPD solar glass (about INR3,900 crore, greenfield approved) and 16.5 GWh BESS plant.
Indian cell capacity to reach 15.4 GW against 24.2 GW module capacity by FY27-end; US BESS cell 3.5 GWh to commission within FY27, with 95% site construction done.
Potential QIP of about INR10,000 crore approved by Board and shareholders; timing depends on market conditions.
demand_pricing: Order book INR61,500 crore as of 28 July 2026 (25.2 GW), up from about INR53,000 crore at FY26-end; geographic mix India about 40%, US about 36%, exports about 24%.
Realisations per watt: exports USD0.25-0.26; DCR USD0.20-0.25; non-DCR USD0.13-0.14. Order book realisations seen at USD0.24-0.25 for near quarters; long-range DCR orders at USD0.21-0.22.
Non-DCR offtake delayed by developers in Q1; ALMM-II effective 1 June with about a 5-6 month window, leading to expected offtake from Q2.
Top 5 customers 27.1% of sales (from 33% in FY26); top 10 at 37.1% (from 47%).
Imported cell about USD0.04-0.045/W versus Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W; DCR market price about USD0.12-0.13/W.
US market had about six months of installation lull due to tariff uncertainty; management reports recent order and enquiry pickup, including data-centre demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expansion timeline for 10 GW cell and wafer and battery capacity over FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 28 GW modules, 15.4 GW cells, 4 GW inverters and 20 GVA transformers by FY27-end; FY28 to see about 16-18 GW modules and about 10 GW cell output. The 10 GW Indian cell facility adds from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did module gross margin fall, and what are the recovery levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower IRA realisation in Q1 because US dispatches came from OEM manufacturing; delayed non-DCR offtake; softer exports. Levers are DCR cell output, US local scaling, exports from August, and non-DCR offtake over the six-month window.

qa_highlights.question: How are US export and US local manufacturing margins structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports from India earn about USD0.04-0.05/W EBITDA. US local manufacturing nets about USD0.055-0.06/W after expenses, with IRA incentive of USD0.07/W. Management guides total US local realisation and EBITDA at USD0.07-0.08/W, helped by a USD0.01-0.02/W cut in US conversion cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a lower-cost import option for cells compared with domestic manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported cell is about USD0.04-0.045/W against Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W and DCR market price of USD0.12-0.13/W.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS volume and earnings outlook for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The 5.15 GWh container line is live and order book is building. The 3.5 GWh BESS cell line is due to start commercially in FY27. FEOC-compliant cell realisations are about 25-30% above Chinese pricing, with non-FEOC at USD75-80/kWh versus Chinese USD50-55/kWh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP plan and funding need?
qa_highlights.answer: Board and shareholders approved about INR10,000 crore of fundraising including equity. Management says FY27 EBITDA is broadly sufficient to fund the capex and it will wait for the right market window. Balance capex is about INR22,000 crore over three years.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from raw material inflation and a lower IRA realisation mix in Q1; watch whether 18.2% operating EBITDA margin recovers toward the FY27 guidance band.
Second-half weighted order book and inventory build; utilisation of India modules around 50% annualised in Q1 versus a 70-75% target for Q3-Q4.
Timing of the 10 GW Indian cell commissioning (targeted by December) and ALMM-II extension window; the non-DCR offtake ramp is unconfirmed.
US export clearance delays and the start of US local line output from August; US IRA incentive monetisation timing.
Capex execution across INR31,500 crore programme and the glass capex decision, with an update promised in about one quarter.
Pending QIP and funding plan; BESS Make-in-India incentive is not yet announced.

Management repeatedly tied recovery to specific dated levers and reaffirmed guidance. Responses on glass capex, BESS incentives and QIP timing were less specific.
key_quotes: Our order book stands at approximately INR61,500 crores, the highest in our history, up from INR50,000 crores just a quarter ago, with about INR16,000 crores in new orders won in this quarter alone.
Our cell-to-module integration ratio is going to rise from roughly around 20% currently to around 65% in next two to three quarters, close to a threefold increase.
It is on this trend that we affirm and reaffirm our 2027 operating EBITDA guidance, what we have stated in our last call.

net cash balance sheet as of 30 June

rows.why: Operating EBITDA margin was 18.2% in Q1 and FY27 guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore is reaffirmed; cell-to-module integration to rise from about 20% to about 65% within 2-3 quarters, with DCR cell output rising from 800 MW in Q1 to 1.5 GW in Q3, and integrated cell lines show 35-40% margin.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Module volume rose 89% YoY to 3.6 GW in Q1, the order book is a record INR61,500 crore (25.2 GW), and cell output is set to ramp from 0.8 GW to 1.2 GW in Q2 and 1.5 GW in Q3, with module utilisation targeted at 70-75% in Q3-Q4.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Board has approved about INR10,000 crore QIP and a 2,500 TPD solar glass greenfield (about INR3,900 crore) with an update promised in about one quarter, while utilisation is only about 50% so new capex is not the immediate need; announcement depends on the glass decision and QIP window.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore was only reaffirmed, not raised, and Q1 operating EBITDA was INR1,440 crore with 18.2% margin, which leaves little room to beat the band at this stage.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q1 margin of 18.2% was pressured by raw material costs and delayed non-DCR offtake, India module utilisation is about 50% against a 70-75% Q3-Q4 target, and the 10 GW cell start is targeted for about Q3 with the non-DCR ramp unconfirmed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: 5.15 GWh BESS container line is already live, 3.5 GWh BESS cell line is due to start commercially in FY27, and 16.5 GWh BESS plant plus 2,500 TPD glass are slated for FY29.

rows.label: Record order book INR61,500 crore (25.2 GW)
rows.why: Order book rose from about INR53,000 crore at FY26-end after INR16,000 crore net inflows against about INR7,300 crore executed in Q1, a 16% quarter-on-quarter increase.

rows.label: Q1 inventory build ahead of H2-weighted dispatches
rows.why: Inventory was built in Q1 for second-half dispatches, and IRA incentive receipts are expected quarterly from Q3-Q4 FY27 via refund or sale of credits.

rows.label: US local manufacturing and IRA incentive monetisation
rows.why: US production is set at 400-500 MW per quarter from Q3, with IRA incentive of USD0.07/W and US local realisation guided at USD0.07-0.08/W, plus a USD0.01-0.02/W cut in US conversion cost.

tone.note: Management was confident on the order book, cell ramp and reaffirmed FY27 EBITDA guidance, but candid about Q1 margin and dispatch shortfalls; analysts pushed on margin recovery, module utilisation and the timing of glass capex, BESS incentives and QIP.

544277|2026-09.headline: Waaree Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23.9% YoY to Rs 7,517.7 crore, with operating EBITDA of Rs 1,335.2 crore (17.8% margin); FY27 EBITDA guidance of Rs 7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
544277|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was Rs 7,517.7 crore (up 23.9% YoY) with operating EBITDA of Rs 1,335.2 crore and PAT of Rs 753.6 crore. H1 revenue rose 47.3% to Rs 15,449.5 crore, but H1 PAT was flat at Rs 1,645.5 crore versus Rs 1,651.1 crore a year earlier. Management said the US export order book was rationalised after Section 232 minimum import prices, cutting export share of the order book from about 24% to 7.8%, while retail and US-manufactured volumes grew. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance and expects H2 to deliver 55-60% of it, driven by cell and US capacity ramp-ups.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 margin was 18.2% per analyst; Q1 included US duty refund

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 3,464 crore, 46.1% of Q2 revenue

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 2,875 crore a year ago

financial_highlights.value: about Rs 59,200 crore; module order book 25.6 GW
financial_highlights.change: geography: 48.4% domestic India, 43.8% domestic US, 7.8% exports

segments.name: Retail / cash-and-carry (India)
segments.commentary: Q2 retail revenue about Rs 3,464 crore (46.1% of Q2 revenue), up 252% YoY; 775+ exclusive retail centres and about 3,000 distribution points. FY27 retail revenue guided at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore; over 92% of retail revenue is modules.

segments.name: Utility, IPP, C&I
segments.commentary: Contributed about 22.9% of Q2 revenue.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: 18.5% of Q2 revenue (Rs 1,389 crore vs Rs 2,875 crore a year ago). Within it, US domestic revenue rose to Rs 1,300 crore from Rs 732 crore; exports from India fell to Rs 89 crore from Rs 2,143 crore.

segments.name: EPC, O&M, T&D, others
segments.commentary: Combined 12.6% of Q2 revenue. T&D acquisition sits under the listed subsidiary, which runs a blended EBITDA margin of about 14-15%.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: Domestic US manufacturing revenue up 113% YoY in H1 FY27; US module output reached 0.3 GW in the period at 71% annualised utilisation. Q2 US supply about 400 MW, of which about 300 MW self-manufactured.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance reaffirmed at Rs 7,000-7,700 crore; H1 was about Rs 2,775 crore, so H2 needs about 55-60% of the guided total per management.
Q3 and Q4 volumes expected to be heavy, with 5 GW of Indian cell capacity going live in Q3 and another 5 GW in Q4.
US 1.6 GW module line to become operational in Q3 FY27; a second 1.6 GW line in the next quarter, taking Waaree Solar Americas to 4.8 GW.
Retail revenue guided at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore for FY27.
Newer businesses (BESS, transformers, inverters, T&D, EPC, electrolysers) expected to rise from 15-20% of revenue to 30-35% over 2-3 years; long-range solar 50-60% of revenue.
Management's ambition is Rs 90,000-1 lakh crore revenue over 4-5 years (about 20 GW module output at 75% utilisation plus non-solar businesses); no timeline firmly committed.
capex_capacity: Capex programme about Rs 30,000 crore: 35% deployed, 28% under execution, 37% in planning. Management says cash balance covers under-construction projects without new borrowing.
Installed module capacity 25.8 GW, including 1.6 GW in the US; India cell capacity 5.4 GW rising to 15.4 GW with the 10 GW Unn expansion (cell-to-module ratio from about 22% to about 65%).

Ingot-wafer: 10 GW facility at Nagpur, commercial production targeted September 2027; capex about Rs 5,500 crore per management (analyst cited Rs 6,200-6,500 crore). Ingot-wafer civil works about 70% complete.

BESS: 5.1 GWh container and 5.1 GWh pack Phase 1 (container commissioned in Q2; pack expected in Q3; 3.5 GWh cell pilot from Q4 FY27). Phase 2 (16.5 GWh cell, 15 GWh container) is in planning; funding tied to policy clarity and overseas orders.

Inverter capacity 4 GW (production started); transformer capacity 20,000 MVA with incremental capacity by March 2027; electrolyser capacity also coming. Combined committed capital about Rs 1,200 crore.
Solar glass: about Rs 3,900 crore budget, about Rs 360 crore spent (land, filling, EOP); location near Navsari, Gujarat; go-live targeted FY29; technology partner talks ongoing.
Renewable power infrastructure: about Rs 3,250 crore committed; about 10 GW of grid connectivity, about 2 GW of PPAs (including 700 MW SECI FDRE), 25,000-30,000 acres of land under procurement.
demand_pricing: US pricing reset under Section 232: minimum import price of 38 cents/W plus 15% duty (about 44 cents landed) versus 27-28 cents landed today; realisation on US-made modules expected to rise from 26-27 cents toward 30-35 cents.

US-manufactured margin estimated at 8-9 cents/W at 70%+ utilisation (incl. about 7 cents/W incentive) versus about 3-4 cents/W EBITDA on exports from India; IRA incentives booked against dispatches and some sold.

India DCR module spot prices: utility 19-21 cents/W, retail 22-24 cents/W; forward FY28 prices 17.5-18.5 cents (utility) and 20-21 cents (retail). Non-DCR utility about 12-12.5 cents, retail 13.5-14 cents.
Management expects broad price correction in FY28 as capacity ramps across the industry; large integrated players expected to retain scale benefits.
Domestic module CUF fell to about 45% in Q2 as ALMM List-II extension shifted supply chains; management expects higher non-DCR volumes in Q3.
Indian demand (AC): residential plus C&I rooftop about 15 GW annualised; utility about 25 GW annualised; total about 55-60 GW DC per year per management.

qa_highlights.question: Retail channel economics: distributor margins, profitability, and how the distribution model is managed without visible opex increase.
qa_highlights.answer: Retail network is 775+ exclusive retail centres with about 3,000 distribution points and about 5,000 people; H1 retail revenue about Rs 5,700 crore, FY27 guided Rs 10,000-11,000 crore. Management cited operating leverage and partner growth (some partners from Rs 1-2 crore to Rs 50-75 crore a year), without giving channel margin figures.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be further US order cancellations after the 2-2.5 GW deemed cancellations in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 3 GW-plus of export orders were stopped being reported, cutting export share of the order book from about 24% to 7.8%; US order book is rising. Post Section 232, US realisation is expected to rise from 26-27 cents to 30-35 cents per watt. Renegotiation into MIP-compliant contracts is ongoing for orders already dispatched but not yet recognised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic module CUF fall below 50% (about 45%) in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: ALMM List-II extension of about 6 months shifted supply chains and replanning took time, so non-DCR supply was delayed. Management expects non-DCR supply to rise and Q3 volumes to be higher.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall sequentially from 18.2% to 17.8%?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 included a US duty refund; the refund rose from Rs 349 crore in Q1 to Rs 360.4 crore in Q2 (about Rs 11 crore booked in Q2). Like-for-like, margin improved with cell utilisation up from about 800 MW to over 1.1 GW per quarter and US module utilisation up from 60% to 70%+. Q3 and Q4 are expected to be heavy with 5 GW cell capacity each quarter plus US 1.6 GW lines; H2 expected at 55-60% of FY27 EBITDA guidance.

qa_highlights.question: US margin: how do exports from India compare with US-manufactured modules, and are IRA benefits included in reported numbers?
qa_highlights.answer: Export from India yields about 3-4 cents/W EBITDA; US manufacturing gives about 2-3 cents operating margin at 70%+ utilisation plus about 7 cents/W incentive, so 8-9 cents/W total. Management said this is more than double export margins. IRA incentives are booked against dispatches and some are sold, so reported numbers include them.

qa_highlights.question: Domestic pricing: DCR and non-DCR prices and expected correction in FY28.
qa_highlights.answer: DCR spot: utility 19-21 cents/W, retail 22-24 cents/W; FY28 forward utility 17.5-18.5 cents and retail 20-21 cents. Non-DCR utility about 12-12.5 cents, retail 13.5-14 cents. Broad price correction expected in FY28, with scale players retaining benefits.

qa_highlights.question: Why are subsidiary (listed entity) EBITDA margins low relative to revenue of about Rs 22 billion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the listed subsidiary runs about 17-18% EBITDA standalone, but after acquiring a T&D entity (T&D margins about 10-11%) the blended margin is about 14-15%. T&D is lumpy, so the subsidiary is chasing larger order books.

qa_highlights.question: BESS, inverter and transformer revenue contribution in FY28 and margins.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guidance of low double digits in constant currency maintained; Chirok and CareSeed revenue sits on top of organic guidance.
FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 25-26% from 24-25%; management said it sees 24-26% as the structural range, with possible marginal upside if AI productivity gains are retained.

OE/AEP revenue expected to be slightly lower than last year, roughly 100 bps lower as a share of total revenue (last year about 6%); marginally below flat YoY per CFO; subject to change over coming weeks.
Management intends to repay all outstanding debt in full during FY27.
Interim dividend of INR 0.15 per share approved, payable in Q3 FY27.
No explicit provider revenue-share target given; management declined to give Chirok guidance until late FY27.
capex_capacity: H1 fixed asset additions INR 1,168 mn; H1 acquisition cash outflow INR 1,338 mn.
Employee strength 51,486 at end Q2; quarterly voluntary attrition 25.7%, down from 28.6% in Q1 FY27 and lower than Q2 FY26.
Delivery centre count fell to 28 from 31 in March 2026 (33 in FY25), but management said this reflects counting multiple facilities on one campus as one site; seat count continued to rise.
Some short-term leases used during site consolidation; Jamaica sites closed earlier.
Staffing to capacity for AEP season with some flex capacity available.
105 active client groups; all top 10 client groups above $20 mn TTM revenue for the first time.
demand_pricing: Deal ACV up 18.2% YoY to $40.2 mn in Q2, from wins across 31 existing clients and one new client.
Payment integrity win from a Big Ten health plan is contingency-based, so revenue builds over time.
Clients making more deliberate, senior-level buying decisions for large transformation deals; pipeline skewed to managed services and mid-market Blues plans.
Agentic AI deployments: Synchrony Claims Lifecycle (claims adjudication) and Synchrony RCM Lifecycle (denials and appeals), with humans in the loop.
Management said provider deals have historically been smaller; gross margin difference between payer and provider is about 200-300 bps and deal-specific.
On AI pricing, most productivity gains will be passed to clients, with some retained.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the margin improvement and what supports the raised guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO cited operating efficiencies, a small FX tailwind from Q1 to Q2, and favourable geo mix; he expects FX to stay broadly at current levels and efficiencies to continue for the full year.

qa_highlights.question: How much could open enrolment contribution fall this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said about 100 bps lower than last year's roughly 6% of revenue on current visibility; CFO said it is marginally below flat YoY at this early stage.

qa_highlights.question: Is Chirok a step-up in provider mix, and is there an explicit provider target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is a much larger provider share over time but gave no explicit 2-3 year target; provider share is about 10% today. Investment is mainly the Chirok deal plus a dedicated provider go-to-market team, with no major margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why is provider growth lagging, and what is Chirok's growth history?
qa_highlights.answer: Provider growth has been 10-11% with some revenue taper from discrete projects at one client. Chirok revenue dipped in 2023-24 when one client's volumes fell, then recovered; management said the 35.8% margin is broadly on the same basis as Sagility's adjusted EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Is there conflict in serving both payers and providers?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said there is no inherent conflict, citing about 15 years of running both businesses and claims-denial friction the company helps resolve.

qa_highlights.question: Will margin stay in 24-26% range or structurally rise with AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh said the range remains 24-26%, with possible gradual upside if the company keeps some AI productivity benefits; most gains are expected to flow to clients.

qa_highlights.question: What are the minimum wage impacts and delivery centre trends?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the full minimum wage impact is baked into guidance (Q2 about INR 148 mn vs INR 70 mn in Q1), with Karnataka and Telangana effective end May and 1 June. The drop in site count reflects campus consolidation.

risks_watch: OE/AEP revenue is running slightly below last year, and the number could still shift over the coming weeks.
Chirok revenue per headcount is well below a listed Indian provider peer; management could not explain the gap and will follow up. Chirok pricing is said to be at market.
Chirok's AI disruption exposure in mid-cycle RCM: management says outpatient coding is most vulnerable, while inpatient coding is less exposed.
Provider growth has lagged payers; watch whether Chirok and cross-selling lift provider growth above 10-11%.
Statutory minimum wage increases in Karnataka and Telangana are a continuing cost headwind; any stay would be upside.
Q2 margin benefited from FX and geo mix, so sustainability depends on FX staying near current levels.
Earn-out payments on Chirok (up to $12.35 mn) and the $10 mn+ payment integrity deal depend on revenue milestones, so timing is uncertain.
Possible acquisitions: management said it stays open to clinical capability or client-focused tuck-ins, but named no specific target.
544282|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on operations and margins, with management raising margin guidance and citing record-level Q2 profitability. More cautious on AEP/OE season, which is described as early and subject to change, and evasive on some detail: Chirok revenue per head, the ACV split between payers and providers, and an explicit provider target were all deferred.
key_quotes: We are pleased with the progress that we have made through the first half of FY '27. The business momentum has been strong.
Operating profitability remains strong with Q2 adjusted EBITDA at INR 5,353 million, or $56 million, representing a year -on-year growth of 23%, with a margin of 26.3%, the highest in six quarters.
But over a period of time, it could marginally increase if we manage to retain the benefits of AI.
Like I said, it's exactly to accelerate the growth in the provider segment.
So this is not an acquisition where we want to try and improve the margins of Chirok.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guidance raised to 25-26% from 24-25% after Q2 margin of 26.3% (highest in six quarters) and H1 at 25.2%, driven by operating efficiencies, FX tailwind and geo mix, though management calls 24-26% the structural range and minimum wage cost in Q2 was about INR 148 mn vs INR 70 mn in Q1.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Delivery centre count fell to 28 from 31 in March 2026 on campus consolidation, seat count still rising, and staffing is described as matched to capacity for AEP season, so no new capacity is guided; the Chirok acquisition adds 750+ employees but is not a greenfield build.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Deal ACV rose 18.2% YoY to $40.2 mn in Q2 across 31 existing clients, the Big Ten payer win covers over 10 mn members with minimum potential ACV above $10 mn, and H1 revenue grew 13.7% in constant currency, though this is partly offset by OE/AEP softness.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed beyond H1 fixed asset additions of INR 1,168 mn, and no utilisation figure was given to base a new capex call on.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Margin guidance was already raised to 25-26% and management sees possible marginal upside if AI productivity gains are retained, but revenue guidance of low double-digit organic CC growth was only held, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: OE/AEP revenue is guided roughly 100 bps lower as a share of revenue (from about 6%) and marginally below flat YoY, and provider growth is only 10-11%, while Q2 margin benefited from FX that management needs to stay near current levels.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Agentic AI offerings Synchrony Claims Lifecycle and Synchrony RCM Lifecycle are already deployed, and Chirok adds mid-cycle RCM, HEDIS and risk-adjustment offerings, but no specific launch dates were given.

rows.label: Chirok Health acquisition and earn-out
rows.why: Chirok closed with $20 mn upfront plus up to $12.35 mn earn-out on TTM revenue of $13 mn at a 35.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, adding a provider-side RCM capability on top of organic guidance.

rows.label: Debt repayment in FY27
rows.why: Management intends to repay all outstanding debt in full during FY27 after moving from INR 1,962 mn net debt at FY26 end to INR 1,127 mn net cash at Sep 2026.

rows.label: Big Ten health plan payment integrity win
rows.why: Win covers over 10 mn members with minimum potential ACV above $10 mn, but it is contingency-based so revenue ramp is gradual and earn-out timing uncertain.

tone.note: Management was confident on operations, Q2 profitability and the raised margin guide, but cautious on the early AEP/OE season and evasive on Chirok revenue per head, the payer/provider ACV split and any explicit provider target.
